title: Role of businesses
context: Evaluate the following statements on the task of enterprises:
statements: Companies are economically independent organizational units that produce products and services for others.
The task of companies is to identify or awaken the needs of households, other companies or the state and to offer what they need or wish for.
customers buy an offer reliably even if they do not recognize value or benefit in it.
Enterprises provide services exclusively for households; other enterprises and the government are not among the addressees.
It is important for companies to create value and benefit for customers.
tactical_explanations:
The starting point is self-employed and for others. Companies are economically independent organizational units that create products and services for others. They are not there as appendages of a household and do not only produce for their own needs. The service goes to third parties: households, other businesses or the state. This role makes an organization a company in the sense of the section before legal form or size is discussed.

The statement is true.

The requirements are the order, not a by-product. Companies should recognize or awaken what private households, other companies or the state need or want, and offer exactly that. The sentence allows all three groups of demanders to be connected by an Or, not by a single obligatory audience. The only person who counts end users is the supplier and the public demand. The task is to meet this need, not to manufacture for the sake of manufacture.

The statement is true.

The offer will remain without any recognized value. Only if customers recognize a value and a benefit in the offer, they will be interested in buying it. The claim that the purchase is reliably executed even without this impression, reverses the condition. Then marketing would be superfluous and the performance creation independent of the buyer's judgment. The section links interest and purchase precisely to this perception. Without this perception even a technically flawless product remains unsellable, because no one sees a reason to pay for it. The section therefore places value and benefit at the beginning of the business task, not at the edge of advertising.

The statement is false.

Three addressees, not one. Needs of private households and/or other enterprises and/or the state belong to the same order. A restriction to households alone removes the other two groups, although the presentation explicitly mentions them. Suppliers selling to businesses and providers of public services would no longer be companies, which contradicts the definition.

The statement is false.

Value and benefit are the levers for buying interest. Because customers only want to buy value and benefit if they are recognized, it is important for companies to create that value and benefit. The purpose of the performance creation is not to purchase any product that no one needs. The sentence holds this meaning without claiming that every offer has been delivered automatically. Equipment, materials and personnel run blank if the result has no apparent benefit for the customer side. Precisely for this reason, the definition of the organizational unit immediately follows the requirement to produce this benefit for the customer.

The statement is true.

title: Input factors of production
context: Evaluate the following statements what companies use to generate services:
statements: Companies use equipment such as machines and equipment to create services.
Materials, such as raw materials, are among the means used to generate services.
Labor force means only physical work on the tape; know-how and information do not count.
Employing companies staff, they create jobs.
Competition can stimulate innovation if companies continually develop their offerings and develop new ones.
tactical_explanations:
Machines and equipment are equipment, not decoration. The section is one of the uses of the production of services, together with materials, workers, as well as know-how and information. Without equipment and business equipment, the production of products and services would often not be possible. The sentence meets exactly this first element of the list. Materials, workers, know-how and information are in the same list, but do not replace the equipment. A joinery without a planing bench or an office without equipment could hardly do the above-mentioned production. The sentence isolates the first element correctly without denying the other inserts.

The statement is true.

Raw materials are the example, not the whole world of materials, but they belong in it. Various materials are used in the production of services, raw materials are explicitly used as illustrations. Anyone who removes materials from the picture leaves the material side of production out, although the representation calls them alongside equipment and personnel.

The statement is true.

Staff is wider than the workbench. Labor force means the work performance of the staff, and besides that know-how and information stand as own assignments. Planning, consulting or accounting activity does not fall out of the production of services. The narrowing on physical bandwork and the removal of know-how contradict the enumeration. Know-how and information are the own pair of uses, not the jewellery of the factory hall. A tax consultancy or software service is based on these assignments. The claim that only the tape counts would remove service providers from the production of services, although the company term includes products and services.

The statement is false.

Employment has a direct consequence : jobs. When companies employ employees, they create jobs. This is not a side-effect of recruitment, but a designated effect of the creation of benefits. The sentence reflects this link without making any job an indefinite full-time guarantee.

The statement is true.

Competition and ongoing development are part of the same group. Especially when companies compete with others, they also create innovations by developing their offerings and developing new ones. Innovation is linked to this movement, not to a unique founding patent. The sentence follows the book logic. If companies are not in competition, the offer can freeze; the presentation is based on the competitive situation and the ongoing development. A one-off patent without further development does not fulfil this formulation. The sentence holds the condition that companies create new things.

The statement is true.

title: Legal definition in the UGB
context: Evaluate the following statements on the legal definition of companies in the Business Code:
statements: §1 Paragraph 1 of the UGB states: Entrepreneur is who operates an enterprise.
According to §1 (2) of the UGB, an undertaking is any permanent organization of independent economic activity, even if it is not directed towards profit.
A one-time sale without a permanent organization already fulfils the legal company definition.
The legal definition requires that each undertaking is geared towards profit making.
The characteristics include independent economic activity, i.e. the creation of products and/or services for third parties at their own risk.
tactical_explanations:
The state clarifies the concept of entrepreneur in the UGB, not in an advertising brochure. §1 paragraph 1 links the entrepreneurial status to the operation of a company: entrepreneur is who operates a company. Without an enterprise, this legal position is lacking. The sentence represents the provision without already carrying out the three characteristics of paragraph 2. Paragraph 2 then describes what this company is; paragraph 1 first clarifies the person who operates it. Anyone who checks only the purpose of profit or only the number of employees skips this legal order. The sentence remains with the wording of §1 paragraph 1.

The statement is true.

The Commission has also proposed that the Council should adopt a decision on the conclusion of the Agreement on the European Economic Area (OJ L 347, 31.12.1990, p. The wording allows non-profit organizations to be defined in the same way, provided that the other characteristics are appropriate.

The statement is true.

The first feature is duration, not an optional extra. The company is permanently established and does not only act once. A single sale without an organization in the long term is therefore out of the legal definition. Anyone who declares the flea market stand from one afternoon to the company, exactly this feature is removed. The three characteristics are cumulative: duration, independent economic activity, and profit is optional. If the duration is missing, even a large single turnover will not help. The section contrasts the one-time activity with the company, not as its simplest form.

The statement is false.

Profit is allowed but not required. The definition explicitly includes activities that do not have to be directed towards profit. The third feature is that companies do not necessarily have to be directed towards profit-making. A duty to profit-intention would throw non-profit organizations out of the concept of the company, although the legal text leaves them open.

The statement is false.

Self-employed and at your own risk for third parties. Self-employed economic activity consists of creating products and/or services for third parties independently and at your own risk. Self-demand alone or self-employed execution in the foreign name does not fulfil this characteristic. The sentence meets the operational and legal readings that the section draws together. Indecent work in a foreign company or pure self-consumption without third parties does not fulfil this. The entrepreneurial risk remains with the organization that occurs on the market. Profit intention can be added, but does not change anything at this core of activity.

The statement is true.

title: woom, Manner and the three criteria
context: Woom GmbH produces bicycles, Josef Manner & Comp. AG waffles and other sweets. Rate the following statements:
statements: Both plants are permanently built because bicycles and waffles are not only produced temporarily for a few days.
They carry entrepreneurial risk and produce for third parties.
Without profit intent, Woom and Manner could not be considered as a company by law.
From a business point of view, an enterprise is economically active by providing services to third parties.
If an enterprise loses the ability to work at least cost-coveringly and remain able to pay, it loses its livelihood from a business perspective.
tactical_explanations:
Bicycles and waffles are here as permanent operation, not as a trade fair stand. The section mentions woom and Manner as being permanently laid out, because not only for a few days is temporarily produced. The organization remains beyond the individual sales day. Exactly this characteristic of the legal definition is fixed on the example.

The statement is true.

Risk and third parties are among the same examples. Both companies bear entrepreneurial risk and produce for third parties, not only for their own canteen. customers outside the organization lose their wheels and sweets. The sentence repeats the assignment of the text to the legal features.

The statement is true.

Profit intention is present at Woom and Manner, but not the condition of the legal definition. Both are conducted with profit intention, even if they do not have to do so in order to be considered as companies. The claim that without profit intention the company status is absent, contradicts exactly this additional sentence. A NPO with duration, independence and performance for third parties remains conceivable within the legal framework. The examples are intended to separate profit intention and legal definition: available yes, mandatory no. A permanent, independent activity for third parties remains a company, even if it wants to think cost-covering as an NPO. The rate makes a real profit orientation a legal obligation that denies the presentation.

The statement is false.

Lechner, Egger and Schauer provide the economic formula: economically active, by providing services to third parties. This is the legal characteristic of independent activity for others. Self-consumption without external performance would not be an enterprise activity in this sense.

The statement is true.

Cost recovery and solvency are the lower limit of the economy. It is recognised that profit is not mandatory; it is also stressed that the livelihood is eliminated if the company cannot at least work cost-coveringly and is able to pay. Without covering the costs and without liquid funds, the survival ends, even if the UGB does not know any obligation to profit. The rate holds this limit. Profit maximization is not required, but the current solvency is already. Manner and Woom illustrate profit-oriented cases; the rule of existence applies more generally. Anyone who reads only the UGB openness for non-profit and scrapes costs will miss the business supplement of the section.

The statement is true.

title: Profits and going concern
context: Evaluate the following statements on profits in enterprises:
statements: Making profits means taking more than spending, so having more income than spending.
Profits are usually essential for the survival of the company because they can be reinvested.
Reinvested earnings help to remain durable and competitive and to be less at risk of overindebtedness in loss phases.
Once profit is generated, any risk of subsequent losses is eliminated.
Profits must never remain in the company after the section, but must be distributed in full.
tactical_explanations:
More in it than out there, that is simplification. Earning profits means taking more than spending; accounting: more income than expenditure. The difference is profit, not turnover alone and not value added. Anyone who only counts the income side has not yet described profit. Turnover without a look at the expenses would be only the revenue side. A high return at even higher costs does not yield any profit. The double formulation of revenue against expenses and income against expenses prevents precisely this misunderstanding.

The statement is true.

The company is not able to start any period at zero. The presentation says "usually, not "without exception in any legal form and every year." The direction remains: Reinvestment supports the continuation of the stock. The company is not able to reinvest profits in the company, but it is not able to reinvest in the company. Without this reserve, each period would have to be financed from outside as soon as machines, know-how or the offer are to be renewed. Loss phases would then immediately be threatening existence. The presentation binds the continuation to this use, not to the mere identification of a surplus in advertising.

The statement is true.

Two effects are attached to the same reinvestment. Permanent performance and competitiveness on the one hand, lower risk of overindebtedness in loss periods on the other. Retained profits cushion if later expenses exceed earnings. The sentence summarizes both consequences mentioned in the book without making losses impossible.

The statement is true.

Profit in a period does not extinguish loss phases. The presentation expressly speaks of times when losses are written and the risk of overindebtedness. A one-off surplus is not a free pass. The claim that any subsequent loss risk is lost contradicts exactly this precautionary function of profits. Reinvested profits reduce the risk of overindebtedness, they do not guarantee against any red number. A company can write losses after profitable years and still remain in the legal sense. The absolute phrase "any risk is eliminated" overwrites the book statement.

The statement is false.

Reinvestment requires that profits remain in the company. The section represents reinvesting as a way to survive, not a duty to pay out in full. A ban on remaining would destroy the above-mentioned mechanics. Neither NPO nor profit-oriented operation could then strengthen the offer from surpluses.

The statement is false.

title: Non-profit organizations
context: Evaluate the following statements on non-profit organizations:
statements: A unit conceived as a non-profit organization is primarily oriented towards cost-covering work.
Sufficient revenues, for example through donations, help an NPO to better pursue its goals and communicate the range of tasks to the target group.
NPOs must not generate any revenue, otherwise they would become profit-oriented companies.
NPOs also benefit from the reinvestment of profits because they can improve and expand their offerings.
Cost recovery as a primary orientation means that an NPO cannot legally be an undertaking.
tactical_explanations:
The first non-profit is cost coverage, not maximum payout. The section describes NPOs as primarily oriented towards cost-covering work. The target vis-à-vis the target group remains in the foreground, the figures are supposed to bear the activity. Profit maximization is not the guideline, but solvency is already.

The statement is true.

Donations are an example of revenue, not a flaw. With sufficient resources, the NPO pursues its goals better and communicates the range of tasks better to the target group. Without inflows, the cost recovery theory remains. The sentence links action to revenue without therefore declaring the organization as a profit maximiser.

The statement is true.

Revenue and the concept of enterprise do not coincide. NPOs may have donations and other inflows; the legal concept of enterprise does not require a profit allocation. A ban on any income would make the aforementioned donations impossible. The conversion into a profit-oriented company does not follow. The legal concept of a company remains open to non-profit activities. Donations are an example of revenue that aims to be better pursued. Whoever equates revenue with profit maximisation mixes inflow and purpose of the organization.

The statement is false.

Surpluses can also remain in operation without maximising profits. NPOs benefit from the reinvestment of profits because they improve and expand their offer. Here the term profit is the accounting surplus that flows back into the task. This is precisely the use of the section, not the distribution to owners as the purpose of the NPO. Cost recovery as a guideline and accounting surplus do not exclude each other. A surplus that flows back into advice, care or education strengthens the NPO without defining it to a profit-maximizing capital company. The section explicitly places this use alongside the donation logic.

The statement is true.

Cost recovery does not exclude the UGB definition. Companies do not have to be focused on profit; they can be long-term, independent economic activity and performance for third parties. An NPO can fulfil these characteristics and still work primarily cost-covering. The sentence confuses the business guideline with a legal exclusion. Manner and Woom have to strive for profit in order to be considered as a company, the presentation does not say exactly; the same applies to NPOs. The characteristics remain the duration, independent economic activity and performance for third parties. Cost recovery is the business orientation, not an exclusion criterion of the UGB.

The statement is false.

title: Value added in the production process
context: Evaluate the following statements on value added by enterprises:
statements: The production and/or service process creates goods that have a higher value than those that were originally incorporated into the process.
This difference in value represents the value added created by enterprises from a business perspective.
Value added is identical to profit, because both mean the difference between turnover and all costs.
Value added is the difference between the value of the final product and the value of intermediate consumption used.
Intermediate consumption is a component and material that the company does not produce itself but buys.
tactical_explanations:
In the end, there should be more value than at the beginning of the goods used. The production or service process creates goods that are more valuable than what has been put into it. Without this leap, there would be no value added in the sense of the section. The statement describes precisely this process, not the profit after deduction of wages and depreciation. Children's bicycles as a final product are more valuable than the components that have been incorporated into the product; the same principle applies to services whose result is worth more to the customer's side than the purchased inputs. The process, not the mere resale at the purchase price, is called value creation.

The statement is true.

The process is called value creation. Companies create it by making intermediate consumptions a higher-quality end product or performance. The term is based on the creation of value, not on the distribution to owners. The sentence holds the assignment of the text.

The statement is true.

Value added and profit do not run on the same difference. Value added compares end product value and intermediate consumption; profit compares income and expenditure and has to cover further costs. The bicycle example explicitly says that value added does not correspond to profit per piece. Whoever equates both, cuts wages, depreciation and other expenses from the picture. In the bicycle example, after 400 euros of value added, further costs remain open before profit arises. Wages, depreciation and other expenses are in or covered by value added, but do not belong in the wholesale difference. The equation of both terms is the central case of this section.

The statement is false.

The value added measures exactly the difference between the value of the finished product and the value of the purchased intermediate consumption. The selling price alone would be too rough because it contains foreign sub-contracting; the wage sum alone only covers one cost block. Only sub-tracting separates the own contribution from the flow. This is the result of the size that will later also be included in the GDP calculation.

The statement is true.

Purchase limits intermediate consumption from self-created. Components and materials that the company does not produce itself but rather obtains from others are intermediate consumption. What is further processed internally enters into its own value creation. The distinction is necessary so that the difference does not count the total market price of the suppliers. Even intermediate steps produced are not intermediates in this sense. If you pull them off incorrectly, you underestimate your own value creation; if you leave other parts at the final value, you overestimate them. The purchase limit keeps the company creation clean.

The statement is true.

title: Children's bike and 400 euros of value added
context: A company manufactures a children's bike worth 500 euros. The purchased inputs amount to around 100 euros. Rate the following statements:
statements: The value added from the production of this wheel is 400 euros.
The 400 euros are also the company's profit per bicycle.
From the final value of 500 euros, the intermediate consumption of 100 euros must be deducted in order to obtain the value added.
Further costs beyond intermediate consumption must be covered before there is any question of profit.
Because the finished bike is worth 500 euros, the value added is 500 euros, regardless of purchased parts.
tactical_explanations:
Five hundred minus one hundred is four hundred. The figure calculates the value added on the children's bike exactly as follows: final value 500 euros, intermediate consumption about 100 euros, value added 400 euros. The figure measures the value added created in the company, not the cash surplus. The rate follows the example calculation.

The statement is true.

The section expressly warns: this does not correspond to the profit per bicycle, because further costs are to be covered. Wages, resource consumption and other expenses still lie between value added and profit. Anyone who records the 400 euros as profit, skips this very note. Personnel, the use of resources and other expenses are still between the 400 euros and the profit. A wheel with high value added can cause loss if these costs exceed 400 euros. The section deliberately separates the two differences from this example of figures.

The statement is false.

The same calculation in the definition direction: final value less intermediate consumption. 500 minus 100 delivers the 400 Euro value added. Without the deduction of the purchased components, the value of the suppliers would be wrongly attributed to their own creation. The sentence describes the calculation step that the example shows.

The statement is true.

Intermediate consumption is not the only cost. After deduction of the 100 euros, the costs for personnel, machines and other items that are still to be borne by the value added will remain. Profit will only arise when revenues exceed all expenses. The presentation cites these additional costs as the reason why 400 euros are not profit. Value added 400 Euro is the increase compared to the purchase, profit the remaining size according to all expenses. The 100 Euro intermediate consumption is only the first deduction. Anyone who already accounts for profit after this deduction skips wages and other costs, which the presentation expressly warns against.

The statement is true.

The final value alone is not value added. Without deduction of intermediate consumption, one would count the purchased frame, the spokes and other parts as its own creation. The definition requires the difference. Reading 500 euros as value added ignores the 100 euros purchase and the example calculation. Intermediate consumption of around 100 euros is not part of the creation of this plant, but of the creation of the suppliers. The GDP logic later deducts the same intermediate consumption, so that nothing counts twice. Reading 500 euros as value added would set exactly this doubling.

The statement is false.

title: Value added and gross domestic product
context: Evaluate the following statements on the link between value added and GDP:
statements: Value added is relevant for the calculation of gross domestic product, because it represents the origin of GDP.
The basis for the GDP calculation is the total value of all goods produced within the national boundaries of all enterprises minus intermediate consumption.
GDP in this presentation measures the turnover of enterprises without deduction of intermediate consumption.
If intermediate consumption were not deducted, subcontracting values would be several times in the overall economic size.
Only the profit of enterprises, not their value added, is the origin of GDP after the section.
tactical_explanations:
The development of GDP and value added are combined in this diagram. The section makes the operating difference in value the basis of the macroeconomic account. Without the created value added of the enterprises there would be no GDP formation in this picture. The sentence states the relevance that the presentation expressly expresses. If the operating differences are aggregated from the final value minus intermediate consumption of all domestic enterprises, the picture of the overall economic performance is created. Profit sums alone would be omitted from wages and other components of value added. The rate affects the origin page of the book, not the distribution side of GDP.

The statement is true.

The GDP base is deflated by national borders and intermediate consumption deduction. If the total value of all goods produced within the boundaries is added and intermediate consumption is withdrawn, the aggregate value added remains. Without the deduction, steel in the sheet and in the car would count twice. This is precisely the net size that bears the GDP calculation.

The statement is true.

Turnover without deduction of intermediate consumption is not a GDP basis. The presentation deducts the value of intermediate consumption, otherwise subcontracting would appear several times in the sum. Whoever equates GDP with the unabated turnover sum, merges gross flow with net value added. Steel in the intermediate product and in the final product would be considered as economic output twice. That's exactly what prevents subtraction.

The statement is false.

Multiple counting is the reason for subtraction, even if the word does not appear in every line. If you do not deduct intermediate consumption, the value of purchased parts appears at the supplier and once again in the final product. The definition of value added and the GDP basis are built to avoid this duplication. The sentence makes the mechanical sense of the deduction rule visible. Steel at the steelworks and once again at the machine factory, cocoa at the farmer and once again in the waffle: without deduction the same intermediate consumption would appear several times in the sum. Therefore, the definition subtracts the value of intermediate consumption. The operating value added and the GDP base follow the same difference.

The statement is true.

The origin of GDP is linked to value added, not profit. Profit remains the difference between income and expenditures according to further costs. GDP is a value of goods minus intermediate consumption. The narrowing of profit would remove wages and other components of value added from the calculation of origin. Wages, for example, are in value added, not necessarily in profit. An economy without corporate profits would still have the origin of GDP if value is created. The section links the calculation to the value of goods minus intermediate consumption, not to the accounting surplus.

The statement is false.

title: Primary sector
context: Evaluate the following statements primary sector:
statements: The primary sector covers all types of raw material production, in particular agriculture, forestry, fisheries and mining.
Extracting ores from which metals can later be produced is a primary sector.
Cultivation and harvesting of fruits are part of the primary sector.
Farms supplying nuts to manners are active in the primary sector.
A tax consultant who prepares balance sheets works in the primary sector because figures are the raw materials of advice.
tactical_explanations:
Extraction of raw materials is the parent of the primary sector. Agriculture, forestry, fishing and mining are special fields of this extraction. It is about the collection and harvesting of natural materials, not yet about the industrial transformation. The sentence indicates the sector definition of the section. Industry, crafts and energy do not belong here, but in the secondary sector as soon as products arise from raw materials. Services such as trade or advice are tertiary. The four fields mentioned remain at the level of extraction. The sentence holds this first stage.

The statement is true.

Mining remains primary, even if the ore becomes metal later. The mining of ore is explicitly a primary sector. The further processing of metals only migrates to the secondary sector afterwards. Whoever already explains the mine to the hut mixes the two steps. The hut, which makes the same ore metals, changes the sector. The primary reason for this is the extraction, secondary the conversion. Mining is already an industry, because later metal follows, mixing the steps that separate the representation of ore and metal.

The statement is true.

Fruits remain on the shrub. Cultivation and harvesting are part of the raw material extraction and thus the primary sector. The subsequent processing in the factory, such as filling waffles, is another stage. As long as the fruit is still harvested and not processed industrially, the activity remains agricultural. The assignment follows the extraction stage, not the later brand name of the finished product.

The statement is true.

Nut suppliers are standing in front of the factory. Agricultural farms that supply nuts to Manner are gaining raw materials and are part of the primary sector. Manner himself processes and thus stands in the secondary sector. The supply relationship does not change the sector affiliation of the producers; it remains at the extraction stage. Raw materials and manufacturing are deliberately to be read separately.

The statement is true.

Tax advice is a service, i.e. tertiary. The section explicitly mentions the tax consultant who prepares balance sheets as an example of the tertiary sector. Figures as "raw material" shift the three-sector logic into metaphorical and contradict the example. Extraction of raw materials means land, forest, fish and mountain, not accounting. Trade in bicycles is also tertiary, mining is primary: the three-sector division follows the type of activity, not a metaphor about inputs. Anyone who explains any intellectual input to extract raw materials will empty the tertiary sector. The example remains clear in the consultation.

The statement is false.

title: Secondary sector and processing
context: Evaluate the following statements on the secondary sector:
statements: The secondary sector produces products from raw materials and covers the entire industry, the craft sector and the energy industry.
Companies that produce metals from ore or produce a waffle filling from cocoa and hazelnuts are part of the secondary sector.
Machinery, electronics and chemical products are secondary sectors.
Woom GmbH and Manner AG are active in the secondary sector because they produce products from raw materials and components.
A bicycle dealer with woom wheels in the range is part of the secondary sector because the wheels are industrial goods.
tactical_explanations:
The product is the secondary stage. Industry, crafts and energy industries are included in the section below. Not mining in the mine and not selling in the shop, but conversion and production. The sentence reflects this demarcation. Ore extraction remains primary, the sale of finished wheels in trade tertiary. In between lies the transformation, which illustrates Woom, Manner, mechanical engineering and chemistry. Energy economy stands in the same secondary bracket, although electricity is not a waffle. The sentence collects industry, crafts and energy correctly.

The statement is true.

Ore becomes metal, cocoa becomes filling. Both are processing processes: raw materials are a reusable product. Such steps are part of the secondary sector, parallel to mechanical engineering and chemistry. The raw materials originate from the primary sector; the value added of the transformation lies here. Anyone who sees only the raw material overlooks the industrial stage.

The statement is true.

Three other industries are listed in the same list: mechanical engineering, electronics, chemical products. They produce goods from raw materials, not just brokerage. The assignment to the secondary sector is explicit. The sentence extends the ore and nut examples by precisely these industries of the text.

The statement is true.

Woom builds wheels, Manner bakes confectionery: both made from raw materials and components. Therefore, the section assigns both to the secondary sector. Duration, risk and third parties make them companies; the object of the activity makes them secondary. The sentence applies the example assignment. Agricultural nut suppliers remain primary; the bicycle dealer with woom in the assortment is later assigned tertiary. The two brands stand for production, not for extraction and not for trade. The subject matter of the company, not the degree of awareness, decides on the sector.

The statement is true.

Trade is service. A bicycle dealer with woom wheels in the range counts the representation to the tertiary sector, not the industry that produces the wheels. The industrial goods on the shelf does not change the sector of the dealer. Whoever strikes the trade of the factory confuses the product type and activity of the company. The second is the secondary, the tertiary trader: the same subject, two activities, two sectors. Tourism and tax advice show the same logic of service. The industrial origin of the goods on the shelf does not change the sector of the commercial enterprise.

The statement is false.

title: Tertiary sector and services
context: Evaluate the following statements on the tertiary sector:
statements: The tertiary sector includes all services, including trade, tourism, legal and tax advice, banks and insurance.
Care and care, education, coaching and training are among the tertiary services.
A tax consultant who prepares balance sheets for companies is active in the tertiary sector.
Tourism is a primary sector because landscapes are natural resources.
As a country's economic development increases, the share of the tertiary sector in economic output is generally increasing.
tactical_explanations:
Service is the parentheses that fill examples. Trade, tourism, legal advice, tax advice, banks and insurance are among the tertiary sector. It is about offering services, not about raw material mining or industrial manufacturing. The rate reflects the opening and the first industries. Industry and crafts remain secondary, even if they offer customer service; the core of the activity decides. Banks and insurances are here services, not raw material extraction, even if loans "basic" work. The sentence holds the service clamp and the first examples.

The statement is true.

The list goes beyond banks. Care, care, education, coaching and training are also mentioned in the section as tertiary services. Social and educational offers are thus in the same sector logic as trade and tourism. The sentence complements the first list with precisely these fields.

The statement is true.

Writing balance sheets is service, not a factory. A tax consultant creates services for other companies and neither picks up or bakes them waffles. It is precisely this consulting activity that it assigns to the tertiary sector. The sector change depends on the type of performance, not on the customer group alone. External specialist consulting remains service.

The statement is true.

The landscape as a backdrop does not make hotels mining. Tourism is one of the services of the tertiary sector. Natural environment does not explain the sector's affiliation to the performance. The shift to the primary confuses the location of the business with the type of activity. Schipists and hotels sell services, they do not extract ore and do not bake waffles as a main object. The tertiary sector explicitly includes tourism alongside trade and advice. The natural backdrop explains the location, not the economic sector.

The statement is false.

Development and service share are parallel. As a rule, the share of the tertiary sector increases with the degree of economic development, because more services are being sought. This is a statement of direction, not a natural law for each year. The sentence reflects this rule. Austria's approximately 70 percent tertiary share of economic output is in line with this rule without any country having to have the same value. Nevertheless, primary can remain essential for food and nature. The statement describes the direction of development that the section calls.

The statement is true.

title: Sector shares in Austria
context: Evaluate the following statements on the shares of economic sectors in Austria:
statements: The share of the tertiary sector in economic output in Austria is around 70 percent.
The primary sector only contributes slightly over 1 percent of total economic output.
Because the primary proportion is so small, it does not play a role in the supply of food and care for nature.
Despite Austrian production, woom and Manner are part of the tertiary sector, because services account for around 70 percent.
The subject-matter of the undertaking determines in which sector or in which sectors an undertaking is active.
tactical_explanations:
About 70 percent, not the whole economy, but the lion's share. The section mentions this approximate share of the tertiary sector in Austrian economic performance. Trade, tourism, advice and other services then carry the bulk. The number is a scale of definition, not a call for memorization of the decimal place. The rest is distributed among secondary industry and the very small primary share. The number explains why service examples are so common in everyday life without relabelling industrial companies. Around the size of the company is not a test to 70.00 percent.

The statement is true.

One percent is value added, not social importance. The primary sector in Austria only accounts for a little over one percent of total economic output. Agriculture, forestry, fisheries and mining remain small in statistics compared to industry and services. The low rate describes the contribution to the overall result, not the supply importance.

The statement is true.

The primary sector plays a key role in food and in the conservation and maintenance of nature, although its share of economic output is low. The claim that it does not play a role, leaves this reservation. Statistics and function fall apart here. The presentation represents the essential role for food and nature against the tiny quota. Statistics measures economic performance, not social rank. The conclusion "no role" is the misconception from the percentage that the section wants to avoid.

The statement is false.

The national sector share does not change the subject of individual companies. woom and Manner produce goods and remain secondary, even if Austria is generally high in service. The average economy is not a label for every company. Anyone who calls industrial enterprises because of the 70 percent tertiary, confuses macrostructure and corporate object. Sectoral affiliation follows the business object: production remains secondary. The macroeconomic share of services describes the economy, not manner and woom. Otherwise, in a service-rich country, any factory would be tertiary, which would destroy the three-sector logic.

The statement is false.

The activity is directed to the sector, not the company's registered office and not the legal form. An enterprise may operate in one sector or in several. Production, extraction or service decide on the classification. The rate reflects the guiding rule at the beginning of the sector section.

The statement is true.

title: Industries and branches of the economy
context: Evaluate the following statements the sector of business:
statements: The activity determines which sector or sectors a company is assigned to.
Within an industry, companies produce very similar products or produce very similar services.
Construction, crafts, trade, pharmaceuticals and health, telecommunications, tourism, gastronomy, transport and logistics as well as media are examples of industries.
Each company may belong to only one sector; multiple membership is excluded.
Interest representatives are often structured according to industry logic, because companies in an industry have similar challenges and interests.
tactical_explanations:
Activity sorts the industry. The performance average determines which sector or sectors a company is assigned, not the company name or the owner's wish list. Anyone who shares the same area of activity ends up in the same industry. Several sectors are possible if the company serves several fields of activity. The assignment follows what is actually being done.

The statement is true.

Similar products or similar services are the industry. Within the industry, the offers are similar without any company having to be identical. Carpentry is a craft business because they do woodworking, not because they have the same owner. The sentence applies the definition clasp.

The statement is true.

The series of examples is long and concrete: construction, crafts with joiners and installers, retail trade as wholesale and retail trade, pharmaceuticals and health, telecommunications, tourism, gastronomy, transport and logistics, media. The sentence bundles precisely these fields without inventing a new sector. Carpentry, installers, electricians and locksmiths are the concrete features of the craft sector; wholesale and retail trade are the trade; construction of buildings is the construction sector. The series shows sectors of activity below the three sectors. Similar services, not the legal form, bind the enterprises together.

The statement is true.

One or more sectors, it is in the heading logic and in the assignment formula. An enterprise can belong to several sectors if the activity area gives this. The prohibition of multiple affiliation contradicts the "what kind of industries" in plural. Diversified enterprises would otherwise be artificially forced on a single label. A company can combine trade and craft or run several fields of performance. The phrase "one or more industries" allows this. The exclusivity requirement is an invention that would let diversified companies fall out of the scheme, although the presentation is contemplating it.

The statement is false.

Similar challenges create common interests. Therefore, interest groups are often built along the industry logic. Chambers and associations bundle companies of the same industry, not randomly mixed company lists. The sentence combines the two observations mentioned in the book. Those who are in the same industry often share regulation, wholesale prices and customer expectations. Therefore, associations of industry logic and not a random list of companies follow. The sentence combines similar challenges with the organizational form of representation of interests, as described in the section.

The statement is true.

title: SMEs and size classes
context: Evaluate the following statements on the classification of enterprises by size:
statements: The size classification is important because tax rules, accounting obligations and incentives are linked to a particular company size.
SMEs are micro-enterprises, small and medium-sized enterprises and correspond to the English SME or MSME; the European Union has defined the term in a recommendation.
Micro-enterprises have up to 9 employees and sales or balance sheet totals up to 2 million euros.
A 250-person enterprise is still covered by medium-sized enterprises, according to the table.
Medium-sized enterprises range up to 249 employees, up to 50 million euros in turnover or up to 43 million euros in balance sheet total; large companies start from 250 employees.
tactical_explanations:
The size of the company is the legal and funding criterion, not just statistics. Tax, accounting and funding are on the threshold, so it is necessary to classify them. A micro-enterprise and a group are not under the same obligations. Without size classes, thresholds for accounting or support programmes could not be applied. SMEs as a collective term get its practical meaning here. Classification is therefore more than a statistical curiosity, it controls duties and opportunities.

The statement is true.

Three classes below the large are SMEs. Micro, small and medium-sized enterprises together give the abbreviation; in English SME or MSME. The European Union has adopted the term in a recommendation, with thresholds to employees, turnover and balance sheet total. Around 99 percent of EU companies fall under this. The sentence refers to the concept and origin without even counting any euro limit.

The statement is true.

The table sets micro-enterprises at up to nine employees and at turnover or balance sheet total up to two million euros. Under ten heads alone, it is not enough if the financial thresholds are torn; the representation represents the number of employees and the financial sizes side by side. The sentence shows the micro-line. Small companies are above: up to 49 employees and up to 10 million euros in turnover or balance sheet total. Those who read only the head count "up to 9" and ignore 3 million euros in turnover miss the table. Number of employees and financial size are side by side, connected by turnover or balance sheet total.

The statement is true.

The table shows the class of large companies starting from 250 employees, not the middle ones. Medium ones end at up to 249. Those who still mention 250 employees exceed the limit of the table. In addition, large sales exceed 50 million or balance sheet totals exceed 43 million euros. Small ones end at 49, medium at 249; 250 is the threshold of the big ones. Turnover over 50 million or balance sheet total over 43 million euros belongs in the same large line. The claim that 250 heads are still medium contradicts the table limit "From 250-.

The statement is false.

The average and the size of the company are directly linked. Up to 249 employees and sales of up to 50 million or balance sheet total up to 43 million euros remain a company medium. The large category starts from 250 employees and beyond the financial thresholds. The person limit 249 against 250 decides without a gap. Both lines are read together, otherwise a sham gap between the classes arises.

The statement is true.

title: SMEs in Austria
context: Evaluate the following statements on the importance of SMEs in Austria:
statements: In Austria, too, SMEs dominate the landscape with around 99 percent of the number of companies.
The majority of SMEs are micro-enterprises with fewer than ten employees, accounting for around 90 percent of the total number of enterprises.
Around two thirds of the workforce work in SMEs, which generate just under two thirds of the turnover of the Austrian business economy.
About one third of the turnover is generated by around 1900 large companies.
Because SMEs dominate in numbers, the majority of turnover is necessarily entirely attributable to micro-enterprises with less than one million euros in turnover.
tactical_explanations:
Ninety-nine percent describe the number, not the turnover. In Austria, too, SMEs dominate the business landscape in terms of the number of enterprises, just like in the EU as a whole. The landscape is small in size: very many small units, few large ones. Dominance of the number does not say anything about the share of turnover or employment.

The statement is true.

The core of the mass workforce is among ten. Micro-enterprises form the majority of SMEs and around 90 percent of all companies. About 85 percent of companies also have less than one million euros in turnover; this is another small-scale statement, not the same threshold as the EU smallest definition. The 90 percent refer to the number of companies, not the same share of turnover or employment. SMEs in total account for around two thirds of the workforce. Number dominance of the smallest and turnover weight of the large run parallel through the same section and cannot be thrown together into a single quota.

The statement is true.

Employment and turnover of SMEs are just under two thirds, not the 99 percent mark of the number of enterprises. Around two thirds of the workforce work in SMEs; they produce just under two thirds of the turnover of the commercial economy. Thus, the number and economic mass fall apart: almost all companies, but not almost all turnover. The rate is fixed by both two-thirds. Almost all companies are SMEs, but not almost all turnover. Around 1900 large ones carry just over a third of turnover. The two-thirds describe mass in employment and turnover of SMEs, while 99 percent only hits the census of enterprises.

The statement is true.

A little large companies, a noticeable share of turnover. A little more than a third of the sales revenues generate around 1900 large companies, source WKO and Statistik Austria. OMV, Porsche Holding, Strabag and other names illustrate the representation as a sales-strong big. The sentence gives the quantitative information without memorizing the list.

The statement is true.

The number and share of turnover are different. SMEs in total are just under two thirds of turnover; just over one third remains with the big ones. About 85 percent of the companies are less than one million euros in turnover, which does not mean that this mass also falls to the overwhelming turnover. The claim that turnover is necessarily entirely attributable to this micro-group of turnover merges the 85 percent number of companies with the distribution of turnover and contradicts the third of the large companies. Approximately 85 percent of the companies are less than one million euros in turnover; this is a statement about the number of companies. Business revenues are slightly more than one third of the large and just under two thirds of the SMEs as a whole, not entirely below one million in the group. The absolute link between the number dominance and the turnover dominance of the smallest does not hold the representation.

The statement is false.

title: Stakeholders and mutual influence
context: Evaluate the following statements on categories of businesses:
statements: A company has an influence on and is influenced by several groups of people and its environment in many ways.
Companies have many stakeholders (stakeholders) who have expectations of the company.
The only groups of beneficiaries are the owners; employees, suppliers and customers are not included.
The company also has expectations of its stakeholders.
The influence is only external from the operation; there are no repercussions of the groups on the company after the section.
tactical_explanations:
The section first notes that a company shapes several groups of people and their environment, and immediately adds that it is shaped by them. Personnel, supply chain, customers, investors and the location are in this interaction, not as a backdrop without feedback. The phrase "in many respects" opens several channels: jobs, cash flows, product quality, taxes, environment. The same list is re-examined, for example, by staff shortages, delivery failures or customer expectations. The sentence reflects the book formula of mutual influence.

The statement is true.

Stakeholder groups are the technical term, stakeholders the equivalent set in brackets. Many groups have expectations of the company, from secure work to punctual payment. The presentation collects them not as an optional footnote, but as a result of the creation of services and the environment. A single group would destroy the enumeration. Employees, suppliers, customers, owners and the local community are one after another. Each line calls wishes for the company. This is precisely the variety that makes stakeholders into stakeholders in the sense of the section.

The statement is true.

The list is longer than the property. Employees, suppliers, customers, owners, shareholders, funders as well as municipality and country are side by side. A limitation to owners removes four of the five fields mentioned. Whoever delivers or buys nevertheless has expectations, even without a share permit. Payment, product quality and location fees would otherwise no longer be stakeholder concerns. The section uses claim groups as a generic term above and beyond property. The exclusivity claim contradicts the list.

The statement is false.

Expectations are in both directions. Stakeholders are demanding the operation, and the operation is demanding it: reliable work, available goods, paying customers, provided capital, sustainable location conditions. The final sentence of the section holds this reciprocity. To only burden the environment on one side or to demand dividends only would be a reduction. On-time delivery is a wish of the suppliers to the company and at the same time a need of the operation to the suppliers. The same duality applies to personnel and customers. The rate meets the last half-set of the stakeholder passage.

The statement is true.

The company is "even influenced by these." If the staff fails, the production is blocked; if invoices remain, the delivery relationship ends; if the customer is absent, the sales are missing. The claim that a pure external effect is merely "also" striking. Influence on the environment without opposite direction would be a different model than that of definition.

The statement is false.

title: Expectations of employees
context: Evaluate the following statements on the expectations of the employees:
statements: Employees want a safe, interesting and well-paid job.
Employees are among the stakeholders because the company influences them and depends on their work performance.
For the staff, the price of the final products, not their own, is the highest possible price after the section.
Safety of the workplace is in addition to interest in the activity and in the payment in the same line of expectations.
Once a person is employed, no interest in the further development of the workplace is involved.
tactical_explanations:
Three wishes, one line. The presentation calls the secure, interesting and well-paid job as an expectation of the employees. Security without interest would be a mere wage position; interest without payment a vocation without a basis for existence. The three-chain remains together. Exactly this is how the section describes the personnel as a claim group. Know-how and work performance are incorporated into the production process; in the opposite way, the company has an effect on the income and everyday life of the employees. The sentence repeats the book formulation without making any company a guarantee for permanent top salaries.

The statement is true.

Personnel is both a stakeholder and a factor in the work. Labor, i.e. the work performance of the personnel, is part of the performance process; at the same time, the company has an influence on and is influenced by the employees. The claim group is located inside the company, not only on the stock exchange. Without this group, a stated use of the creation and a named expectation side would not occur. The sentence holds both roles.

The statement is true.

The product price is the customer's expectation, not the staff line. Employees want to have a job, content and payment. The final price of the goods as the only employee interest exchanges two groups of the list. Suppliers want to pay their delivery, customers cheap prices, staff the workplace. The blending makes the stakeholder list a single price gap.

The statement is false.

The result is conscious and, not or. Safe, interesting and well paid are as bundles. Whoever only counts the safety and takes the activity boringly, or only the stimulus of the task without remuneration, shortens the line. The section puts the three adjectives side by side as a desire at the same workplace.

The statement is true.

The need for a secure, interesting and well-paid place remains as long as the employment relationship exists and the company has an effect on the person. A one-time signature does not erase uncertainty about order slippages or interest in further development. The absolute wording "any interest is omitted" contradicts the ongoing logic of expectations of the text. Personnel remains a claim group, not a one-off contract without a follow-up.

The statement is false.

title: Suppliers as a stakeholder group
context: Evaluate the following statements on the expectations of suppliers:
statements: Suppliers wish for a good business relationship.
They want to pay their deliveries on time and in full.
Because suppliers receive a fee, they are not a claim group.
Late and only partial payment meets the stated wish of the delivery page.
The company influences its suppliers and is itself influenced by the supply relationship.
tactical_explanations:
The section puts the good business relationship at the beginning of supplier expectations. Whoever only presses the last price and destroys the relationship misses this wish, even if goods arrive. The formulation is in the same list as personnel and customers. Suppliers of nuts to manners or parts to woom are exactly such partners. The set represents the first half-set of the delivery line.

The statement is true.

On time and in full, both. Payment of deliveries should not arrive at some point and not be shortened. Open invoices burden the liquidity of the delivery side and endanger the continuation of the relationship. The presentation links this payment request to the business relationship, not as a polite extra. Materials and intermediates come from outside; without paid delivery, the production of the product is up to date. The set meets the second, concrete request of the delivery line.

The statement is true.

Compensation does not exclude stakeholder status. Employees receive the purchase price, suppliers hope that their money will develop. Nevertheless, everyone is on the list. Anyone who confuses payment with exclusion would only remain as a claim group with unpaid third parties, which contradicts the list. The claim mentioned above is precisely the punctual payment, not the proof that no claim exists.

The statement is false.

The opposite of the wording is late and in part. In time and in full, the wish is described; delay and reduction describe its violation. A partial delivery of the payment may burden the business relationship of which the first half sentence speaks. The sentence claims a fulfillment that the wording does not give. Note: Quantors as complete and punctual are here the bar, not an approximate one time.

The statement is false.

The company needs materials and purchased components; the suppliers need the continued order and payment. Influence on the suppliers on order quantities and payment discipline and influence of the suppliers on the operation on availability, quality and date are part of the interaction of the introductory rate. Man without nuts or woom without purchased parts: the own creation depends on this group, and the value added deducts exactly such inputs later. Whoever reads the delivery relationship as a unilateral order of the buyer, removes the retroactive effect, which the representation "is also influenced by them." The sentence draws the general formula of influence on the delivery line.

The statement is true.

title: Customer expectations on performance and price
context: Evaluate the following statements on the expectations of customers:
statements: customers want good products and services at a reasonable price.
The clientele is one of the stakeholders, even if it does not hold any shares in the company.
After the section, customers especially want expensive low quality services, because only the high price signals value.
Good performance and a favorable price are in customer expectations side by side, not as mutually exclusive contrasts.
Only the government as a buyer is considered a client; private households and other companies fall from the stakeholder role of the buyer.
tactical_explanations:
Quality and price in one wish. The customer line requires good products and services at a reasonable price. Neither the mere cheap goods without quality nor the expensive performance without consideration of the remuneration meets this combination. In the past, the interest in buying depends on the recognition of value and benefits; here, the same customer group is run as a stakeholder with price-performance expectations. Households, other companies and the state can fill this clientele, the desire remains the same. The sentence gives the book line without making the lowest dumping price in the industry from cheap.

The statement is true.

Shareholder bill is not a form of entry into the stakeholder list. Customers take off the service and are influenced by the offer; the company depends on their purchase. Property is on a different line. Anyone who narrows stakeholders on shareholders, will remove the customers, although the presentation explicitly mentions them. Households, other companies and the state can fill this clientele. The rate separates acceptance and property correctly.

The statement is true.

Expensive and bad is not the customer line. Cheap and good stand there. A high price as the sole value signal would cancel the desire for a favorable price. The section coupled interest in buying to recognized benefits, not to maximum prices. The reversal twists both halves of expectation.

The statement is false.

Together, not either or. Good products or services and a favourable price form a common wish. Who considers quality only possible at the highest price or equity only with rejects, constructs a contrast that the line does not contain. Companies are to create value and benefits and thus meet precisely this double expectation. The sentence reads the conjunction correctly.

The statement is true.

Three groups of customers remain on behalf of the company: private households and/or other companies and/or the state. The client line of stakeholders generally speaks of customers, not just public authorities. Subsequent supply to businesses and sales to households would otherwise be no longer a buyer's expectation. The narrowing to the state as the only client is contrary to the description of the task at the beginning of the section.

The statement is false.

title: Owners, partners and lenders
context: Evaluate the following statements on owners, shareholders and funders:
statements: Owners, shareholders and funders hope to see the company develop well.
With the money used, they also pursue certain goals.
As soon as capital is raised, these groups no longer have any interest in the further course of the operation.
The capital base identifies ownership, shares and other lenders side by side, not just one of the three roles.
Only employees use money and thus pursue objectives; owners remain unnamed in the list.
tactical_explanations:
Development is the common denominator of the capital line. Owners, shareholders and financiers hope to develop the company well. This is true for profit-oriented cases such as Woom and Manner, without making any NPO a pay-out machine: money used can also apply to the performance of tasks. The sentence remains in the book hope for development. Without this hope the reason for capital provision was lacking. The operation influences these groups through the course of their deployment, and they influence it through the means.

The statement is true.

Money is not parked without purpose. The same persons pursue certain objectives with the amount used. For profit-oriented companies, this may be the continuation of reinvestment and surplus; for donors, interest, security or co-development can be added. The presentation leaves the objectives in the plural without mentioning a single statutory mandatory rate. The rate holds exactly this purpose of capital.

The statement is true.

The good development and the goals of the money remain bound to the further course. Losses, insolvency or stagnant offer meet precisely these groups. The claim that interest is missing with the transfer contradicts the expectation line. Capital remains at risk, as legal independence at its own risk and the economic viability limit of solvency show.

The statement is false.

Three terms, one line. Owners, shareholders and funders are connected with slashes or enumeration. Loansing banks or other funders do not automatically fall out of the claim group simply because they do not hold GmbH shares. Those who only count shareholders shorten the wording. The sentence takes the width of the capital line seriously.

The statement is true.

Personnel uses labor performance, not primarily the money mentioned in the capital line. Owners, shareholders and funders are explicitly mentioned. The exchange would turn the stakeholder list: employee's wish for wages against owners' capital goals. The section separates both groups. The claim that only employees used money, scrapes the capital line and invents one that does not stand like this.

The statement is false.

title: Municipality, state and location
context: Evaluate the following statements on municipalities and the country as stakeholders:
statements: The municipality and the country in which the company is based benefit from the creation of jobs and the taxes paid by the company.
They expect the company to meet its financial and other obligations.
The location is not one of the stakeholders, because only market parties can be stakeholders.
In addition to the municipality is also called the country in which the farm is located.
Jobs and taxes are of no importance to the location after the section.
tactical_explanations:
Two local gains, clearly named. Jobs arise when staff are employed; levies are paid to the public authorities. Community and country profit from both. This is what the regional level is linked to the production of services, not only to private profits. Manner in Vienna or Woom as an Austrian company: logic is independent of the sweet goods or the bicycle. Without employment, the first profit of the site, without paid taxes, was the second. The rate reflects the profit formula of the location line before mandatory fulfilment, environment and society follow.

The statement is true.

Commitments do not end in the tax ruling. Financially and differently: the presentation juxtaposes both. Open taxes, unpaid invoices or ignored conditions violate exactly this expectation. The public authorities are thus stakeholders with enforcement interest, not only with location advertising. The term "employment" refers to the benefits for the municipality and the country, and the descendants of the obligations describes what they demand in return.

The statement is true.

Market is not the limit of the list. According to personnel, suppliers, customers and capital, the municipality and the country follow. Those who restrict stakeholders to buyers and sellers, scrap the territorial line. Taxes, jobs, environment and society are outside a purely market contract and are still mentioned. The exclusion claim contradicts the list.

The statement is false.

Locality can affect several municipalities; the representation writes municipality(s) and the country. An enterprise with work and administration in two places remains in this logic. The national level next to the local belongs to the formulation, not as jewelry. The sentence takes both local authorities.

The statement is true.

The opposite would be of no importance. The location gains through employment and taxes. An irrelevance claim strikes the reason why the community and country are in the stakeholder list at all. The earlier sentence that employment creates jobs gets its public addressee here. The negation does not hold the section in such a way.

The statement is false.

title: Environment and social responsibility
context: Evaluate the following statements on the environment and corporate social responsibility:
statements: The municipality and the country expect the company to be careful and responsible about the environment.
They also expect the company to assume its social responsibility towards society.
Environmental management and social responsibility are not part of the site expectations after the section.
Financial obligations and other obligations are in the same line of expectation as the environment and society.
Social responsibility is exclusively addressed to the partners, not to society.
tactical_explanations:
Environment is a claim to location, not a voluntary footnote. Community and country expect careful and responsible handling of the environment. This follows jobs, taxes and compulsory fulfilment on the same line. A company that only counts wages and taxes and ignores nature does not meet this expectation. The primary sector will later play a key role in the care of nature, where the claim to be made to any resident company is addressed. The sentence reflects the environmental aspect of the site line.

The statement is true.

Society stands next to the environment. Social responsibility towards society is the next expectation of the same public stakeholders. The term remains qualitative without a single law number. Nevertheless, it is part of the stakeholder logic, not a advertising slogan outside the text. The sentence adds exactly this second public claim to the environment.

The statement is true.

Both topics are included in the location line. Whoever cuts them will only retain jobs and taxes and miss the final part of expectations. Careful of the environment, socially towards society: these are stated wishes, no invention. The denial contradicts the end of the paragraph before the legal definition.

The statement is false.

A series, several members. First profit through jobs and levies, then duty fulfilment financially and differently, then environment, then social responsibility. The public claim group bundles this. Whoever only counts the cash register of the municipality, shortens; whoever only counts CSR language without levies, likewise. The sentence assigns the elements of the same line.

The statement is true.

Society, not just shareholders. Social responsibility towards society aims at the wider environment, while owners and shareholders pursue their own goals with money used in the capital line. The confusion between the words society and shareholders turns the addressee. The location expects perception of society as a whole. The exclusiveness of shareholders does not hold the presentation.

The statement is false.

title: Mutual expectations
context: Evaluate the following statements on reciprocity between businesses and stakeholders:
statements: Stakeholders have expectations of the company and the company has expectations of the Stakeholders.
Once a group is considered a stakeholder, the company cannot expect any more consideration.
The interaction includes personnel, supply chain, customers, investors and the location at the same time, not just a single group.
The technical expression Stakeholder groups are equated with stakeholders.
Only large enterprises with 250 or more employees have stakeholders; micro-enterprises remain without such groups.
tactical_explanations:
The final sentence of the passage is a plier. Many stakeholders have expectations of the company and the company expects to do so. Punctual work, available goods, paying customers, provided capital, viable public frameworks: these are counterparts to wages, pay, favorable price, capital development and location quality. To demand only one side without affording, this pliers blows. The introduction had already formulated the same thought as reciprocal influence; here it is repeated as a logic of expectation. The sentence represents precisely this reciprocity.

The statement is true.

Stakeholder status does not erase the opposite. The company expects employees to perform, from suppliers goods, from customers acceptance, from funders funds, from the location reliable conditions. A ban on any consideration would delete the phrase "to which the company also has expectations". Claim group means relationship, not unilateral alimination. The absolute lock does not hold the representation.

The statement is false.

The list is cumulatively read the landscape of the stakeholders, not a menu with just one course. Personnel, suppliers, customers, owners and sponsors, community and country are one after another. Influence on several groups of people and the environment means exactly this breadth. Whoever only allows the clientele as a stakeholder, repeats the narrowed-down ownership trap in a different form. The sentence takes the whole list.

The statement is true.

Stakeholders: the German term means, the English equivalent is beside it. The section introduces anglicism not as a substitute theory, but as a synonym in brackets. Exam answers may both use, if they mean the same group. The sentence meets this equation.

The statement is true.

Size does not change the existence of stakeholders. The passage is before the UGB definition and far ahead of the SME table. A micro enterprise with three persons nevertheless has personnel or at least owner work, suppliers, customers, often a municipality. The threshold 250 employees sorts large enterprises in the size chart, not the stakeholder definition. The linking of both chapters is an invention.

The statement is false.

title: Small firms in the size table
context: Evaluate the following statements on the category of small enterprises:
statements: Small companies have up to 49 employees and sales or balance sheet totals up to 10 million euros.
A company with 8 employees and 5 million euros of annual turnover remains a micro-enterprise according to the table.
Micro-enterprises and small enterprises are the same category with the same thresholds in the table.
A company with 40 employees and 8 million euros in turnover lies within the thresholds of small companies.
The financial sizes of the microline and the small line differ: up to 2 million euros compared to up to 10 million euros in sales or balance sheet total.
tactical_explanations:
The second row of tables is based on the smallest. Up to 49 heads, sales up to 10 million euros or balance sheet total up to 10 million euros: these are the small companies. The coupling of staff and financial size is as true as the smallest: both dimensions are in the table, connected with turnover or balance sheet total. Tax regulations, accounting and promotion are hanging on such thresholds, therefore the line is more than statistics. The sentence returns the small line without retelling the EU recommendation.

The statement is true.

Eight heads would be small-scale, five million euros in sales would not. Two lines, two bundles of thresholds. Small: up to 9 and up to 2 million. Small: up to 49 and up to 10 million. The case illustrates the small category without touching the 250 threshold of the big ones. The sentence assigns the numbers to the right line.

The statement is true.

Two against ten, that is the financial leap. Micro-enterprises up to 2 million euros in turnover or balance sheet total, small to 10 million. The employee limits 9 against 49 run parallel. title: SMEs in the EU and turnover under one million

SMEs as a collective term include micro-enterprises, small and medium-sized enterprises below the class of the large ones.

The same number dominance across Europe as in Austria later on. Around 99 percent of companies in the EU are SMEs, defined in a Union recommendation. The sentence reflects the EU number of the section. Austria's also around 99 percent are in the next data box and confirm the picture for the domestic market, but do not replace the European figure.

Less than one million is less than two million, not more than one million. 85 percent are small enough to fit into the smallest line financially, provided the employee limit is right. The conclusion that they are above the 2 million smallest threshold, twists smaller and larger. If you confuse 1 million with 2 million over, you cannot apply the table, 85 percent of which measure the number of farms, not an automatic middle class.
