The absolute "no large companies" exceeds the 99 percent figure.

The statement is false.

Three classes under the umbrella SMEs, the fourth is called large. Small, small, medium, the abbreviations are given; English SME or MSME respectively. Large start in the table from 250 heads or above the financial thresholds. The collective term is necessary precisely because tax, accounting and promotion depend on size. The sentence holds the composition without recalculating the thresholds.

The statement is true.

title: High-turnover large firms in Austria

Membership of this top-of-the-line turnover makes each of the above-mentioned groups mandatory for a micro-enterprise according to the EU table.

Names as illustrations of the top sales, not as a duty to memorize all company names. Rechtsformen AG, GmbH and SE appear, but belong to the next section; here counts the size of sales, not the registration technology and not the brand advertising.

The scale is in the bracket: measured by turnover. Knownness, number of employees or sector alone do not replace this bar in the formulation. A small cult enterprise can be more known than a silent wholesaler and still not fall into this top. The data box separates number dominance of SMEs from the turnover mass of the big ones. The set holds the scale.

The statement is true.

99 percent of the total number of companies allows the remaining percentage to be large. Some more than one third of the turnover is generated by around 1900 large companies. That is why OMV or Strabag can be strong in sales, while almost all companies remain SMEs. The conclusion "cannot happen" merges the counting of companies with the existence of the corporations. The section juxtaposes both observations.

The statement is false.

The series goes on to three names. REWE International, Spar, voestalpine, Mondi, ÖBB, Andritz and Red Bull are listed in the same list. Trade, steel, paper, railway, plant construction, beverages: various industries, common feature of sales size. The set bundles the remaining explicitly mentioned examples without inventing a non-named company.

The smallest is up to 9 employees and up to 2 million euros in turnover or balance sheet total. The turnover peaks of the Austrian commercial economy are beyond this line and illustrate large companies. The EU table and the list of names together show the opposite of micro. The mandatory micro-labelling is a confusion of brand awareness with the lowest size class.

The statement is false.

title: Demand, costs and profit motive
context: Evaluate the following statements the ratio of revenue, expenditure and profit intention:
statements: Strong customer demand alone does not guarantee any profit if expenditure exceeds revenue.
Mr Manner and Mr Woom are well led with a profit intention, even if they do not need to do so legally in order to be considered as companies.
The usual guideline for profit-oriented holdings is, according to the section, merely cost recovery without any surplus.
Profits can be reinvested to support the long-term performance and competitiveness.
Profit means keeping yields and expenses exactly the same.
tactical_explanations:
Profit is a difference, not a visitor's volume. Take more than spend, more income than expenditure: if the cost side overtakes the revenue, no profit remains despite the rush. Value and benefit can arouse buying interest and still not save the bill as soon as equipment, materials, personnel and know-how come to be more expensive than the proceeds. Strong demand explains sales opportunities, not automatically the surplus. The rate draws the simplification formula against the trap, demand suffices. Note: Sales or sales quantity are not the same size as profit.

The statement is true.

The actual intention and legal obligation are different. Both example businesses are led with profit intent; the UGB definition does not require this because the activity does not have to be directed towards profit. The phrase "even if they do not need to be the point of the example." An NPO can be a company, Manner remains profit-oriented. The sentence holds exactly this doubling.

The statement is true.

Cost recovery is the primary orientation of the NPO, not the guideline of profit-oriented. woom and Manner are to take more than spend; reinvestment of profits supports survival and competitiveness. Just cover without surplus would be the lower limit of existence (covering and payable), not the usual goal of profit intention. The confusion between NPO's guideline and profit operation reverses the section.

The statement is false.

The bridge mechanism is to reinvest. Profits are usually essential for the survival, because they can flow back into the company. Thus, the operation remains performance- and competitive and in loss phases less risk of overindebtedness. The sentence applies this use without claiming that every profit must remain absolutely completely within. Distribution and reinvestment can stand side by side; the presentation emphasizes the second as a way to survival.

The statement is true.

The balance of income and expenditure is cover, not profit. Profit means more income than expenditure, i.e. a surplus. Exact equality describes the cost-covering limit at which business economy can still bear existence, but no profit arises in the sense of simplification. The equation of profit and zero balance contradicts "more ... than." For NPOs, cost recovery can be the guideline; that does not make the zero balance a profit concept.

The statement is false.

title: NPOs between cost recovery and surplus
context: A non-profit organization accepts donations and places occasional surpluses in the offer. Rate the following statements:
statements: The primary orientation remains cost recovery, even if accounting surpluses arise and flow back into the supply.
Donation money is an example of revenue that can be used to better pursue goals.
Without sufficient revenue, an NPO still pursues its objectives according to the text equally well, because non-profit makes any financing unnecessary.
Reinvested surpluses can help an NPO to improve and expand its supply without necessarily following profit maximisation as a purpose.
Each surplus transforms the NPO into a company that must be geared towards profit making.
tactical_explanations:
Guideline and accounting balance are two levels. The NPO is primarily oriented towards cost-covering work. An occasional surplus that flows back into the offer does not change this orientation into profit maximization. The section explicitly says NPOs benefited from the reinvestment of profits because they improve and expand offer. Profit means the accounting surplus here, not the purpose of the organization. Donations can bear the income side; the balance made is the extension of the task. The consulting institution remains NPO as long as cost coverage and order lead.

The statement is true.

Donations are inflow, not blemish. With sufficient income, for example donations, the NPO pursues its goals better and communicates the range of tasks better to the target group. The institution in the case can therefore accept donations without becoming a man. The sentence links capacity to action to means, as the presentation does.

The statement is true.

Non-profit does not mean free of funding. The presentation combines better target tracking with sufficient revenue. Lack of inflows, cost coverage theory and communication to the target group remain weaker. The claim that non-profit makes financing unnecessary and the goals always remained equally well accessible contradicts this very condition structure. Volunteering does not replace the mentioned donations as an example in the book text.

The statement is false.

The same reinvestment that keeps profitable companies efficient helps NPOs in offering. The purpose remains the task compared to the target group, not the maximum payout. Therefore, the consulting institution can leave in surplus without abandoning the NPO concept. The sentence separates mechanics (return) and purpose (non-profit).

The statement is true.

UGB does not require a profit-or-profit orientation. An enterprise is any permanent organization of independent economic activity, even if it is not directed towards profit. A surplus does not change this third feature into a duty. The NPO can remain legally enterprise and still do not have to be geared towards profit-making. The change statement merges accounting balances and legal definition.

The statement is false.

title: Several sectors, energy and crafts
context: Evaluate the following statements the sector classification beyond the three core examples:
statements: Whether a company operates in one or more sectors of the economy depends on the subject matter of the company.
The energy sector is the secondary sector.
The craft sector, together with the entire industry, is a secondary sector.
The energy sector is a primary sector because electricity comes from natural resources.
A company must never be active in more than one economic sector at the same time.
tactical_explanations:
Subject before label, and the plural is allowed. In which sector or sectors: the formulation allows multiple affiliation if the subject gives this. A company can promote and process or produce and act. Legal form, number of employees and registered office do not replace this examination. The sentence is at the beginning of the sector section and controls all the following examples. which remains secondary because of wheel production, a mixed object could carry two sectors. The subsequent industry rule follows the same logic of the activity area.

The statement is true.

Energy in addition to industry and crafts. The secondary sector produces products from raw materials and covers the entire industry, the trade and the energy industry. Electricity generation is thus at the conversion stage, not at the ore pit and not at the consulting office. The sentence isolates the third element of the secondary bracket, which is slightly lost in the core examples Woom and Manner.

The statement is true.

Handicraft is secondary, even without group format. Carpentry, installers, electricians and locksmiths later appear as industry examples of the handiwork; sectorwise they remain in the production of raw materials and raw materials. Industry plus handicraft plus energy form the secondary brackets. Anyone who pushes craft into the trade (tertiary) confuses workshop and shop. The sentence follows the sector definition.

The statement is true.

Natural origin does not make a primary sector. Primary is raw material extraction: agriculture, forestry, fishing, mining. Secondary is the transformation, and that is where the energy industry stands. Tourism on the landscape is tertiary; energy production is the other trap of the same natural metaphor. Electricity from water or wind remains secondary in the book system. The shift into the primary mixes source and transformation.

The statement is false.

"What sectors is never the same in plural? The object can fill several sectors. A company with a sawmill and furniture factory or with production and its own trade would otherwise be forced to deny half of the activity. The absolute is a rule that does not set up the introductory sentence. The sector of activity is then subject to multiple membership.

The statement is false.

title: Forestry, fishing, construction and craft trades
context: Evaluate the following statements on finer allocations in sectors and sectors:
statements: Forestry and fisheries are part of the primary sector's raw material extraction.
The construction of buildings illustrates the construction industry.
Carpentry, installers, electricians and locksmiths concretely define the trade as an industry.
Wholesale and retail trade are the trade sectors.
Gastronomy is a mining sector and thus a primary sector.
tactical_explanations:
Four fields of extraction, two of which are often overlooked. Besides agriculture and mining, forestry and fisheries are in the parenthesis of the primary sector. Wood picks and fish catch remain raw material extraction, even if later furniture or fillets are created. The rate is applied to the two middle segments of the definition, without needing to produce and harvest fruit as a single example, or relabelling the forest to the furniture industry.

The statement is true.

Construction is an industry, not just a synonym for the secondary sector as a whole. Building construction is a staple example of the construction sector. Services are similar within one sector; building is a common feature of both high and related construction. Sectorally, much of it is secondary, but the industry label is construction. The sentence meets the first industry example of the text.

The statement is true.

Four trades, one industry. Carpentry, installers, electricians and locksmiths are in the handrail. Similar craftsmanship is tied to them, not the same legal form. Interest groups often follow exactly this kind of industry logic because challenges are similar. The sentence fills the craft with the mentioned sectors instead of with an empty heading.

The statement is true.

The trade divides into wholesale and retail trade. Both remain tertiary as a service of mediation, not secondary as a production. The bicycle dealer with which in the range was the sector example; here the industry is differentiated internally. The rate reflects both mentioned trading levels. Pharma, telecommunications, tourism, gastronomy, transport and logistics as well as media are other sectors that are sidelined, but do not replace this internal division of trade.

The statement is true.

Gastronomy is a sector of services related to catering, not mining. Mining remains primary raw material extraction. Those who equate kitchen and mine confuse two completely separate lists: sector definition against industry examples. Gastronomy sits alongside tourism and trade in the service field. The assignment to mining is not relevant to the text.

The statement is false.

title: Size, sector and location claims
context: Evaluate the following statements , linking size classes, sectors and stakeholders:
statements: The number dominance of SMEs does not preclude high-turnover companies such as voestalpine AG being a factor in the secondary sector.
Because the tertiary sector in Austria accounts for around 70 percent of the economic output, steel production is attributable to the tertiary sector.
The local community expects jobs and taxes at the same time with mandatory fulfilment, environmental care and social responsibility.
Micro enterprises according to the table and Austria's largest groups of companies fall into the same size class.
An enterprise can be classified in several sectors, while the sector is classified in the same way as the enterprise.

Two cuts, one country. Almost all companies are SMEs, but voestalpine is on the list of the largest companies in sales and produces metals, i.e. secondary. Number of companies and economic weights fall apart; sector follows the subject, not the SME share. Steel from ore is the book bridge from primary mining to secondary hut. The rate of co-existence of small business census and large industrial enterprises is not changing the classification of about two thirds of the workforce in SMEs and just under two thirds of the turnover of the commercial economy.

The statement is true.

Macro-part is not a company sign. Around 70 percent of Austrian economic output is described in terms of tertiary. voestalpine remains metal production, i.e. secondary, just as Manner Waffles bakes and Woom builds wheels. The average of the economy does not re-label every single production. Otherwise, in a service-rich country, every hut would be a consulting office. The confusion of aggregate and object is the same trap as in Woom and Manner, here at steel production.

The statement is false.

The public line is a bundle, not a single point. Profit through jobs and taxes, descendants of financial and other obligations, careful environmental management, social responsibility towards society: all expectations of the community and the country. Whoever only counts the wage sum or just a sustainability brochure does not fully meet the list. Stakeholders at the site are thus wider than the tax payer. The sentence reads the line cumulatively as the representation writes it.

The statement is true.

Lower and uppermost line of size. Small: up to 9 employees, up to 2 million euros in turnover or balance sheet total. The turnover peak with OMV, Strabag or Red Bull illustrates large companies, from 250 heads or more than 50 million euros in turnover or 43 million euros in balance sheet total. The same class of claims makes the classification for tax, accounting and promotion worthless. Number of SMEs does not explain why the table needs four lines. The equation is wrong.

The statement is false.

Two allocation rules, related to the plural. The activity determines the sector or the sector; the subject of the enterprise determines the sector or sectors. Similar products or services bind the sector; the extraction of raw materials, production or service bind the sector. A trade and craft company can carry two branches and touch tertiary plus secondary. The sentence combines both book rules without putting size or legal form in their place.

The statement is true.

title: Firm size under the EU recommendation
context: A business consultant will classify companies in size classes according to the EU recommendation. Evaluate the following statements about the company size:
statements: A bicycle shop with 9 employees, 1.8 million euros in turnover and 1.6 million euros in balance sheet total is considered as a micro-enterprise according to the EU recommendation.

A supplier with 45 employees, 9 million euros in turnover and 11 million euros in balance sheet total is still one of the small companies, because one of the two limits is sufficient for turnover and balance sheet total.
A mechanical engineering company with 240 employees and sales of 65 million euros remains medium-sized, because the number of employees under 250 alone decides on this.

A company with 200 employees, 55 million euros in turnover and 40 million euros in balance sheet total remains medium-sized, because the balance sheet total is less than 43 million euros, even if the turnover exceeds the 50 million limit.
For medium-sized companies, the balance sheet total ceiling of EUR 50 million is higher than the turnover ceiling of EUR 43 million.
tactical_explanations:
Micro-enterprises may have a maximum of 9 employees, with a maximum turnover of 2 million euros or balance sheet total. The bicycle shop remains exactly on the passenger limit with 9 heads, and both 1.8 and 1.6 million euros are below 2 million. None of the three values breaks the respective threshold.

The statement is true.

Turnover and balance sheet total are alternatives: it is enough if one of the two monetary sizes meets the limit of 10 million euros. The supplier remains below the 49 limit with 45 employees, and its turnover of 9 million is below 10 million, although the balance sheet total of 11 million already exceeds it. Because only one money size has to fit, the company remains small.

The statement is true.

240 employees are below the 250 threshold of large companies, but the number of persons is only one of two conditions. In addition, it requires a maximum of 50 million euros of turnover or a maximum of 43 million euros of balance sheet total. With 65 million euros of turnover, the company breaks the higher money limit without a lower balance sheet total absorbing this. The number of persons alone does not save the middle class.

The statement is false.

For medium-sized enterprises, turnover and balance sheet totals may have different ceilings: 50 million in turnover, but only 43 million in balance sheet total, and both are considered as alternatives. With 200 employees under 249 and a balance sheet total of 40 million below 43 million, the company remains medium-sized, even if the turnover of 55 million exceeds the 50 million limit.

The statement is true.

The two monetary limits of medium-sized enterprises are not equal: The turnover may amount to 50 million euros, but the balance sheet total only up to 43 million euros. The balance sheet total threshold is therefore lower, not higher than the turnover threshold. Those who exchange both figures consider the smaller limit to be the larger.

The statement is false.

title: EU size classes: OR/AND traps
context: Four farms are to be assigned to the EU size classes. The thresholds themselves are not printed. Rate the following statements:
statements: A company with 8 employees, 1.5 million euros in turnover and 2.3 million euros in balance sheet total remains micro-enterprises, because at least the turnover is less than 2 million euros.
A company with 40 employees and 9 million euros in turnover is automatically a small company, regardless of its balance sheet total, once the number of employees is below 49.
A company with 9 employees and 12 million euros in turnover remains micro-enterprises, because the number of persons is less than 10.
A company with 249 employees, 50 million euros in turnover and 43 million euros in balance sheet total is still in the middle category.
A company with 250 employees and only 20 million euros in turnover is already one of the large companies.
tactical_explanations:
Eight heads and a suitable money size are sufficient. For micro-enterprises, a maximum of 9 employees and a maximum of 2 million euros are valid for turnover or balance sheet total; one of the two monetary sizes is sufficient. The company has 8 employees and 1.5 million euros in turnover, i.e. under both thresholds on the person and turnover side. The total balance sheet of 2.3 million is over 2 million, but the Oder criterion allows the turnover to be a saving size. Therefore, the micro category remains.

The statement is true.

No small company is making any of 49 heads alone. In addition to the number of persons, the category also needs a maximum of 10 million euros in turnover or balance sheet total. Here 40 employees and 9 million euros in turnover are mentioned, but the balance sheet total is missing. "Automatically and "independent of the balance sheet total" misrepresent the number of persons alone. Without the second money size, the assignment remains uncertain.

The statement is false.

Nine heads do not save a broken turnover limit. Micro-enterprises need an additional turnover of up to 2 million euros or balance sheet total. With 12 million euros turnover this limit is far exceeded. Without a low balance sheet total as an alternative, no door to the micro-category remains open. The operation slips at least into the next higher class, no matter how narrow the passenger limit is still maintained.

The statement is false.

The middle class still counts on the border. 249 employees, 50 million euros in turnover and 43 million euros in total balance sheet are exactly on the three upper limits of the medium-sized companies. At the border itself the category is still fulfilled, not already exceeded. Only 250 employees, more than 50 million turnover or more than 43 million balance sheet total open the large category. All three values are still holding here.

The statement is true.

The number of people is determined by 250 heads and above. The threshold 250 makes the company a large company, regardless of how low sales or balance sheet total are. 20 million euros turnover does not change this, because the person characteristic already takes hold. The money sizes play the decisive role only below 250 employees. Here the threshold of the person is already torn.

The statement is true.

title: FunBike: size class from memory
context: FunBike GmbH has a balance sheet total of 9 638 250 euros at the end of the year. Further thresholds are not repeated here. Evaluate the following statements about the EU size class and the SME term:
statements: Just because of this balance sheet total, FunBike can still fall into the category of small companies, provided that the number of employees and turnover meets the remaining limits.
The category of micro-enterprises is excluded solely because of this balance sheet total.
Just because the balance sheet total is below the balance sheet total limit of medium-sized enterprises, FunBike is automatically a large company.
Around 99 percent of EU businesses are micro, small and medium-sized.
Large enterprises are also SMEs, according to the SME concept, because they are the largest of the four size classes.
tactical_explanations:
The door to "small" remains just under ten million. Small companies may have a balance sheet total of up to 10 million euros if the other criteria are appropriate. FunBike has 9 638 250 euros, including them. The category of small companies does not exclude this balance sheet total alone; the number of employees and turnover only have to comply with the remaining limits. The sum is compatible with "small".

The statement is true.

Two million are the balance sheet ceiling of the smallest. Micro-enterprises may have a maximum balance sheet total of 2 million euros. FunBike is clearly above 9 638 250 euros. Even this one value is sufficient to exclude the smallest category, regardless of how low sales or number of persons would be. The balance sheet total alone ends here the lowest size class.

The statement is true.

No one is big at the budget line. Large companies start with 250 employees or more than 50 million euros in sales or over 43 million euros in total assets. FunBike's balance sheet total is below 43 million and does not automatically close the large category. The statement distorts the threshold logic: being below a limit is the opposite of "automatically large".

The statement is false.

Almost the total number of enterprises is SMEs. Small, small and medium-sized enterprises together form SMEs; large enterprises are outside the EU. Around 99 percent of the enterprises in the EU fall below the large ones in these three classes. The quota measures the number of enterprises, not the percentage of turnover of the giants. The sentence meets exactly this dominance of the smaller legal and size forms.

The statement is true.

Large is outside the definition of SMEs. SMEs only bundle micro, small and medium-sized enterprises; the fourth size class of large enterprises does not belong to them. "The largest class is not "still part of SMEs", but the counterpart. Anyone who refers to large enterprises in the SME concept, cuts the distinction that makes the term meaningful.

The statement is false.

title: Austria's business landscape in shares
context: Evaluate the following statements on the Austrian business landscape and the importance of SMEs:
statements: SMEs also dominate in Austria, with around 99 percent of the number of enterprises, as well as in the EU as a whole.
Because around 90 percent of companies have fewer than ten employees, around 90 percent of all employees work in such micro-enterprises.
About 85 percent of companies have less than one million euros of turnover per year.
Around two thirds of the workforce work in SMEs.
Because around 1,900 large companies only make up a small part of the number of companies, they automatically generate only a correspondingly small share of the total turnover.
tactical_explanations:
Austria reflects the EU quota. Around 99 percent of the companies here are SMEs, as measured by the number of enterprises. The order of magnitude corresponds to the EU as a whole, because the Austrian landscape is also characterized by very many small units. Dominance of the number is not the same as dominance of turnover. Nevertheless, the landscape remains clearly small-scale.

The statement is true.

The number of enterprises and the number of employees is two different indicators. Although around 90 per cent of the enterprises are micro-enterprises, because each of them employs only a few people, only a small part of the workforce works there; in total, around two thirds of all employees work in SMEs as a whole, not especially in micro-enterprises. Many plants with few heads do not automatically result in many heads overall.

The statement is false.

One million euros marks the lower margin of turnover. About 85 percent of companies remain below this brand and are therefore still below the minimum turnover limit of 2 million. The figure describes the accumulation of very small sales, not the EU class threshold itself. It shows how strongly the distribution at the lower end is compacted.

The statement is true.

Two thirds of the heads, not of the companies. As employers, SMEs employ around two thirds of all the workers. This is a measure of the number of people, not of the number of companies. The approximately 99 percent of the company does not contradict this: many small enterprises employ just a few people. Number and employment share are deliberately to be read separately.

The statement is true.

A small number of companies can still generate a large share of turnover. Around 1,900 large companies are a small group in terms of numbers, but bear just over a third of the total sales revenues of the Austrian commercial economy, because individual large companies implement many times more than individual micro-enterprises. Number and share of sales are deliberately running counter.

The statement is false.

title: EU size classes: how the criteria interact
context: Evaluate the following statements on the interaction of the number of employees, turnover and balance sheet total in the EU size classification of enterprises:
statements: In order to be classified as a size class, turnover and balance sheet total must be below the same euro limit at the same time; one criterion alone is not sufficient.
For medium-sized companies, the turnover and balance sheet totals are limited to different amounts: 50 million euros in turnover, 43 million euros in balance sheet total.
