Origin decides on the name. What founders, founders and partners bring in is considered equity, regardless of whether banks lend later. The deposit creates their own basis from which theory distinguishes the debt financing by third parties. Anyone who only lets bank money be considered as capital miss the starting point according to the legal forms: first the parties contribute funds, only after that more possibilities come. Deposits of property are on this own basis as well as transfers of funds as soon as they are assigned to the company. The statement is made precisely by this allocation of the contribution, not by the credit relationship with the bank that was later treated.

The statement is true.

The capital includes financial resources and in-kind deposits. A vehicle or computer that goes into the operation increases its own base as well as a transfer. The claim that only money amounts count, removes the item from the definition. Both are called in one breath and illustrates it on the van with two PCs. Without contributions in kind, the definition of equity would be incomplete.

The statement is false.

The example and rule coincide. If a small van and two PCs are introduced in addition to money, these deposits increase equity. The text of the teaching selects this image to make it clear that not only the account balance but also usable items count as soon as they belong to the company. The foundation capital base grows by the value of these deposits. Those who absolve them as private toys without capital impact contradict the example.

The statement is true.

Repayment is not the rule at this time. Equity does not have to be repaid and is therefore available in the long term, usually indefinitely. An obligation to return everything to donors after a short period of time would treat equity as a temporary loan. This is exactly what distinguishes the table: debt capital is limited and repayable, subject to agreement, and equity is not. The rate reverses this feature.

The statement is false.

Indeterminately, the normal case of own funds is the case. Because there is no obligation to repay, the deposits usually remain without the end date for the company. Therefore, equity capital is suitable for long-term investments whose benefits run for years. "In general, indefinite" leaves rare contractual special routes open, but does not change the book rule. If you think equity is a three-month loan, you miss the timeline of the table.

The statement is true.

title: Equity, profits and interest
context: Evaluate the following statements on the consequences of equity for interest, distributions and investments:
statements: Equity is a possible appropriate financing method for long-term investments.
In periods when no profits are generated, the interest on equity must be the same as on a loan.
If profits are generated, disbursements can be made to the equity providers, but there is no obligation to do so.
If profits are retained in the company, they increase equity.
For many companies, it is realistic to finance itself entirely through equity.
tactical_explanations:
The deadline and purpose are consistent. Because equity does not have to be repaid and usually remains indefinite, it is called a possible appropriate financing method for long-term investments. Machines, fleets or computer equipment are only purchased at larger intervals; the funds are to bear for as long as possible, otherwise the repayment pressure is created while the plant is still being used. Suitable does not only mean that debt capital can also be long-term, for example as a multi-year bank loan, depending on the agreement. The rate determines the suitability of own funds without banning loans or reinterpreting short-term delivery liabilities to machine financing.

The statement is true.

Interest is imposed on the loan, not on the deposit. No interest is paid for equity in periods without profit as for a loan. Creditors usually demand interest regardless of the annual result; equity providers do not have such a fixed claim in loss years. The equalization of both charges in sluggish years is therefore wrong. Only when there are wins can payouts follow without becoming a requirement.

The statement is false.

It is not possible, but it does not. In the case of profits, disbursements may be made to the equity providers, but there is no obligation to do so according to theory. The shareholders can leave instead. This freedom distinguishes profit shares from credit interest, which are due regardless of the wishes of the management. The sentence specifies the option and the missing obligation.

The statement is true.

Leave strengthens its own base. Profits that remain in the company increase equity. This is the same process that the section later calls self-financing: internal financing from the turnover that raises the crisis resistance. Distribution reduces this increase, retention increases it. The statement describes the capital effect, not the tax return.

The statement is true.

Full self-financing is often desired. For many companies it is unrealistic to finance itself entirely via equity. Therefore, third parties, typically banks, occur and debt capital is generated. The claim that complete self-financing is realistic for many, reverses the teaching sentence. Mixing of own and foreign means is the normal case, not the exception.

The statement is false.

title: Debt capital from third parties
context: Evaluate the following statements on debt capital:
statements: If the capital comes from third parties, for example from a bank, it is called debt capital.
Debt capital is usually available for a limited period and must be repaid.
Loans are the most important form of debt capital.
Debtors usually have the same say in corporate governance as equity providers.
Interest must never be paid for debt capital because only equity is paid interest.
tactical_explanations:
Third parties provide foreign funds. As soon as the capital does not come from founders or partners, but from outside, for example from a bank, it is called debt capital. The bank becomes a creditor, not a co-owner, by credit; participation in the management usually remains out. Suppliers can play the same role in the short term when paid for on target. The term follows the source of third parties, not the mere fact that money is in the account. Repayment and mostly interest are part of this relationship, in contrast to the deposit. The statement is made by the book definition of foreign means.

The statement is true.

Temporary and redemption are part of the debt capital. It is usually only available for a limited period and must be repaid. At the end of the term, the capital itself is due, in addition to any interest. "Generally" leaves special cases open, but describes the standard that the feature table holds: short or long term depending on the agreement, always with repayment.

The statement is true.

Credit is the main form, not the only one. Loans are called the most important form of debt capital. In the long term, banks are the main providers, in the short term, suppliers with payment targets are added; large companies can issue bonds. The priority of the loan does not break these other ways, but orders them according to frequency. Anyone who treats the loan as a marginal phenomenon misses the weighting of the text.

The statement is true.

The legal status follows, not the amount of money. Capital investors have rights to participate depending on the legal form; debt investors usually have no say in corporate management. A bank does not control the operation simply because it gives a loan, unless special collateral contracts regulate otherwise. The equation of both participation is the reversal of the table. Creditors secure repayment, shareholders lead.

The statement is false.

Interest is typically on the outside. Usually, debt capital must be interest-bearing, i.e. interest payments to creditors. Equity does not require such interest in loss years. The claim that debt capital is never to be interest-bearing and only equity-bearing interest, twists both columns of the table. Even those who pay on target and skip discount pay exactly for the supplier's loan. Free interest is the exception here, not the rule.

The statement is false.

title: Equity and debt: voice, security, term
context: Evaluate the following statements on the typical characteristics of equity and debt capital:
statements: Equity providers have rights to different degrees depending on the legal form.
Debtor investors usually have no say in corporate governance.
Equity providers always have a guarantee for the repayment of their capital.
If the loan is sufficiently secured, lenders may have a guarantee for repayment.
Debt capital may be available in the short term or in the long term by agreement.
tactical_explanations:
The legal form controls the voice of the own. Equity providers have rights to participate, but not in uniform strength: the extent depends on the legal form. In a partnership, different rules of participation apply than in a capital company with management and shareholder meeting. Different does not mean zero; it means that the form determines who is talking to how far. Debt investors usually remain outside.

The statement is true.

Creditors usually do not run the business. Debtors provide temporary funds, demand interest and repayment, but do not sit in the management instead of the shareholders. "As a rule, special contractual commitments are left open, but do not change the basic rule. Anyone who assigns the Bank the same influence as the owners merges credit agreements and the creation of a company.

The statement is true.

Own funds do not have any repayment security. Equity does not have to be repaid; a permanent guarantee for repayment would treat own funds as a secured loan. That is why there is no such guarantee in principle for equity providers. "Always a security reverses this feature. The collateral is part of the debt-capital logic, not the deposit.

The statement is false.

The collateral is determined on the external side. If the loan is sufficiently secured, the lender may have a security for the repayment. Mortgage, pledge or similar collateral will give access if not paid. Without sufficient collateral, this security is missing. The statement makes the condition clear and does not claim automatic full collateral of each loan.

The statement is true.

The agreement sets the deadline. Debt capital can be available in the short term or in the long term, depending on the contract. Delivery liabilities often cover weeks, bank loans years, bonds also longer term. Equity usually remains indefinite; the external side is precisely the flexible one. Anyone who thinks of debt capital as always long-term or only as always short-term ignores the freedom of agreement.

The statement is true.

title: Trade payables and cash discount
context: A trading company buys goods at destination and checks whether it should use discount or exploit the payment target. Evaluate the following statements:
statements: In the case of short-term credit financing, suppliers are important lenders in addition to banks.
If deliveries need to be paid on target, the suppliers will finance them and the delivery liabilities will arise.
If, for the benefit of the payment goal, a possible deduction for immediate payment (screet), interest is paid for the payment on target.
The discount's effective return is in most cases so low that it should always be paid on target.
The short-term overdraft of the bank account to pay more quickly and use discount can be the more economically meaningful option.
tactical_explanations:
Short-term credit has two typical donors. Long-term credit financing comes mainly from banks; in the short term, suppliers stand alongside banks. Anyone who thinks of the institution as a lender only has to overlook the payment target as a loan relationship with delivery liabilities. The commodity is there, the money is not yet: that is precisely short-term debt capital, often without a separate loan agreement. Lost discount makes it even an expensive variant. The sentence juxtaposes both donors, as the text describes the short-term page.

The statement is true.

The supplier will finance the time period if paid later; delivery liabilities to these suppliers will be incurred in an accounting manner. This is not a gift and not an equity capital, but short-term debt. The wording "to the target" explicitly translates the presentation as payment at a later date. Without this shift, the operation would have to use liquid funds immediately.

The statement is true.

The loss of interest is in a different form. Whoever leaves the price deduction for immediate payment pays for the payment goal: the higher invoice amount is the consideration for later payments. It is therefore true that it would actually also pay interest for the payment on target. The supplier credit is not interest-free, just because no separate interest invoice comes. Discount waiver and interest on loans are economically related.

The statement is true.

High, not low, is the typical effective interest rate. In most cases, the effective interest rate of the discount is very high. Therefore, the target's outreach may be more expensive than a short current account. The recommendation to always pay to target because the discount effect is low, reverses the order of magnitude. "In most cases, very high" is the book statement, not a marginal note. Anyone who treats the target as a free-of-charge study underestimates the costs.

The statement is false.

Overdrafting can be cheaper than cancelling off the discount. Because the effective interest rate of the discount is often very high, the short-term overdrafting of the bank account for faster payments can be the more economically meaningful option. The operation pays the bank interest for a few days and retains the discount.

This is not a plea for permanent overdraft, but a comparison of two short-term borrowing costs. The statement reflects this very consideration.

Note: Discount acts like an expensive supplier loan, even without a reported interest rate.

The statement is true.

title: Internal financing and self-financing
context: Evaluate the following statements Internal financing:
statements: If the source of funding comes from the company's turnover, it is called internal financing.
Retention of profits is an important source of financing, is also called self-financing and increases equity.
Self-financing is external financing because customers pay the remuneration from outside the company.
Depreciation and provisioning may also be an internal source of financing.
Internal financing is only available if a bank grants the company a loan which is later served by sales.
tactical_explanations:
Source in turnover, name of internal financing. The section separates from where the funds come from: from the turnover of the company or from outside. If the source is in turnover, the transaction is called internal financing. Sales proceeds feed self-financing through retained profits, as well as earned depreciation and provisioning effects, because there is no disbursement. The definition depends on the source, not on the legal form label and not on the fact that customers transfer. Anyone who confuses internal financing with anything in the building or with a bank loan later redeemed from sales misses the source's revenue receipt.

The statement is true.

Retention has a second name and a capital effect. Retention of profits is an important source of internal income, means self-financing and increases equity. Less dependence on creditors, no interest on debt, buffers against losses: that is why it makes crisis-resistant. Distribution would be the opposite. The sentence combines description and effect as the text of the teaching combines them.

The statement is true.

Customer payment does not make any external financing out of profit. External financing is available if the source is outside the company: new deposits, loans, bonds. The fact that customers transfer the remuneration is the turnover from which internal financing comes. If every customer payment means external financing, there would not be internal financing. Self-financing remains internal financing and equity increase, not external input in the sense of the chart.

The statement is false.

Three internal routes are side by side. In addition to the retention of profits, depreciation and provisions can be sources of internal financing. Both reduce the profit as expense without paying out at the moment; the funds remain in operation for the time being and can bear other investments. The presentation explicitly links them to internal financing. Those who only allow self-financing to apply, will remove two of the above forms.

The statement is true.

Bank credit is external financing with debt capital. The source is outside the bank as a third party. The fact that repayment comes later from sales does not change the origin of the funds received. Internal financing requires that the source of funding itself comes from the turnover, not that a debt loan is earned at some point. The restriction "only if the bank..." distorts the definition.

The statement is false.

title: Retained earnings and over-indebtedness
context: Evaluate the following statements why retained profits make a company more crisis-resistant:
statements: Through self-financing, the company is less dependent on debt providers.
No interest on debt must be paid for retained profits.
If there is a lot of equity, an entity can survive several years of losses without being over-indebted.
If equity capital is rapidly used up and debt exceeds assets, the company is over-indebted and economically at risk.
Profits reinvested in the company cannot be renewed because self-financing is only used to repay the debt.
tactical_explanations:
Less leverage is derived from more own funds. Self-financing increases equity; the company then depends less on debt providers. Loans can remain, but the share and dependence decline if profits are not distributed but left. Crisis resistance means that not every investment step needs a new bank commitment, and loss years first consume at their own base instead of immediately on the threshold of over-indebtedness. The rate reflects the first of the reasons mentioned above, in addition to interest-free interest rates, loss buffers and reinvestment in investments.

The statement is true.

Own funds do not bear credit interest. Retained profits are equity, not interest-bearing debt. Therefore, no debt interest must be paid for. This relieves in years without profit, in which a loan would nevertheless demand interest. The free interest applies to this indoor source, not to bank loans running parallel. The second point of crisis in the text is precisely this lack of interest rate burden.

The statement is true.

Buffer against loss years is equity. Losses reduce equity. If much of it is available, several years can be taken up with minus without the company being over-indebted. The inventory starts the supply. Thin equity would be used up after a short time. The statement describes this temporal buffer without any loss to be trivialized.

The statement is true.

Overindebtedness has a clear threshold. If equity capital is quickly exhausted and debt capital exceeds assets, the company is overindebted and economically at risk. Debts larger than assets: its own base is gone. That's why a lot of equity strengthens resilience. The rate is the counter-probe to the loss buffer, not a second definition of insolvency proceedings.

The statement is true.

Reinvestment keeps the company modern. Profits that remain in the company and are reinvested help to renew plants and equipment; the company remains equipped and competitive. The claim that self-financing can only repay debts and cannot renew assets, strikes this fourth reason. Retention is internal financing for renewal, not a ban on replacement investments.

The statement is false.

title: Depreciation financing
context: An enterprise has invested 200,000 euros in property, plant and equipment that are used for ten years in a year. Evaluate the following statements on depreciation financing:
statements: If an enterprise also takes into account the loss in value of machinery, computers and vehicles, this loss in value means depreciation.
Depreciation represents a payout, so that the money leaves the company at the moment of booking.
The depreciation earned can be used for other investments in the meantime.
If the tangible fixed assets are used for ten years, the depreciation in this example amounts to 20,000 euros per year.
If the products are sold at the calculated prices, the depreciation of the products will be available for EUR 200,000 each year for ten years.
tactical_explanations:
The cost of the production is taken into account by the company. The cost of the production is usually plus profit. The cost of the production is the loss of value of machines, computers, vehicles: this is depreciation. If the price is sold at the calculated prices, this expense is also earned, although no payment is made in the year of booking in the amount of the loss of value. This is precisely the result of the internal financing margin for other investments, in the example 20,000 euros per year at 200,000 euros of purchase and ten years of use. The statement calls the term as the section introduces it without confusing the depreciation with the original purchase payment.

The statement is true.

The value loss does not constitute a payout; the money remains in the company for the time being. This is precisely the financing effect: effort reduces the profit, the cashier does not leave the amount. Anyone who treats depreciation as a transfer to the machine dealer in the booking year confuses purchase payment and later distribution of the loss in value. The internal source arises because it is not paid out.

The statement is false.

Parking and re-use. Because the depreciation earned does not flow, the funds can be used for other investments in the meantime. Thus, resources remain up to date, rather than the full purchase amount being broken by the replacement year. This is depreciation financing as internal financing, not a second equity of shareholders. The sentence shall apply to the purpose specified in the book.

The statement is true.

Purchase divided by useful life. 200,000 euros in one year, usage ten years: 200,000 divided by 10 results in 20,000 euros of depreciation per year. This amount goes into prices like other costs. The division is the linear distribution of the example, no new number invention. If you put 200,000 in depreciation every year, you'd want to make the same purchase ten times.

The statement is true.

Every year 20,000 euros are available, not 200,000. If the wheels are sold at the calculated prices, 20,000 euros are available every year for ten years. The 200,000 are the one-time purchase, not the annual internal financing amount. Who expects the full investment sum as a depreciation inflow, tenfold the example. The identity is: acquisition 200,000, duration 10, annual amount 20,000.

The statement is false.

title: Provisions financing
context: Evaluate the following statements on provision financing:
statements: Companies provide provisions for possible expenses in the future and thus provide for this in accounting.
Provisions may include a possible judicial process, holiday entitlements, pensions or settlement payments.
The provisioning is an effort that reduces the profit but does not represent a payout.
Because a provision reduces profits, there is no funding available for other investments in the meantime.
Pension provisions for employees who retire only in 20 or 30 years can have a long-term financing effect.
tactical_explanations:
Provision is the core of the provision. For possible future expenses, accountancy is provided before the amount flows. The company recognizes the imminent expense early, instead of reacting only on the payment day. Internal financing arises because the education is effortless without immediate cash outflow, analogous to depreciation. Court risk, vacation, pension and handling are typical occasions; for pensions in 20 or 30 years, the effect is even long-term. The sentence gives the definition without claiming that the money has already been passed on to creditors.

The statement is true.

Four occasions explicitly mention the presentation. A court process that the company could lose, vacation claims, pensions and settlement payments are mentioned cases. The list is exemplary, not closed, but exactly meets the mentioned types. Anyone who thinks provisions only as tax trick without factual reference misses these occasions. Each case is a possible later effort for which is now booked.

The statement is true.

The formation is expense and reduces the profit, similar to depreciation, without payment. Therefore, liquidity, which would otherwise be visible and perhaps distributed as profit, remains in the company. Creditors of a later pension have not yet received the money; the company can use the funds in the meantime. The statement separates the effect of success and the effect of payment as the text of the teaching does.

The statement is true.

Reduction of profit does not block the funds. Especially because the amounts are not paid out, the amounts are available for other investments in the meantime. This is the financing effect, analogous to depreciation. The claim that after reduction of profit nothing can be used any more confuses accounting expenditure with a drain from the account. Internal financing through provisions is based on this difference.

The statement is false.

Long horizons extend the effect. If employees only retire in 20 or 30 years, there is a further period between education and payment. This is called a long-term financing effect. Short-term holiday provisions have a shorter effect; pensions bear years. The statement takes the numerical example of the text as a time horizon, not as a mandatory rate.

The statement is true.

title: External financing with equity and debt
context: Evaluate the following statements on external financing:
statements: If the source of funding is outside the company, it is called external financing.
Both equity and debt can be transferred from outside.
External financing consists exclusively of debt capital, because equity can only arise through internal financing.
As previously stated, the most important external lenders are the suppliers and the banks.
Retention of profits from sales is the most important form of external financing.
tactical_explanations:
Outside the company, the source is not the building. If the source of funding is outside the company, the process is external financing. New shareholder deposits, i.e. equity of existing or new participants, bank loans, supply liabilities and bond issues come from there. The contrast is that sales as an internal source of self-financing, depreciation and provision. Anyone who confuses externally with export markets or with the mere location of the machine misses the financial distinction. The statement is the definition of the section and the entry into Figure 19.

The statement is true.

Two types of capital from outside. The graph and the presentation explicitly say: from outside, equity and debt capital can be transferred. Existing or new shareholders bring equity; banks, suppliers and bondholders bring debt capital. External financing is therefore not synonymous with credit. Whoever allows only one of the two sides halves Figure 19. The statement holds the double assignment.

The statement is true.

There is a very good external equity. The regular deposits of a GmbH, the share issue of an AG, the inclusion of new shareholders in other legal forms: this is external financing with equity. The internal capital is created primarily by self-financing. The claim that equity can only arise inside and outside is only foreign, contradicts the section. Both grids, own/foreign and inside/outside, are to be crossed, not equated.

The statement is false.

Suppliers and banks remain the main creditors. The presentation refers back: the most important lenders are suppliers and banks. Short-term payment target, short- and long-term credit; large companies additional bonds. The ranking does not exclude the bond, but presents everyday donors. The statement repeats this weighting.

The statement is true.

Retention is an internal part. Self-financing is generated by sales, increases equity and is internal financing. External financing would be a new deposit or a loan from third parties. The renaming of the profit retention to the most important external form mixes the two grids. Customers pay for performance; this does not make the retained profit a supply of investors outside the meaning of the graphic.

The statement is false.

title: Capital contributions and share issues
context: Evaluate the following statements on external financing by shareholders of a GmbH and a public limited company:
statements: Shareholders of a GmbH must make deposits called parent deposits or shares.
The share capital of different partners must always be equal and there is no minimum share capital.
In a public limited company, the share capital is divided into shares, so that large amounts of capital can be obtained more easily.
If shares are issued by the public limited liability company and bought by persons, this issue has a financing effect for the AG.
The share certifies a right of claim against the public limited company as a bond and not a share capital.
tactical_explanations:
GmbH deposits have two names. Shareholders must make deposits, regular deposits or shares. This is external financing with equity: the funds come from the parties involved, not from retained turnover and not as a bank loan. Different levels are possible as long as the minimum capital base is reached; equality of each individual contribution does not require the presentation. The AG later dissects share capital into shares, which does not change the GmbH terms. The sentence meets the name and obligation of the GmbH shareholders, without already mixing issue and share trading.

The statement is true.

The share capital of different shareholders may be different, but the minimum capital must be achieved overall. Equality of each contribution is not required, the minimum capital exists very well. The sentence asserts the opposite of both rules. Who demands the same mini-ins without a lower limit, does not describe the GmbH of the text.

The statement is false.

The share capital, also called share capital, is divided into shares, so that large capital amounts can be purchased more easily. Many people buy pieces instead of a single huge deposit. This is the financial sense of the AG in this section, not primarily the stock market prestige. The statement reflects exactly this procurement effect.

The statement is true.

Issue does not bring funds, the subsequent trading. If the AG issues shares and buys them, the AG will receive capital: financing effect of the issue. The share certifies a share right in the share capital. Permanently, without a planned repayment to the shareholders. The sentence describes only this first step, which separates the presentation of later share trading.

The statement is true.

Share is a share, bond is a claim. The share is a share right, a share of the share capital. Bonds are a claim right of the buyers against the issuer. Whoever makes the share a bond, exchanges equity inflow and debt capital inflow. Price is generated by supply and demand for the shares, which does not change the legal character. The statement is the wrong definition of securities.

The statement is false.

title: Share trading, price and capital increase
context: Evaluate the following statements on share trading and capital increase:
statements: The repayment of the share capital to shareholders is not foreseen; it is an unlimited capital provided.
If a shareholder sells her shares to another person, a further financing effect for the company will be the same as for the issue.
Shareholders benefit from price gains in stock trading.
If a public limited company increases its share capital, the existing shareholders have the right to buy the newly issued young shares.
Those who sell the subscription right to young shares prevent other persons from becoming shareholders.
tactical_explanations:
Indeterminate and without repayment plan. Share capital shall not be repaid to shareholders; it is available indefinitely, matching the equity side of the feature table. Shareholders increase by selling shares to others, not by the AG amortizing the share capital as a loan. This sale does not produce any further financing effect for the company, in contrast to the issue. The statement states exactly this duration of the deposit. Repayment to the nominal would be the vocabulary of the bond as debt capital, not the share as share right.

The statement is true.

The second market does not feed the AG. No further financing effect for the AG arises from the stock trading. Money changes between old and newly involved persons; the share capital of the company remains the same. Only the issue, the sale by the AG itself, brings its means. The equation of resale and issuance falsely doubles the inflow.

Price gains go to the selling shareholders.

Note: Only the issue by the AG finances the company, not the trade among investors.

The statement is false.

The price gain remains with the shareholders. Those who sell more than they bought realize the difference; the AG does not receive this amount during the second sale. The presentation clearly separates: no further financing effect for the AG, from price gains the shareholders profit. Supply and demand set the course. The statement is the allocation of the advantage.

The statement is true.

The subscription right secures the quota. In the event of a capital increase, existing shareholders may first buy the young shares and thus hold their percentage share capital if they wish. The right follows from the creation of the company, not from a stock market mood. Whoever ignores the young shares thins his share, if others sign. The sentence represents the first stage of the increase.

The statement is true.

Selling the subscription right opens the door instead of closing it. Selling the subscription right allows others to buy shares and become new shareholders. This is expressly considered an alternative to own purchase. It would prevent the holding and self-writing of the subscription right. The claim reverses the effect of the sale.

The statement is false.

title: Bonds as debt capital
context: Evaluate the following statements on financing of borrowings:
statements: Large companies have the opportunity to borrow from the issue of a bond.
Bonds are also called bonds, pensions or bonds and are securities that securitise a right to claim.
The bond ominal can be divided into smaller portions (splitting), so that many donors can make partial amounts available.
At the end of the term, a bond is usually not redeemed because bond capital is equity and remains in the company for an indefinite period.
Bondholders earn interest according to the interest rate and, if they sell before maturity, the difference between the purchase and the selling price.
tactical_explanations:
The issue of a single giant loan. Large companies can borrow from the issue of a bond because particularly large amounts are difficult to obtain as a loan from a bank. The Austrian state appears to be another major debtor alongside voestalpine AG. Denomination divides the nominal amount so that many creditors subscribe sub-assets. The bond is external financing with debt capital and right to claim, not a second share issue with share rights. Repayment at the end of the term remains the expectation. The statement makes possibility and type of capital.

The statement is true.

Debt securities, pensions or bonds are other words for bonds. They are securities that securitise a right to claim: the buyers have a claim against the issuer, a major debtor, on agreed terms of interest and maturity. This is the counterworld to the share with share rights. The sentence combines name and legal content.

The statement is true.

Denomination opens many donors. The bond ominal, the large amount required, is divided into smaller sub-assembly. Many different donors buy one or more parts. This makes it possible to finance what would be difficult to obtain as a single bank loan. voestalpine AG and the Austrian state serve as a theory of scale, not as a mandatory issuer of any GmbH. The statement describes the technical core of the denomination.

The statement is true.

The repayment is the normal case at the end. Usually, at the end of the term, the borrowed money is repaid at the nominal or fixed price; it is said that the bond is redeemed. Borrowing capital is debt capital, temporary, with repayment, non-permanent equity capital as share capital. Creditors expect repayment at the due date plus agreed interest. The rate makes the bond a share wrongly.

The statement is false.

Two sources of income, if not held to the end. Interest according to the interest rate and, if sold before maturity, the difference between the purchase and the selling price. Anyone who holds up to the date, receives redemption plus interest, not necessarily the same price gain. The price during the term follows supply and demand. The statement exactly mentions the two listed yields.

The statement is true.

title: Bond interest, Euribor and floaters
context: Evaluate the following statements on borrowing terms and at Euribor:
statements: The interest rate is one of the most important bond conditions and can be fixed, i.e. variable, or variable during the maturity.
In the case of variable interest rates, the interest rate is adjusted to the general interest rate level, for example to the Euribor.
Euribor means Euro Interbank Offered Rate and refers to average interest rates at which banks grant each other short-term investments in euro.
Variable-interest bonds are called floaters.
The price of a bond is never based on supply and demand, but solely on the nominal.
tactical_explanations:
Interest rate rule is at the heart of the terms. Interest rate, maturity and related agreements determine the terms on which the principal lends money. Interest rate may remain fixed or change over the term. Fixed means immutable, variable means adaptable to the general interest rate level, for example via Euribor; such papers are called floaters. Anyone who knows only one of the two forms as the bond, undermines the other and also confuses prices and nominals. The sentence represents the book alternative as the most important condition without the redemption at the end.

The statement is true.

Adjustment needs a reference. Variable means: the interest rate is adjusted to the general interest rate level, as example the presentation calls Euribor. If the reference interest rate level rises or falls, the bond rate moves along. This is true of creditors and issuers differently than a fixed coupon. The statement combines variable and sample index without forcing any contract on Euribor.

The statement is true.

Banks among themselves, euro, short term. Euribor is the Euro Interbank Offered Rate: average interest rates at which banks grant each other short-term investments in euro. There are different rates depending on the exact term. They serve as the base rate for financial transactions, including variable-interest bonds. The statement is the definition of the box, not a stock market wisdom outside the book.

The statement is true.

Floater is the name for the variable bond. Variable-interest bonds are called floaters; the Euribor can be its base rate. The nickname does not change the character: further debt capital, further repayment at the end, only the interest side swims with the market. Whoever thinks floater for shares, because the name sounds English, leaves the text. The statement equates the term and the facts.

The statement is true.

The price and nominal values are not the same. Bonds can be bought at issue or during the term; their price, the price, depends on supply and demand. The nominal value is the nominal amount at which usually is redeemed at the end, not the current market price. "Never supply and demand" contradicts the rate at which the bond price is redeemed. Anyone who knows only the nominal as price cannot think of intermediate sales and price difference.

The statement is false.

title: Equity, debt, internal and external
context: A Wiener Produktions GmbH combines contributions from the founders, retained profits, delivery liabilities, a bank loan and later a share issue after conversion into an AG. Evaluate the following statements:
statements: A bank loan is external financing with debt capital.
Self-financing through retained profits is internal financing and increases equity.
The in-kind contributions of the founders are debt capital because a van drives from the outside into the hall.
Delivery liabilities from the figures on target are short-term debt, not equity.
The resale of shares already issued between investors is the same external financing as the issue for the public limited company.
tactical_explanations:
Two grids, one credit. The bank is third, the source is outside: external financing. The capital must be repaid and usually interest paid, creditors without a typical say: debt capital. Both at the same time, not either or. The profits retained would be the counterpart in and of itself; contributions in kind by the founders remain their own, even if the van rolls through the gate; delivery liabilities are foreign in the short term. Only the issue feeds a new AG, not the later share trading. The statement correctly crosses the definitions of the most common example of bank credit.

The statement is true.

Turnover, retention, higher own base. The source is turnover, i.e. internal financing; the form is self-financing; the effect is more equity and more crisis resistance. No new creditors, no debt interest on this amount, buffer against loss years. Whoever reinterprets the same retention of profits as credit from customers slips into the outside-foreign corner, which does not provide for the theory. The rate holds origin and type of capital.

The statement is true.

Physically externally, the company is not financially external. In-kind contributions from the founders increase equity: vans and PCs count like money. External financing with equity would be conceivable if the contribution comes from shareholders, but never debt capital only because the vehicle rolls through the gate. Debt capital comes from third parties as a loan relationship. The confusion between the place of property and the quality of capital is the trap.

The statement is false.

Paying target creates creditors, not partners. Paying target means supplier financing and delivery liabilities: short-term debt capital, often without formal banking contract, with hidden interest over lost discount. Equity would be deposit or retained profit. Suppliers usually have no say in the management. The statement places the position in the foreign column and the short period.

The statement is true.

The issue is not the second market. Capital flows into the company's first sale, external financing with equity. Investors then exchange pieces; the AG does not receive any further financing effect, price gains remain with the sellers. The same booking as with the issue does not exist when the sale is made. The equation of both processes is the hardest classification trap in the section.

The statement is false.

title: How long are equity and debt available?
context: A company is financed by both shareholder deposits and bank loans. Evaluate the following statements about the maturity of equity and debt capital:
statements: Equity is usually available to the company for an indefinite period, while debt capital always has a fixed repayment period of not more than one year.
A 10-year bank loan is usually contrary to the rule that debt capital can be available in the short and long term.
Whether debt capital is available in the short or long term depends on the agreement between the parties, not on a single deadline.
Because equity is usually indefinite, it must still be fully repaid to donors at a certain end date.
A shareholder who can demand his deposit back at any time on request is in line with the rule that equity is tied in the long term.
tactical_explanations:
Equity is usually available for an indefinite period, which is true. Debt capital, however, can be agreed on both the short term and the long term, depending on the agreement between the creditor and the debtor - a bank loan over several years is just as much debt as a short term payment target. The claim that debt capital is always limited to a maximum of one year in a rigid limit that does not exist.

The statement is false.

Ten years remain debt capital. A bank loan with a long term does not contradict the rule that debt capital can be short- or long-term; it illustrates precisely the long-term variant. Investment loans with multi-annual deadlines are common. Only equity capital is generally considered indefinite. Long term does not change the assignment to debt capital.

The statement is false.

Neither weeks nor decades are required for debt capital; the decisive factor is what creditors and debtors agree on. Delivery liabilities run short, investment loans or bonds often over many years. This flexibility distinguishes debt capital from the usually indefinite equity bond.

The statement is true.

A repayment obligation at a fixed end date is precisely the characteristic of debt capital, not equity. Because equity does not have to be repaid, it is suitable for long-term investments; a duty to complete repayment would treat the deposit as a loan, which is usually contrary to the rule.

The statement is false.

A right to demand the deposit back at any time upon request is more like a short-term claim than a long-term tied deposit. The rule describes equity capital precisely because it is usually bound indefinitely and cannot be deducted on demand. A right to recover at any time would be the exception, not the rule.

The statement is false.

title: How are equity and debt providers paid?
context: The same company pays both profit shares to its shareholders and interest to its bank. Evaluate the following statements on the remuneration for equity and debt capital:
statements: Equity providers can receive profit shares, but do not necessarily depend on them every year as do creditors on their interest.
Anyone who repays a loan to the bank also pays back the debt capital itself, in addition to the interest.
A shareholder, similar to a bank, has a fixed interest claim, which must be paid independently of the company's annual result.
The obligation to repay the capital invested at the end of the term relates to debt, not to the contribution of the equity providers.
Because equity does not have to be remunerated, it is the more predictable and therefore less risky source of financing than a fixed interest-bearing loan for the company in bad years.
tactical_explanations:
Profit shares in equity providers are possible, but not necessarily due; if the profit is not, the distribution is usually also cancelled. Creditors, on the other hand, have an interest claim, which basically consists of independent of the business success. This difference makes equity no fixed loan obligation.

The statement is true.

Interest and capital are included. Interest is payable during the term of the loan and in the end the capital itself must be repaid. Anyone who only counts interest is undercut by the repayment of the loan amount. Both components form the repayment to the bank. Equity does not know this double obligation in this form.

The statement is true.

A fixed interest claim, independent of the annual result, is typical for creditors, not for equity providers. Shareholders receive profit shares if and to the extent that profit is generated; in loss years this claim is cancelled. The equalisation with a fixed loan interest transfers creditors logic to equity.

The statement is false.

Debt capital must be repaid at the end of the term; the deposit of the equity providers does not have to be paid. Equity remains permanently available to the company as long as it is not consumed by losses. The same obligation to pay back is a key difference between the parties.

The statement is true.

Without fixed interest burden, equity remains more flexible. In weak years, fixed credit rates burden liquidity more than a deposit without compulsory interest. Equity contributes losses without additional interest and repayment being due. That is why it is considered a risk buffer against a fixed interest loan. Planability here means lack of payment obligation, not higher return.

The statement is true.

title: Annual depreciation with straight-line allocation
context: A company buys property, plant and equipment for EUR 200 000 and plans ten years of service life, written down linearly. Rate the following statements about the annual depreciation:
statements: The annual depreciation is 200 000 euros divided by 10 years, i.e. 20 000 euros per year.
Because the residual book value decreases from year to year, the depreciation of the annual depreciation must also decrease from year to year.
After one year, the remaining book value is 200 000 minus 20 000, i.e. 180 000 euros.
After two years, the accumulated depreciation amounts to 20 000 euros, because only the first year counts.
Each year of use is again available as depreciation of the full purchase amount of 200 000 euros.
tactical_explanations:
Even over ten years. If the depreciation is linear, the purchase amount of 200 000 euros is evenly distributed over the useful life: 200 000 divided by 10 is 20 000 euros per year. This amount remains constant over the entire useful life. There is no rising or falling annual rate in this model. The division is the entire annual logic.

The statement is true.

Linear means constant annual amount, not falling annual depreciation. Although the residual book value decreases with each year, because the amounts already written off add up, the annual depreciation itself remains the same at 20 000 euros. A falling annual depreciation would require a different depreciation method.

The statement is false.

An annual amount reduces the initial value once. 200 000 minus 20 000 results in a residual book value of 180 000 Euro after the first year of use. The residual book value arises directly from this subtraction, without further assumptions. Nine annual amounts are still open. As long as linear and without residual value is worked, the invoice remains so simple and stable.

The statement is true.

Two years are two amounts. The cumulative depreciation after two years is 2 times 20 000 equal to 40 000 euros, not 20 000. Whoever counts only the first year ignores the second year of use, although the question explicitly mentions two years. Cumulated means sum of all previous annual amounts. A single year is not enough for this.

The statement is false.

The purchase price is distributed only once. Over ten years, a total of EUR 20 000 is available, not once every year again EUR 200 000. If you repeat the full purchase price annually, ten times the actual purchase price. Linear depreciation distributes the one amount, it does not multiply it. The annual depreciation remains EUR 20 000.

The statement is false.

title: Net book value after several years of use
context: The same acquisition of more than 200 000 Euro is written down linearly for ten years. Evaluate the following statements about the residual book value after several years of use:
statements: After five years, the remaining book value is half the purchase value, that is, 100 000 euros.
After five years, only EUR 20 000 are written off cumulatively, because only the last year's amount counts.
After five years, the remaining book value is only EUR 20 000, because only one annual amount would be left open.
After 10 years, the residual book value is zero if no residual value has been agreed and is written down linearly over the entire useful life.
The annual depreciation of 20 000 euros is actually paid from the bank account in each year of use.
tactical_explanations:
Half-life, half-book value. After five years of 10, 5 times 20 000 are written off equal to 100 000 euros; the remaining book value is 200 000 minus 100 000 equal to 100 000 euros. If linear distribution without residual value is equal to half the time exactly half of the purchase value. Symmetry is intended here.

The statement is true.

Cumulated means the sum of all years. After five years, 5 times 20 000 are written off equal to 100 000 euros, not only the last annual amount of 20 000. The claim counts a single year instead of all five. The residual book value drops accordingly to 100 000 euros. Those who take only the last amount, greatly underestimate the already distributed sum.

The statement is false.

Five years later, five years remain open. Remaining useful life 5 times 20 000 results in 100 000 Euro remaining book value, not 20 000. A residual book value of 20 000 would only be after nine years (200 000 minus 9 times 20 000). The statement confuses half of the useful life with the penultimate year. Five years are not nine.

The statement is false.

At the end of the useful life there is zero. After ten years the total purchase amount is distributed: 200 000 minus 10 times 20 000 equals 0 Euro. Without agreed residual value nothing remains in the investment. The linear distribution has then reached its goal. A positive residual book value would require an explicitly set residual value.

The statement is true.

Depreciation is an accounting expense, not an actual payment. The money for the purchase has already been paid out in the year of purchase; the annual 20 000 euros will only reduce the profit after that, without money flowing from the account again in these years. That is exactly the internal financing effect of the depreciation.

The statement is false.

title: Voice and repayment security for equity and debt
context: Evaluate the following statements who is in charge of equity and debt capital and who is guaranteed a guarantee for repayment:
statements: The degree to which equity investors can participate depends on the legal form of the company and is therefore not equally pronounced everywhere.
Creditors who lend to an enterprise usually have the same say in corporate governance as shareholders.
In principle, equity providers have a security similar to a secured bank loan to repay their deposit.
A credit may be secured for the creditor but does not have to; the security depends on whether the credit has been adequately secured.
Because creditors are usually better secured than shareholders, they also have more say in corporate governance.
tactical_explanations:
Legal form controls the voice. In a partnership, different rules of participation apply than in a GmbH or AG. Differently pronounced does not mean equally strong everywhere and not basically zero. Equity providers talk with, but the extent follows the form. Anyone who expects the same voice everywhere ignores this gradation.

The statement is true.

Credit does not give a shareholder vote. Creditors provide funds and demand interest and repayment, but usually do not sit in the place of the owners in the management of the company. Co-operation and lending are separate matters. Whoever assigns the same management rights to both, merges foreign and equity capital. The bank remains a creditor.

The statement is false.

Capital does not have to be repaid; therefore, there is no guarantee for the deposit in general, analogous to a secured bank loan. A security would only be useful if a repayment obligation were to be paid. The statement transfers debt-capital logic to own funds and is therefore wrong.

The statement is false.

The guarantee is compatible, not automatic. Whether a loan is secured for the creditor depends on mortgage, deposit or similar agreements. Without sufficient collateral, this security does not exist on its own. "If sufficiently secured, the condition makes clear. Debt capital can, but does not have to be secured.

The statement is true.

Creditor can have their repayment secured, but this does not give them an additional say in the management. This usually remains with the equity providers, graded according to legal form. Those who derive more management rights from better protection, link two independent characteristics without any justification.

The statement is false.

title: Financing features and depreciation checked together
context: A workshop finances new machines partly through shareholder deposits, partly through bank loans. The same machines cost 200 000 euros and are written down linearly over ten years.
statements: A bank loan is debt capital: it is interest-bearing, must be repaid and usually does not give the bank a say.
The shareholder contribution of the workshop is equity: bound indefinitely, without guarantee of repayment, with participation depending on the legal form.
The annual depreciation of the machinery will transform it into debt capital once more than half of its value is written off.
After one year, the remaining book value of the machines is EUR 180 000; the depreciation retained remains internal financing and no credit.
Since equity capital is available indefinitely, the annual depreciation of the machines must also amount to the full purchase price of 200 000 euros.
tactical_explanations:
Bank credit bears debt characteristics. It is interest-bearing, has to be paid back and usually does not give the bank a say. The bank remains a creditor, not a shareholder. Interest and redemption burden liquidity planably over the term. This combination distinguishes the loan from the shareholder contribution.

The statement is true.

The deposit bears capital features. It is usually bound indefinitely, without any guarantee for the repayment, with participation depending on the legal form. This is the opposite side to the bank loan. Losses can reduce the deposit without a repayment rate becomes due. The workshop thus permanently finances itself by means of owner funds.

The statement is true.

Depreciation does not change the method of financing. Whether machines have been purchased via deposit or credit, the financing decides at the time of purchase. The annual loss in value does not generate a new creditor and no obligation to pay repayment. Even if more than half is written off, equity remains equity and debt capital debt capital. The statement merges value consumption and capital origin.

The statement is false.

The remaining book value decreases, financing remains within. 200 000 minus 20 000 amounts to 180 000 euros after a year. The 20 000 euros are expense without payment; earned through the calculated prices, the money remains in the company first. This is internal financing through earned depreciation, not a loan agreement with a third party. Book value and source of financing are to be separated.

The statement is true.

The depreciation depends on the useful life: 200 000 divided by 10 is 20 000 euros per year, not 200 000 euros every year again. Whoever merges the maturity of the deposit and the pace of the depreciation, tenfold the purchase price. Both topics belong to different circuits.

The statement is false.

title: Earned depreciation as a financing source
context: The depreciation of a purchase of 200 000 euros over ten years is included in the calculated sales prices. Evaluate the following statements about the financing effect:
statements: The annual depreciation remains the same over the entire service life as long as it is written down linearly.
If the products are sold at the calculated prices, the depreciation is available to the company as an internal source of financing without any money flowing.
The financing effect of depreciation is created because it reduces profit as an expense, but does not trigger any payout in this step.
After two years of use, this one purchase already has 400 000 euros available as annual depreciation.
If the residual book value of an investment is reduced, the annual depreciation automatically doubles.
tactical_explanations:
Linear means constant annual amount. 200 000 divided by 10 is 20 000 euros, equal in each of the ten years of use. Only the residual book value decreases year after year; the annual depreciation itself remains unchanged. Degressive or performance-dependent models would be different distributions. Here the rate remains flat over the entire useful life.

The statement is true.

Depreciation earned remains in. If companies calculate depreciation in the selling prices and sell at these prices, they earn the amount via sales. At the same level, the money does not have to flow again and is available as an internal financing source. The prerequisite is the sale at the calculated prices. Without turnover, the financing effect is missing.

The statement is true.

Depreciation reduces the reported profit without money leaving the company in this booking step; the payment for the investment was already made in the year of purchase. This is the mechanism that explains the depreciation financing. Anyone who equates expenditure with immediate cash flow misses the time difference.

The statement is true.

Two years are 40 000, not 400 000. Cumulated is 2 times 20 000 euros. 400 000 would be 20 times the annual amount or twice the total purchase; both are not available. Anyone who confuses the annual amount and the acquisition value or multiplied by the year wrongly ends up with such fantasy sums.

The statement is false.

The residual book value and the depreciation of the annual depreciation do not develop in the same way as the linear depreciation: the residual book value decreases from year to year, the depreciation of the annual depreciation remains constant at 20 000 euros. A doubling of the annual amount would require another depreciation method which is not used here.

The statement is false.

title: Financing features and depreciation logic combined
context: Combine your knowledge to equity/foreign capital and to write down a linear depreciation of EUR 200 000 over ten years. Evaluate the following statements:
statements: After five years of linear depreciation, the residual book value is half the purchase value.
Since the machines are depreciated over ten years, a loan to finance these machines may only have a maximum duration of ten years.
After two years, the residual book value is 160 000 euros if a linear write-off is made over ten years.
Because equity investors have no repayment guarantee, they must recover their deposit at the latest at the end of the depreciation period of the investment.
The annual depreciation is earned without payment; after five years, half the book value, not five times the initial acquisition as cash inflow.
tactical_explanations:
Half-time is half book value. If a linear depreciation is over ten years, 5 times 20 000 are distributed after five years equal to 100 000 euros; the residual book value is 100 000 euros, i.e. half of 200 000. Symmetry applies until a residual value is agreed. Five out of ten years are exactly the middle of the useful life and thus also of the value.

The statement is true.

The useful life of an investment does not set a ceiling on the credit term with which it is financed. Debt capital can be short- or long-term, depending on the agreement, regardless of how many years the associated investment is written off. Both questions - depreciation period and credit term - are to be answered independently of each other.

The statement is false.

Two annual amounts reduce to 160 000. 200 000 minus 2 times 20 000 gives 160 000 Euro residual book value. This is between the value after one year (180 000) and after five years (100 000). The calculation follows the same linear logic without residual value. Who expects 160 000 has correctly deducted two years of use from the purchase value.

The statement is true.

In principle, equity does not have to be repaid, regardless of how long a investment financed by it will be used or written off. The lack of certainty of repayment is precisely the expression of this lack of obligation to repay, not a period linked to the period of depreciation.

The statement is false.

Five annual amounts are added, not five times the amount. Cumulated are 100 000 euros written off, the remaining book value drops to half. That is something else than a five-fold cash inflow of 1 000 000 euros, which is not available here. Depreciation remains expense without payment. Who multiplies annual amounts by the purchase price, invents an inflow.

The statement is true.

title: Areas of accounting
context: Evaluate the following statements on which questions the business accounting answers:
statements: The financial statement (financial planning, budgeting, cash flow) answers whether the company is managing its financial resources or whether it is in need of financing.
The accounting of the balance sheet and the profit and loss account will answer the assets of an entity, how this asset was financed and whether a profit or loss has been incurred in a period.
The main answer to whether the company is able to use its financial resources is the cost accounting.
The cost calculation asks how much the product or performance produced costs and how much the sales yield contributes to cost recovery.
Financial accounts, accounting and cost accounting all answer the same question, namely only those after the annual profit.
tactical_explanations:
Three questions, three areas. Does the company have its financial resources or does it need funding? This is exactly what the financial statement, i.e. financial planning, budgeting and cash flow, answers. Accounting takes on assets, financing and profit from periods, cost accounting, unit costs and cost recovery. The rate is the allocation of the book.

The statement is true.

Wealth and financing are side by side, the success of the period. What assets does the company have, how was it financed, and has it become richer or poorer in a certain period of time, meaning profit or loss? This is the accounting: preparation of the balance sheet and the profit and loss account. The financial account checks means of payment, not the asset structure. The cost account asks for product costs. The rate remains with the accounting question.

The statement is true.

Liquidity is not the question of costs. Whether the company is able to afford its financial resources or has financing needs is stated in the table in the financial statement. The cost calculation asks how expensive the product or service is and what the sale contributes to cost recovery. Anyone who assigns the cost-income question to the cost calculation exchanges the areas. A company can calculate cost-coveringly and still be insolvent when deposits and withdrawals fall apart in time. The table deliberately separates these questions. The assignment remains tabularly separate, it is not freely interchangeable.

The statement is false.

The amount of the product or service produced, and how much does the proceeds from the sale contribute to the cost recovery? This is the cost accounting. The financial account checks receipts and payments, the accounting assets and the profit for the period. The rate returns the third row of tables without deleting the other areas.

The statement is true.

A profit number does not replace three instruments. The table assigns the financial account to the financial and financing question, the accounting assets, financing and profit for the period, the cost accounting product costs and cost recovery. Anyone claiming all three areas answered only the annual profit, makes three questions one and cancels liquidity and calculation. The profit appears in the accounting, but does not replace either the financial plan or the cost statement.

The statement is false.

title: Solvency and insolvency
context: Evaluate the following statements on the solvency of businesses:
statements: An entity must be cashable at all times, i.e. liquid.
Ability to pay means that all the bills due can be paid for investments and ongoing expenses.
If liquidity is no longer available, the company is at risk and insolvency is imminent.
Unlike households, businesses do not need to be able to pay because they can wait for future profits at any time.
Financial plans, i.e. budgets, are drawn up to plan solvency.
tactical_explanations:
The same coercion is shared between the household and the business. Just as private households, a company must be able to pay at any time: liquid. It is not a matter of a one-off proof on the balance sheet date, but of the ability to meet due obligations whenever they arise. The rate is precisely the same as that requirement. Anyone who checks liquidity only on the balance sheet date fails to fulfil the current character of this obligation.

The statement is true.

Payable means not planned at some point. Payability means that all due invoices can be paid for investments and ongoing expenses. A machine on paper or an expected annual profit does not replace the transfer. The rate combines liquidity with concrete payments that are due now, that is, with what the financial statement controls. An invoice that is due only in months does not threaten today's liquidity; a one that is due now.

The statement is true.

The company is at risk of insolvency if it is no longer able to pay. The presentation links the lack of liquidity to a mere image problem, but to existence. Countermeasures and financial plans have this emergency in mind. The sentence gives the warning of the section.

The statement is true.

The section explicitly juxtaposes companies and households with the following: both must be liquid at all times. The claim that businesses could wait for future profits and therefore do not need ongoing solvency, strikes this parallel. Profit arises in the accounting of income and expenses, liquidity over deposits and withdrawals. Whoever only pushes for the later profit, nevertheless, due invoices cannot settle. Then the insolvency threatens, even if the G&V would later black write.

The statement is false.

Plan instead of hope. To plan the solvency, financial plans are drawn up, the presentation also calls budgets. Without comparing planned deposits and withdrawals, liquidity remains random. The rate hits the instrument with which the section prepares the solvency.

The statement is true.

title: Structure of a financial plan
context: Evaluate the following statements the financial plan of an undertaking:
statements: The basic principle of a company's financial plans is similar to that of households.
The financial plan compares planned payments with planned payments for a given period.
The financial plan compares the profit for the period with depreciation, not deposits and withdrawals.
If a deficit occurs, it means a financial requirement.
For example, a month is considered as the time period for this comparison.
tactical_explanations:
The same principle, different scales. Companies' financial plans are similar to households' basic principles: planned inflows and planned outflows are compared for a period of time. The sizes of hot deposits and withdrawals, the pattern remains close to the budget. Anyone who represents the corporate financial plan as a completely different logic contradicts this starting point. Size and legal form do not change the principle, they only change the amounts and the number of items.

The statement is true.

EZ vs. AZ, not profit against loss. Planned deposits are compared to planned withdrawals for a certain period of time to see whether a deposit surplus or a loss arises. The difference is a payment size. The accounting determines the profit differently. The sentence describes exactly this comparison. A deposit surplus and a deficit are the two possible signs of this difference.

The statement is true.

Profit and depreciation are not included in this comparison. The financial plan compares planned deposits with planned withdrawals. The profit for the period is generated in the accounting system, depreciation is just an example of an issue without payment. Whoever places profit and depreciation in the financial plan merges financial statement and income statement. Then a high profit would fake liquidity, although the money is not yet there, or a write-down would fake a payout that never goes off the account. A planned profit in the G&V will not say anything about the cashier of the next weeks without EZ and AZ.

The statement is false.

If the planned withdrawals exceed the planned deposits, a shortfall remains, and this means financial needs. The company must then obtain funds or postpone withdrawals. The sentence links the sign of the difference to the financing question, which is to answer the financial invoice.

The statement is true.

Month as an example, not as the only grid. The period can be, for example, one month. Week slices or longer horizons do not exclude the representation, but the monthly example shows that the plan should be periodic and concrete, not just an annual fiction. The sentence takes the example correctly.

The statement is true.

title: Cash inflow and cash outflow
context: Evaluate the following statements on deposits, withdrawals, revenue and expenditure:
statements: Most revenue also represents deposits, most expenditures also payouts.
Differences between the receipt and the deposit can occur in time if a receipt becomes a deposit later.
A difference in fact occurs when an issue does not involve a payment, for example, in the case of depreciation.
The receipt and deposit are always identical in the financial statement and the depreciation is considered to be a payment there.
In the context of the financial statement, the terms deposit and disbursement are more precise than revenue and expenditure.
tactical_explanations:
Mostly yes, always no. The presentation states that most income is also deposits and most expenditures are also withdrawals. This is the basic proximity of the pairs, not their complete equality. Exactly therefore the next sentence follows the exceptions. The sentence remains with this majority finding.

The statement is true.

The money is transferred by time. A receipt may already be received, but the corresponding deposit will only end up in the account later, for example when the payment is received later. Then the terms are given in time. The payment moment is counted for the financial statement, not the previous income card.

The statement is true.

Depreciation charges the result, not the account. An issue can be accompanied by amortization without payment, the example is the depreciation. The value consumption of an investment is recorded as expenditure or expense, no money is collected during this period. Anyone who treats depreciation as a transfer overestimates the liquidity outflow. The rate makes the factual difference. The machine loses value, the bank balance remains unaffected by this booking step.

The statement is true.

Identity would be the trap. The presentation explicitly says that differences occur in time or in fact, and calls the depreciation as an expenditure without payment. Therefore, income and deposit are not always identical, and the depreciation is not a payment. In the financial statement EZ and AZ would otherwise be blurred. A company could plan depreciation as a cash outflow and at the same time count a later incoming claim as already available money. Both distort the financial plan. Whoever equates the pairs plans depreciation as a transfer and considers later payment receipts already available money.

The statement is false.

Precision follows from the differences. Because income and expenditure do not always coincide with payments, payment and payment in connection with the financial statement are the more appropriate terms. The financial plan is intended to represent liquidity, not the success of the period. The sentence takes over this terminological decision of the section. Invoices are scheduled with deposits and withdrawals, not with the accounting profit.

The statement is true.

title: Cash surplus and reserves
context: Evaluate the following statements in case the deposits exceed the withdrawals:
statements: If the deposits exceed the withdrawals, the solvency is given.
If the surplus is very high, the total amount may be permanently invested in such a way that it is no longer available in the following months.
In the following periods, the payouts may be higher than the deposits, so that the surpluses will be needed again soon.
Financial reserves that can be accessed quickly are particularly important for unforeseen payments that are not included in the financial programming.
A deposit surplus in one month excludes that a financial requirement arises again later.
tactical_explanations:
The liquidity decides the sign. EZ minus AZ: if the difference is positive, the deposits exceed the withdrawals and the solvency is given. The representation does not link this constellation to the profit, but to the cash surplus. An example: EZ 80,000 Euro, AZ 65,000 Euro, surplus 15,000 Euro. The sentence holds the rule. If the deposits are below, the sign tilts, and the solvency is no longer given.

The statement is true.

If a surplus is very high, it should be considered whether a part is invested better than on the bank account. At the same time, the AZ can be higher in the following weeks or months, the surpluses are then used again. If you permanently bind the entire surplus in such a way that it is not available in subsequent months, exactly this warning is ignored. Liquidity this month is not a free loan for illiquidity in the next. A part can be invested, but only in such a way that quickly available funds remain for the next periods.

The statement is false.

The next month may tip. The section expressly warns that in subsequent periods the payouts may be higher and that the current surpluses will soon be needed again. A financial plan is a chain of discs, not a one-time warning. The sentence reflects this temporal caution.

The statement is true.

Unplanned payments need a quick buffer. Unplanned payments often do not appear in the financial plan and can suddenly burden liquidity. For this, financial reserves that can be accessed quickly, not only long-term fixed investments, are needed. The reserve protects the solvency between the planned deposits and payments. This is exactly the function that the statement calls.

The statement is true.

A month does not prove the year. A surplus in deposits shows that in this period EZ is above AZ. The next period can turn the sign, the presentation explicitly expects higher later AZ. Financial requirements can thus arise again. The absolute claim that a surplus excludes later needs contradicts the period logic of financial planning. Financial planning works in disks, each with its own sign of EZ minus AZ.

The statement is false.

title: Measures when there is a shortfall
context: Evaluate the following statements in case the withdrawals exceed the deposits:
