statements: If the withdrawals exceed the deposits, the solvency is at risk and the company must take immediate countermeasures.
Possible measures include reducing expenditure, agreeing with suppliers a longer payment target and granting their own customers only short payment targets.
Reducing stocks or borrowing from the bank in the short term may support solvency.
If insolvency is constantly threatened and it cannot be easily resolved, the inclusion of further shareholders with capital contributions can permanently improve liquidity.
If the withdrawals are above the deposits, it is sufficient to wait until the liquidity settles itself.
tactical_explanations:
Danger requires action. AZ over EZ means at risk of payment. The presentation requires immediate countermeasures, not a calm observation until the financial statements. Every further day with uncovered due invoices approaches insolvency. The sentence coupling signs and forced action correctly. If the management waits, due bills remain unpaid, and insolvency approaches.

The statement is true.

Payment targets are a liquidity lever. Reduce expenditures, extend supplier targets and shorten customer targets: Money is to be sent in later and earlier. These are operational steps that postpone deposits and withdrawals without changing the legal form. Together with expenditure reduction, they are among the typical measures for a deficit. The statement counts them correctly.

The statement is true.

Reducing the stock levels releases tied money, a short-term bank loan temporarily fills the gap. Both are in the list of measures. Neither does the stock replace the financial plan nor does the loan render the problem invisible, but both can support the immediate solvency.

The statement is true.

Repeating changes the means. If insolvency occurs again and again and is not easy to remedy, the presentation of capital contributions from new shareholders as a way to permanently improve and secure liquidity. This is equity, not just a short loan. The rate hits this escalation stage. This is external equity, not just another short-term loan that would put a strain on the next rate.

The statement is true.

The section says that solvency is at risk, the company must act immediately. Anyone who waits, leaves due bills unpaid. Insolvency threatens precisely when liquidity is lacking. The hope of self-healing contradicts the explicitly demanded intervention. The presentation requires immediate countermeasures: reducing expenditure, turning payment targets, reducing stocks or borrowing, if necessary new capital contributions. Waiting is not on this list. Without such steps, the difference AZ minus EZ remains uncovered.

The statement is false.

title: Financial plan at start-up
context: Evaluate the following statements on financial planning of business founders:
statements: The creation of the company requires relatively high payouts, while most of the deposits and experience for future deposits are not yet available.
This is why founders often have to submit a financial plan when they apply for funding.
This financial plan should be carefully and realistically planned so that investors can be convinced.
Founders can calculate deposits as safely as established companies with long payment lines.
The financial account has a great economic importance, among other things because insolvency threatens without solvency.
tactical_explanations:
The first withdrawals, deposits later. The foundation is characterized by comparatively high withdrawals, deposits are usually still missing, and experience of how much deposits can be calculated is missing. The financial plan is therefore on uncertain ground and is still indispensable. The sentence describes precisely this sluggishness. This is why the financial plan is more difficult to establish than in the current operation with known payment series.

The statement is true.

Capital wants to see the plan. Because the founding situation is so uncertain, founders often have to submit a financial plan when they apply for funding. The plan is the instrument by which the solvency towards investors is argued. The sentence follows requests and plans as the presentation does.

The statement is true.

The plan should be careful and realistic so that investors are convinced. Too high deposits destroy credibility and lead later into the liquidity gap. The rate sets the quality standard that the section places on the founding financial plan.

The statement is true.

Experience values are missing. The presentation emphasizes that most of the deposits are not yet available and no experience values, with how much deposits can be calculated. Established enterprises can continue series, foundations not to the same extent. The claim of equal security strikes the very problem of the founding of the financial plan, for which the financial plan is so difficult and so important. Whoever claims the same security as in established companies, strikes the reason why investors demand a cautious plan. The financial plan replaces missing time series with cautious assumptions, not false certainty.

The statement is false.

Without cash, no continuity. The financial account has great economic importance, because solvency must be guaranteed at all times and its absence can lead to insolvency. Foundation, ongoing operation and capital raising depend on it. The sentence grasps this importance without replacing the accounting. The same question is connected with the establishment, operation and financing applications whether or not EZs cover the credit institutions due.

The statement is true.

title: Cash flow and solvency
context: Evaluate the following statements on cash flow in the financial statement:
statements: Cash flow is determined by comparing deposits and withdrawals within a given period.
If the deposits exceed the withdrawals during this period, cash flow is positive, so there is a cash inflow to the company.
Positive cash flow is an indicator of solvency.
This is of great importance, among other things, for investments and for credit repayments.
Negative cash flow always means that a loss is reported in the profit and loss account.
tactical_explanations:
Cash flow is a payment difference. Deposits and withdrawals of a given period are compared. This follows the same logic as in the financial plan, now designated as a key figure. Profit on income and expenses is another method of calculation. Anyone who confuses cash flow with profit merges payment and success levels.

The statement is true.

The plus sign is inflow. EZ greater than AZ results in positive cash flow, i.e. cash or cash inflow to the company. For example: EZ 120,000 Euro, AZ 95,000 Euro, cash flow +25,000 Euro. The sign describes the cash movement, not automatically the success of the period. The sentence meets the definition. The sign describes the cash movement of the period, not automatically the success of the period of the G&V.

The statement is true.

The positive cash flow shows that more money has flowed into the period than outflows, and is therefore considered to be an indicator of solvency. The later section adds that profit without liquidity and liquidity can be achieved without profit. However, the positive cash flow remains valid as an indicator in the financial statement. A later section adds that profit without liquidity and liquidity without profit is possible; as an indicator in the financial statement, positive cash flow remains valid nonetheless.

The statement is true.

Investments and credit repayments are disbursements. They cannot be made without cash inflow or existing liquidity. The presentation highlights the importance of positive cash flow precisely for these two purposes. The sentence follows this link.

The statement is true.

Two invoices, two results. Cash flow compares cash flows and withdrawals, the G&V proceeds and expenses. Depreciation reduces profit without being disbursed; receivables can be income without being already deposit. Therefore, cash flow can be negative and the G&V can still be in the plus, or vice versa. The claim that negative cash flow is always a reported loss, merges financial statement and income statement. Claims can be income without deposit, depreciation and amortization expenses without disbursement. Therefore, one cannot conclude from the sign of cash flow on profit or loss.

The statement is false.

title: Bookkeeping as external accounting
context: Evaluate the following statements on accounting and its addressees:
statements: Each company is legally obliged to determine its profit or loss for each financial year.
This is not least important for the calculation of income taxes, which, depending on the legal form, must be paid to the entrepreneur or to the enterprise.
Accounting is also called external accounting because it has an information and documentation function externally.
Only tax authorities have an interest in the success of the period; management, investors and employees remain uninvolved.
The management must decide whether the profit is taken or distributed or left in the company, for example to invest in machinery or other equipment.
tactical_explanations:
Compulsory, not free of charge. Every company must determine profit or loss for each financial year. This is a legal obligation, regardless of whether an internal cost accounting is already running. The rate reflects this obligation before EAR or double accounting is differentiated. The choice between EAR and double accounting will later only change the procedure, not the annual obligation to investigate.

The statement is true.

Tax follows the result. The determination is not least used for the calculation of income taxes. Depending on the legal form, the person or the company pays. Without a profit for the period, the tax base is missing. The rate holds this tax reason without denying other addressees. Liquidity in the financial statement does not replace this tax base.

The statement is true.

Information and documentation to the outside world. Because accounting serves addressees outside the company, it is also called external accounting. The cost accounting is later compared to internal accounting. External impact and naming are related: balance sheet and G&V are aimed at creditors, owners and authorities. The statement is precisely this external function.

The statement is true.

Many stakeholders, not just the tax office. The presentation, in addition to the tax office, mentions the management, investors, shareholders (e.g. shareholders), business partners (e.g. suppliers) and employees. Those who only let the authority apply, exactly this list is deleted. The management needs the result for the assessment of how successfully managed, investors for their investment, suppliers for the creditworthiness of the business relationship.

The statement is false.

The profit is the result of the use question: withdrawal or distribution or retention in the company, for example for machines and other assets. Leave strengthens internal financing and equity. The management weighs liquidity requirements and investment goals. The statement describes exactly this choice.

The statement is true.

title: Single-entry and double-entry bookkeeping
context: Evaluate the following statements on revenue and expenditure account and on double accounting:
statements: The revenue and expenditure account compares the revenue of a financial year with expenditure; the expenditure is essentially the same as the disbursements, but also includes depreciation.

In case of double accounting, the balance sheet and profit and loss account are drawn up; the profit is determined in the G&V and must also be based on the comparison of equity at the beginning and at the end of the financial year.
Individual companies and partnerships whose turnover is less than 700,000 euros per financial year can create an EAR.
If they exceed this turnover limit or if a capital company is present, double accounting must be carried out.
Every GmbH may, regardless of size and turnover, only carry a revenue-expense invoice.
tactical_explanations:
EAR mixes payments and depreciation. Revenues of a financial year are in contrast to expenditures. Expenditures are essentially the same as payments, but also include depreciation. Thus, the EAR is closer to money than the G&V, but not purely payment-related. The rate represents exactly this construction. The EAR is closer to the money than the G&V, but not purely payment-related, because the depreciation is still included.

The statement is true.

The profit is in the G&V and at the same time as the change in equity between the beginning and the end of the financial year. Both must be the same amount, hence double profit determination and the name double accounting. The rate holds both ways. If the two paths differ, the double investigation is not fulfilled.

The statement is true.

Limit of 700,000 euros turnover. Individual companies and partnerships below this threshold per financial year may choose the less expensive EAR. This is a can rule, no obligation to EAR. Capital companies are not yet standing here. The rate hits the threshold and the addressee circle.

The statement is true.

The threshold or legal form tilts the system. If Entrepreneurs exceed the turnover limit of 700,000 euros or if a capital company is present, double accounting must be carried out. A GmbH therefore falls under the obligation, regardless of whether someone would find the EAR more comfortable. Both triggers stand alternatively side by side. The statement connects them correctly.

The statement is true.

The description says that if a capital company is present, a double accounting must be conducted. The GmbH is a capital company. A permanent restriction to the EAR regardless of size and turnover contradicts this obligation. Only certain individual companies and partnerships under 700,000 Euro may choose to make use of the EAR. In addition, public limited companies and large companies must publish the annual financial statements. Only certain individual companies and partnerships under 700,000 Euro may choose to make use of the EAR. Stock companies and large GmbHs must publish the annual financial statements in addition.

The statement is false.

title: Assets, liabilities and the balance sheet equation
context: Evaluate the following statements on the structure of the balance sheet:
statements: The assets show the assets, for example, land, buildings, machinery and supplies.
The liabilities show how this property has been financed, with its own resources or with external resources.
The sum of assets is equal to capital, i.e. the sum of assets equal to the sum of liabilities, because each part of the assets must have been financed.
The assets are on the debit side of the balance sheet, the liabilities on the credit side.
The liabilities are on the target side because they show what funds have been used for.
tactical_explanations:
Assets are assets. Land, buildings, machinery, inventories and similar items are on the asset side. They answer the assets of the company. Financing is on the other side. The rate remains on the asset side. Financing is on the liability side, not on the asset list.

The statement is true.

The source of the liability is explained by the source. Own funds are equity, foreign funds are debt capital. Together they show how the assets on the asset side were financed. Without this side the asset side would remain uncovered. The financing question of the balance sheet is precisely: Who owns the capital that carries the assets? Thus the liability side answers the source question of the balance sheet.

The statement is true.

Equality is mandatory. Assets equal to capital, total assets equal to total liabilities, because each asset must be financed. An asset position without a liability counterpart would not exist in this logic. Total assets and total capital are also called balance sheet totals. The rate represents the identity. An asset position without a passive counterpart would not exist in this logic; total assets and capital are therefore also called balance sheet total.

The statement is true.

The balance sheet is to be left, the right is to have assets. Assets are to be on the target side of the balance sheet, liabilities on the have side; both sides must be equal. The difference between assets and debt capital is equity. Interchanged sides would destroy the equality of purpose and possession.

The statement is true.

The purpose is to use, have origin. In the accounting the target page usually shows what funds have been used for, therefore the total assets are there. The credit page shows where the funds come from, therefore the capital is there. To put liabilities on the target page, money use and the source of funds are reversed. The same logic applies to individual business cases: Should use, Have origin. The same set-to-hold logic applies to individual business cases: Should show the use, Have the origin of the funds. Whoever places the liabilities to the left, distorts origin and use.

The statement is false.

title: Equity and period profit
context: Evaluate the following statements on equity, debt and for comparison of two balance sheets:
statements: If the assets exceed the debt capital, the positive difference is equity, i.e. that part of the assets that has not been financed with debt.
When comparing the balance sheets of two dates, an increase in equity means a profit.
A decrease in equity between two dates means a loss.
The balance sheet is compared at a certain time, usually at the end of a financial year.
A rise in the debt capital between two reference days is already considered to be profit in itself.
tactical_explanations:
Capital is residual. Assets minus debt, i.e. debt, gives the positive difference in equity: the part of the assets that is not financed by debt. If there is more assets than debt, the company is richer in its own funds in this sense. The rate represents exactly this difference.

The statement is true.

Two key dates, a message of success. If equity increases from one balance sheet point to the next, this means one profit. This is the same profit that G&V shows only in terms of capital comparison. Extractions can overlay the picture, the section still links the rise to the profit. The rate follows this rule. The withdrawals may reduce equity, while the section links the rise between two reference days to profit.

The statement is true.

If the equity is lost between two dates, the company has become poorer. The G&V and the equity comparison must bear the same loss message. An increase would be profit; a decrease is the loss side. The statement holds exactly this period logic. Profit would be the increase; loss is the decrease of the same size.

The statement is true.

Balance sheet is a photo of the closing date. Assets and capital are compared at a certain point in time, usually at the end of a financial year. G&V and financial plan work over periods; the balance sheet photographs the closing date. Anyone reading balance sheet as a period account mixes three instruments.

The statement is true.

More debt is not a profit. Profit is the increase in equity or the surplus of income over the expenses. Debt capital is debt. If the company receives additional loans, the debt capital and often also the assets rise, without the result already a profit follows. Whoever equates FK-anstieg with profit confuses the middle-income with the profit. If the company receives additional loans, assets and debt capital often rise together without a profit. The source of funds is not a success for the period.

The statement is false.

title: FunBike: assets and current-asset intensity
context: The simplified balance sheet of FunBike GmbH as per 31.12.20xx (amounts in euros) shows on the asset page plots and buildings 750,000, technical assets and business equipment 2,330.000, financial assets 240,000, inventories 5,400,000, receivables from deliveries and services 598,000 as well as bank balances and cash stock 320,250. The liability side includes cash deposits of the shareholders 525,000, profit 3,614,250, provisions 2,000,000, bank loans 3,199,000 and liabilities from deliveries and services 300,000. Total assets and capital are 9,638,250 each. Evaluate the following statements on this balance sheet:
statements: Total assets and capital are called balance sheet totals and amount to EUR 9,638,250 each.
The assets of FunBike GmbH exceed four million euros.
The current assets amount to 6,318,250 euros, and in it the stocks dominate with 5,400,000 euros.
The company is in circulation because it has significantly more current assets than fixed assets.
Bank balances and cash stocks exceed the stocks.
tactical_explanations:
Both sides have the same total. Total assets or total capital are called balance sheet total. Addition of assets: 750,000 + 2,330.000 + 240,000 + 5,400,000 + 598.000 + 320.250 = 9,638,250. Liabilities: 525,000 + 3,614.250 + 2,000,000 + 3,199,000 + 300,000 = 9,638,250. The identity of assets holds capital. The rate applies to the term and amount. The identity of assets equal to capital holds because each asset position must be financed.

The statement is true.

Investment assets remain below four million. Assets are assets that are to remain for more than one year: plots and buildings 750,000 plus technical assets and business equipment 2,330.000 plus financial assets 240,000. 750,000 + 2,330.000 = 3,080.000, plus 240,000 = 3,320.000 euros. Four million would be 4,000,000. 3,320.000 is below. The presentation later speaks of a little more than three million euros of long-term assets, which is the sum of this. The claim that the fixed assets exceed four million is therefore wrong. The presentation later speaks of a little more than three million euros of long-term assets, which corresponds to 3,320,000 euros, not more than four million.

The statement is false.

Current assets. Stocks 5,400,000 plus receivables 598,000 plus bank balances and cash stock 320,250, 5,400,000 + 598,000 = 5,998,000, plus 320,250 = 6,318,250 euros. Stocks alone are 5,400,000 and thus the clearly largest block. The presentation makes this plausible for a bicycle manufacturer. The rate meets total and dominance. The presentation calls high stocks plausible for a bicycle manufacturer, because parts and finished wheels can be in stock.

The statement is true.

Current assets are clearly above fixed assets. FunBike has 6 318 250 euros of current assets against 3 320 000 euros of fixed assets. This makes the company in circulation intensive: the short-term fixed values dominate. Especially the stocks drive this structure. The classification follows the size comparison of the two asset blocks.

The statement is true.

Cash against stock: the stock wins. Bank balances and cash stock are 320 250 euros, stocks are 5 400 000 euros. 320 250 is far smaller, not larger. The claim reverses the ratio. Precisely because the stocks weigh so heavily, the question of stock reduction arises. The statement is numerically wrong. The stocks dominate the asset side clearly opposite the cash register.

The statement is false.

title: FunBike: capital structure and golden balance sheet rule
context: The simplified balance sheet of FunBike GmbH as per 31.12.20xx (amounts in euros) shows cash deposits of the shareholders 525,000, profit 3.614,250, provisions 2,000,000, bank loans 3,199,000 and liabilities from deliveries and services 300,000. The balance sheet total amounts to 9.638,250 euros, the fixed assets 3.320,000 euros.
statements: The equity amount is 4.139,250 euros.
Some 57 percent of the capital is debt capital, most of which is bank loans.
Such a capital structure with a high dependence on debt is not atypical for Austrian small and medium-sized enterprises.

The golden balance sheet rule is fulfilled because the long-term assets of just over three million euros are covered by equity capital of over four million euros and probably also by long-term debt capital.
Equity is below three million euros and is therefore not sufficient to finance fixed assets in the long term.
tactical_explanations:
Add equity. Cash deposits 525,000 plus profit 3.614,250. 525,000 + 3.614,250 = 4.139,250 euros. This is the part of the liabilities that is not debt capital. Sample: Debt 2,000,000 + 3,199,000 + 300,000 = 5,499,000, plus 4,139.250 = 9,638,250, the balance sheet total. The rate applies to the amount.

The statement is true.

Debt ratio. Debt capital 5,499,000 divided by balance sheet total 9,638,250, 5,499,000 / 9,638,250 ᐅ 0,5705, i.e. around 57 percent. Including bank loans 3,199,000, the largest FK block before provisions 2,000,000 and liabilities 300,000. The figure exactly mentions these around 57 percent and the bank loans as a large part. The rate is in line with the invoice. 3,199,000 at 5,499,000 confirms that bank loans bear the bulk of the debt, before provisions and supplier liabilities.

The statement is true.

The section still assigns FunBike to small companies with a balance sheet total of just under 10 million euros and considers high debt dependency to be typical for Austrian SMEs. Thus, the observed structure is expected, not a special case. However, the high profit will strengthen equity and internal financing if it remains in the company. The high profit will strengthen equity and internal financing power if it remains in the company and is not fully distributed.

The statement is true.

The golden balance sheet rule requires long-term assets to be financed in the long term. Assets 3.320,000, slightly more than three million. Equity 4.139,250, i.e. more than four million, and part of the debt capital will probably be long-term. 4.139,250 already covers 3.320,000 alone. The rule is fulfilled. The rate reflects this audit. 4.139,250 Euro equity already covers 3.320,000 Euro fixed assets alone; the rule is fulfilled, not violated. If the equity is smaller than the long-term assets and lacked long-term debt capital, the rule would be violated.

The statement is true.

Four million, not less than three. Equity 4.139,250 is over four million, not less than three. Assets 3.320,000 is smaller than this equity. The claim underestimates equity and falsely explains that it is not sufficient for long-term financing. The exact opposite is supported by the golden balance sheet rule.

The statement is false.

title: Income statement of FunBike GmbH
context: In the G&V, the expenses are deducted from revenues and other revenues. The profit and loss account of FunBike GmbH as at 31.12.20xx shows sales revenues of 70,656,000 euros, material expenses 53,175,000 euros, personnel expenses 7,900,000 euros, depreciation and amortization 1,800,000 euros, other operating expenses 2,875,000 euros, interest income 12,000 euros, interest expense 99,000 euros, taxes 1,204,750 euros and annual result 3,614,250 euros. Evaluate the following statements:
statements: If the sum of proceeds and revenues exceeds the expenses, a profit is achieved.
The G&V's expenses include wages and salaries, material costs, rent, insurance costs, energy costs, depreciation of tangible assets and the creation of provisions.
The annual result of FunBike GmbH amounts to EUR 3,614,250 and corresponds to the profit shown in the balance sheet.
The depreciation of 1,800,000 euros increases the profit in the G&V because they are not a payout.
The same profit can also be determined by comparing equity at the beginning and end of the financial year; both must be consistent, so it is called double profit determination.
tactical_explanations:
Income over expense is profit. In the G&V, the expenses are deducted from revenue and other income. If a positive remainder remains, the company has become richer in the period. Conversely, a loss arises. The sentence returns this sign rule, even without the FunBike numbers.

The statement is true.

List of expenses of the section. Wages and salaries, material, rent, insurance, energy, depreciation of property, equipment, such as machinery, provisioning: all this is one of the expenses. FunBike shows material, personnel, depreciation and other operating expenses as concrete blocks. The sentence remains with the term list, not with a single position.

The statement is true.

Revenues 70,656,000 minus material 53,175,000 = 17,481,000. Minus personnel 7,900.000 = 9,581.000. Minus depreciation 1,800,000 = 7,781,000. Minus other operating expenses 2,875,000 = 4,906,000, EBIT. Interest income 12,000 minus interest expense 99,000 = financial result -87.000. 4,906,000 - 87,000 = 4,819,000 before tax. Minus taxes 1,204,750 = 3.614,250 annual result. The same amount is shown in the balance sheet as profit. The rate meets the number and bridge to the balance sheet.

The statement is true.

Depreciation reduces, it does not increase. After deduction of material and personnel, there are 9.581.000 euros. Depreciation of 1.800.000 euros is expense and is deducted: 9.581.000 minus 1.800.000 = 7.781.000. Without this deduction, the interim result would be 1.800.000 euros higher, the later profit would be likewise. The fact that depreciation is not a payment is part of the financial statement and in the distinction between cash flow and profit. In the G&V it remains an expense with minus sign. The claim that it increases the profit, this sign reverses.

The statement is false.

Two ways, one number. Profit increases equity and can be determined from the comparison of current equity with that at the beginning of the financial year. G&V and equity comparison must show the same profit, therefore double profit determination and in this context double accounting. FunBike shows 3.614,250 in both roles, as annual result and as profit in the balance sheet. The sentence meets the classification.

The statement is true.

title: Cash flow statement and profit
context: Evaluate the following statements the cash flow statement and its relationship to profit:
statements: Cash flow is not identical to profit, because you can achieve profit without having liquid funds, and you can be liquid without earning profit.
In the cash flow account, the operating activity division is the most important because it concerns the core of the business and shows whether there are any surplus payments.
New bank loans and the purchase of machinery are both allocated to the operating activity division in the cash flow statement.
In the investment sector, means of payment are used to acquire fixed assets, while the sale of fixed assets can generate means of payment.
Cash flow and profit are the same as each depreciation is a payout and every turnover is a deposit at the same time.
tactical_explanations:
Two truths side by side. Published financial statements include a cash flow statement and cash flow statement in addition to balance sheet and G&V. Cash flow measures solvency, profit is the result of the period. Profits without cash, such as high claims and depreciation, and cash without profit, such as after a loan. The sentence holds exactly this non-identity.

The statement is true.

Operations first. The area of operating activity, including operations or operating activities, affects the core of the business. Investors often look here mainly because it shows whether the core generates overpayments. Financing and investment explain other causes of inflows and outflows. The rate meets this ranking.

The statement is true.

Three pots, not one. New loans are inflows of financing, the purchase of machinery is part of the investment because cash flows flow into long-term fixed assets. Operating activity shows the core of the ongoing business, not the acquisition of debt capital and not the asset purchase. Those who allocate both of these to the operating activity make the combined cash flow account a single residual size and take the information that the presentation attaches importance to exactly the investors. Financing takes up shareholders and loans, investment buys or sells fixed assets. Only the operating activity measures the core.

The statement is false.

Investment is investment purchase and sale. If money flows into the acquisition of long-term investments, for example in fixed assets, this is a drain in the investment area. The sale of a property or building can generate payment methods there in reverse. This is not operating activity and not merely borrowing. The rate reflects both directions.

The statement is true.

Depreciation separates the two figures. In the financial statement, depreciation is the example of an issue without payment. In the G&V it reduces the profit, from the account does not receive any money. Revenues can be income as receivables before the deposit comes. Therefore cash flow and profit are not the same measure. The claim that each depreciation is a withdrawal and each turnover deposit, removes exactly the differences for which the presentation puts both invoices side by side. Precisely for these differences, G&V and cash flow bill stand side by side and cannot be drawn together to a number.

The statement is false.

title: Purpose of cost accounting
context: Evaluate the following statements on the cost account:
statements: The cost calculation is intended to show how much a product or service produced costs.
An enterprise may exist in the long term, even if the costs are not covered by the income.
Each company must have a cost accounting.
The cost accounting is considered to be internal accounting because it is only used internally.
Small companies carry out a cost calculation particularly frequently and reliably.
tactical_explanations:
Unit costs are the entry into the control system. The cost calculation is based on two questions: How much does the product produced in the company cost or the performance generated, and how much does the sales yield contribute to cost recovery. Without this calculation, it remains unclear whether a bicycle or service justifies the consumption of machinery, work and materials. Precisely for this reason, a company must know its costs, not only the profit from accounting. The task is internal and business-economic, not just a mandatory exercise for the company book. If you only know the annual profit, you do not know whether the individual wheel bears the costs. The cost calculation supplements the accounting with this view of piece and performance.

The statement is true.

Without income coverage, no company can hold out permanently. In the long term, no company can exist if the costs are not covered by the income. A single year with loss may be bridgeable, a permanent undercover consumes substance and solvency. The sentence claims the opposite and removes the condition of existence that precedes the theory of cost accounting. Whoever ignores costs because somewhere else sales are visible, confuses movement with cost recovery.

The statement is false.

No law forces cost accounting. It is not mandatory by law, in contrast to profit determination in accounting. Business economics is advantageous as a control and control tool, but that does not make it obligatory. Anyone who derives a legal obligation from the benefit mixes internal and external accounting. Small businesses often leave them away, although they would be useful; this shows that there is no compulsion.

The statement is false.

Internally, the figures remain in the house. The cost accounting is called internal accounting because it is only used internally. It serves as a control and control tool for the management, not for publication to the tax authority or company book. The investors see the annual financial statements, not necessarily the unit calculation. This is precisely the delimitation to the external accounting system of the accounting system.

The statement is true.

Small businesses often do not run them. It is clear that cost calculations, especially in small businesses, often do not take place, although they would be economically advantageous. The claim that they are conducted there particularly frequently and reliably, reverses this observation. Size and obligation are different here: lack of legal obligation and scarce capacity explain the gap, not special care.

The statement is false.

title: Internal and external accounting
context: A bicycle manufacturer in Graz carries out accounting and cost accounting. Evaluate the following statements:
statements: Accounting is called external accounting because it has an information and documentation function externally.
Investors, shareholders and suppliers are interested in profit or loss for the financial year.
The cost statement must be of the same legal structure as the balance sheet and profit and loss account.
As a control and control tool, cost accounting is economically advantageous.
Owners receive the cost statement in the same form as the published annual accounts.
tactical_explanations:
The external documentation of accounting is not the calculation. Every company must determine profit or loss for the financial year, not least because of income taxes. Therefore, accounting is called external accounting: it informs and documents about tax authorities, investors, shareholders, business partners and employees. The Graz-based manufacturer thus accounts for wealth and success, regardless of how detailed it is calculated internally.

The statement is true.

Many stakeholders read the same success. Whether profit or loss has been achieved is not only of interest to the tax authority, but also to the management of the company, to investors, to shareholders, to business partners, for example, suppliers and employees. The annual financial statements answer whether the company has become richer or poorer in the period. This is precisely the interest behind the external documentation function. The cost accounting does not replace this view, it complements it internally. Without this external report, investors and the tax authority lacked the common basis for figures. Internal piece calculations do not replace this documentation requirement and may be cut differently.

The statement is true.

No legal corset for the internal invoice. The cost statement is not mandatory by law and only used internally. It does not therefore have the same structure as balance sheet and G&V. The management can structure fixed costs, variable costs and cover contributions as it needs decisions. Those who require the same internal structure of obligations as in the annual accounts transfer external accounting rules to an instrument that explicitly calls theory internal and voluntary.

The statement is false.

Taxes and control requires costs, not just annual profit. Business management is advantageous to manage a cost accounting as a control and control tool. Unit costs, additional orders and break-even cannot be seen from the G&V alone. The manufacturer decides on prices and acceptance of orders with these internal sizes. The sentence is of exactly this benefit without claiming a legal obligation.

The statement is true.

Owners are among the stakeholders in accounting; published financial statements include balance sheet, G&V and often a cash flow statement. The cost statement remains internal and is not legally binding. The theory does not invent legal equality with the published annual financial statements. Internal reports can be more frequent and different, they do not replace the external financial statements.

The statement is false.

title: Costs and expenses
context: Evaluate the following statements the ratio of costs and expenses:
statements: The costs are largely the same as the costs in accounting in most cases.
Additional costs that are not included in the accounting are possible, such as the entrepreneur's wage.
The entrepreneur's wage of an individual entrepreneur is always a burden in accounting.
The employer's wage can be based on opportunity costs, i.e. on income that can be obtained elsewhere.
Costs are the same as payments in the financial statement.
tactical_explanations:
In most cases, costs are largely the same as the costs in accounting. Wages, materials, rent and energy appear in both circuits. Nevertheless, differences remain possible. The sentence describes the proximity without claiming identity. Those who think of costs and expenses as completely separate worlds overtake the distinction; those who think they are always identical, undermine the next point of the definition. Material, wages and energy therefore often appear in both circuits, while the entrepreneur's wage makes the gap visible. Anyone who covers the proximity to identity can no longer represent additional costs in the control system.

The statement is true.

Additional costs are included in the accounting. Additional costs that are not included in the accounting are possible, for example the entrepreneur's wage for individual entrepreneurs or OG-partners as well as complementary ones. This is the earnings they expect for their work. Internally, it belongs to the cost calculation so that the service does not appear free of charge. This gap between internal consumption and external expenditure is precisely mentioned.

The statement is true.

The employer's wage is an example of additional costs that are not included in the accounting. Individual entrepreneurs and personally liable partners often derive profit without recording a salary as an employee. The sentence "always as expense" makes an internal calculation size a mandatory item of accounting and is wrong.

The statement is false.

The yardstick is to earn elsewhere. The employer's wage can be based on the opportunity costs, i.e. on the income that entrepreneurs could earn if they were pursuing another professional activity. Internally, it becomes apparent whether the self-employed work covers at least the missed salary. This is not a payment to third parties, but a measure of evaluation. The sentence is precisely this orientation.

The statement is true.

Consumption is not the same as cash outflow. Costs are the value-based consumption of performance factors in production or performance creation. Disbursements belong to the financial statement and concern liquidity. Depreciation is expense and often costs without being a payout in the period; the entrepreneur's wage can be cost without accounting expense. Who equates costs with disbursements, mixes cost accounting and financial account.

The statement is false.

title: The concept of costs
context: Evaluate the following statements What are the costs?:
statements: Costs are the value-added consumption of performance factors in production or production of performance.
The performance factors include, for example, machines, work and materials.
There are never differences between costs and expenses.
Fixed costs are incurred regardless of the quantity produced or produced.
Variable costs usually decrease as production volume increases.
tactical_explanations:
Consumption with value-based approach, not just counting pieces. Costs are the value-based consumption of performance factors in the production or performance of a company. Machine hours, work and materials are valued in money as soon as they enter the performance. Without this term, it remains unclear what the cost calculation measures at all. The sentence reflects the definition of the section, not a colloquial equation with invoices to suppliers. Without monetary value, only a technical quantity list would remain, which cannot be calculated with prices and cover contributions. This very assessment makes consumption a cost size of the cost calculation.

The statement is true.

Three examples make consumption tangible. Performance factors are, for example, machines, work and materials. A bicycle plant consumes frames and circuit parts, working time on the belt and wear of the assembly systems. All three belong in the cost as soon as they enter the performance in value. The sentence counts precisely the examples of definition, without artificially narrowing the circle to material alone.

The statement is true.

Some differences remain conscious. Costs largely correspond to the expenses, but there are some differences, for example the entrepreneur's wage. The claim that there are never differences, leaves this reservation exactly. Internally, a consumption can be calculated, which the accounting does not show as expenditure. If you force identity, you do not need to distinguish the two circuits.

The statement is false.

The amount does not change fixed costs as long as the capacity is valid. Fixed costs are incurred regardless of the quantity produced or produced. Management salaries, location rent and insurance continue to run, whether 10 or 10 000 wheels are assembled. The distinction presupposes that one knows which costs change as the quantity increases and which do not. The sentence applies to the definition of fixed costs.

The statement is true.

With the amount they increase, they do not fall. Variable costs usually increase proportional to the quantity produced. For bicycles, these are essentially the cost of the components. Whoever claims variable costs are lowered with increasing quantity, the direction turns. Unit costs can decrease due to fixed cost degression, while the variable costs of the additional wheels increase with the quantity.

The statement is false.

title: Fixed and variable costs
context: A company generates bicycles. Evaluate the following statements at fixed and variable costs:
statements: The salaries for the management are among the fixed costs.
The rent for the production site is one of the fixed costs if rent is payable.
The cost of the components from which the wheels are assembled is essentially variable costs.
Depreciation is only variable costs and increases proportional to the number of units.
When deciding on an additional contract, consider the additional costs incurred by this contract.
tactical_explanations:
The management is not re-employed per wheel. Fixed costs arise regardless of how many wheels are produced in one period. These include the salaries for the management. Whether the assembly is quieter or fuller, these salaries typically do not change during the period considered. The sentence correctly assigns the item to the fixed costs, as the bicycle example of the definition.

The statement is true.

The rent for the production site is one of the fixed costs if rent is payable. It does not depend on the number of wheels but on the contract of the area. Insurance is in the same group. Anyone who treats rent as proportional material items confuses location costs with components.

The statement is true.

Each additional wheel needs parts. Variable costs usually increase proportionally to the quantity produced. For bicycles, this is essentially the cost of the components from which the wheels are assembled. Frames, tyres and circuit follow the number of pieces. That is why they must be covered in the price at least before a cover contribution can be mentioned.

The statement is true.

Depreciation is at least partially fixed, not purely proportional. Depreciation is called depreciation in fixed costs, at least partly. Machine wear and tear can change with use, a pure proportional increase with each number of pieces is thus not the rule of the text. Those who only take depreciation as variable costs, cancel the reservation "at least in part" and the classification in addition to rent and management salaries.

The statement is false.

Additional order means: which costs are added new. If you decide to accept or reject an additional order, you will consider the additional costs incurred by this order. Even existing fixed costs of the hall and the management often do not change the individual order. The additional used components and additional costs are relevant. This is precisely the consideration that separates the theory from the question of the total unit costs of a normal program. The rent and management salaries that are already in operation usually do not change the individual additional order. Therefore, the question of the additional costs is the appropriate decision size, not the full average unit costs including all fixed costs.

The statement is true.

title: Contribution margin and price
context: Evaluate the following statements at price, variable costs and cover:
statements: The variable costs should in any case be covered by the price obtained.
If the price exceeds the variable costs, a contribution will be made to cover the fixed costs.
This contribution to cover fixed costs is the contribution of the cover.
The contribution of the cover is obtained by deducting from the price the total fixed costs of the company.
Overall, the price should cover the total cost, i.e. variable and fixed costs.
tactical_explanations:
Among the variable costs, one sells loss per piece in the narrow sense. The variable costs should be covered in all cases by the obtained price. If this cover is missing, each additional piece loses additional money before fixed costs come to the discussion. Components and other quantity-dependent consumptions must at least come back in the price. The rate sets the lower limit that the theory calls before the contribution.

The statement is true.

What is above the variable costs is working on the rent and salaries. If the price obtained exceeds the variable costs, a contribution is made to cover the fixed costs. Fixed costs are incurred independently of the quantity; without such contributions they remain uncovered. The sentence describes exactly this surplus, even without the formula unit price minus variable unit costs.

The statement is true.

The name bundles the same surplus. The contribution to the coverage of fixed costs is called a contribution to cover. It is the bridge between price and fixed cost block, not the profit after all costs. Only when the sum of the cover contributions exceeds fixed costs, profit arises. The sentence correctly places the term in this place.

The statement is true.

Fixed costs of the whole operation do not belong in the formula. The cover contribution of a wheel is the price minus the variable costs of this wheel, in the numerical example 400 minus 180 equals 220 euros. The total fixed costs of millions of amounts are not deducted from the individual price, otherwise a senseless negative amount would arise. The fixed costs are offset by the sum of the cover contributions or by break-even turnover and cover ratio. The rate confuses unit invoice and total block. The total fixed costs are deducted by the sum of the cover contributions or by break-even turnover and cover ratio. A deduction of the million block from the individual selling price would make the cover contribution unusable and make the bicycle example 400 minus 180 impossible.

The statement is false.

In the long term, full coverage counts. Overall, the price should cover the entire cost, both variable and fixed costs. The cover contribution is the first hurdle, the full cost recovery the existence condition. Short-term exceptions for unsaleable preseason goods does not change this target size. The rate is set by the target which the theory specifies according to the definition of the contribution.

The statement is true.

title: Short-term price discount
context: A retailer has bicycles from the preseason that can no longer be sold regularly. Rate the following statements:
statements: A lower price can be useful in the short term if the reduced price exceeds the variable cost.
It is more sensible not to sell such a wheel than to give it more favourable with a positive contribution.
The fixed costs are incurred in this situation anyway.
In the short term, any price below the variable cost is just as useful in business as a price above.
The contribution to cover fixed costs will also remain a contribution to a discount.
tactical_explanations:
Unsaleable preseason goods change the price logic for the moment. In the short term, a lower price can be useful if wheels from the preseason can no longer be sold regularly. If the reduced price exceeds the variable costs, at least a cover fee is incurred. Then something still flows against the fixed costs, instead of the wheel stopping. The sentence links the exception precisely to this condition, not to any gift. Regularly, the price should continue to cover variable and fixed costs together. The exception applies only to goods that can no longer be sold at the old price, and only as long as the new price remains above the variable costs.

The statement is true.

If the reduced price exceeds the variable costs, the sale is more sensible than not selling the bike. Fix costs continue, the unsold bike does not cover anything. The claim reverses the recommendation of the definition. Only if the discount price falls below the variable costs would any sale worsen the situation.

The statement is false.

Hall, insurance and management are not waiting for the last wheel. The contribution is a contribution to cover the fixed costs that are incurred anyway. Rent and similar items do not disappear because a model from the preseason seems unfor saleable. This is precisely why a price above the variable costs is worthwhile: it reduces the uncovered load without generating new fixed costs. The rate keeps this inevitability.

The statement is true.

The first contribution is missing from the variable costs themselves. The variable costs should be covered by the price in any case. A price below this increases the loss per piece and is not as useful as a price above it. The short-term exception only applies if the reduced price exceeds the variable costs. The rate cuts this limit and makes the exemption a release of any dumping price.

The statement is false.

The name does not change due to the discount. Also in the case of the lower price one speaks of cover fee, as soon as the price exceeds the variable costs: a contribution to cover the fixed costs. It is smaller than the regular price, but remains the same size. Profit after full costs does not have to follow. The sentence meets the definition that the theory repeats at exactly this point.

The statement is true.

title: Contribution margin of 400 euros
context: A company sells a bicycle by 400 euros. The variable costs are 180 euros. Rate the following statements:
statements: The contribution is 220 euros per wheel.
The coverage rate is 55 percent of the selling price.
The contribution is 180 euros per wheel.
The coverage rate is as 180 euros divided by 400 euros.
55 percent of the selling price can be used to cover fixed costs.
tactical_explanations:
Price minus variable costs, not minus profit target. 400 Euro selling price minus 180 Euro variable costs result in 220 Euro. This is exactly the amount that is called a cover fee for the bike. The 220 Euro are ready to cover the fixed costs before profit arises. Anyone reading 180 Euro as cover fee has confused the variable costs with the contribution. The identity is: Cover contribution = price - variable unit costs = 400 - 180 = 220. 220 euros is the amount that remains after covering the 180 euros components and other volume costs for rent, insurance and similar fixed costs. Only if such contributions exceed the fixed costs in the sum, profit arises, not even with the individual positive cover contribution.

The statement is true.

Share of the price, not share of the parts. 220 euros of 400 euros are 220 / 400 = 0.55, i.e. 55 percent. This percentage is called coverage rate. He says which part of each euro turnover can be paid to fixed costs as soon as the variable costs are earned. The quota depends on the ratio contribution to price, not on the mere material value 180 euros.

The statement is true.

180 euros are the variable costs, not the contribution. The contribution is 400 minus 180 equals 220 euros. Whoever states 180 euros as a contribution to the cover, equals the amount cost block with the surplus. Then the quota would be 180 / 400 = 45 percent, which contradicts the theory. The 180 euros must be covered first, the contribution comes after that.

The statement is false.

The quota depends on the contribution, not on the variable costs alone. Cover rate = cover contribution / selling price = 220 / 400 = 55 percent. 180 divided by 400 is 45 percent and measures the share of the variable costs in the price, not the coverage rate. 55 percent is expressly equal to 220 of 400. The wrong division exchanges counters.

The statement is false.

The same 55 percent logic will later be used to break-even. 55 percent of the selling prices can be used to cover fixed costs, because that is exactly the coverage rate. After variable costs, 55 cents of each turnover euro will remain for the fixed cost block. If the quota is uniform across all models, the same ratio will apply for the total turnover. The sentence repeats the bridge that builds the theory from the sample to the break-even calculation.

The statement is true.

title: Break-even sales
context: The fixed costs amount to 4 million euros, the coverage rate for all bicycle models 55 percent. Evaluate the following statements:
statements: Break-even sales are 4 million divided by 55 and multiplied by 100, i.e. 7 272 727.27 euros.
The company should make at least almost 7.3 million euros in sales to cover all costs.
Break-even sales are obtained by multiplying 4 million euros by 0.55.
With higher sales than break-even sales, the company is entering the profit zone.
By reaching the cost recovery at the break-even point, the company secures its existence in the sense of the section.
tactical_explanations:
Fixed costs equal to 55 percent of the desired turnover. The fixed costs of 4 million euros are equated with the coverage rate 55 percent. Then the following applies: 4 000 000 / 55 × 100 = 7 272 727.27 euros. In other words: turnover = fixed costs / 0.55 = 4 000 000 / 0.55 = 7 272 727.27. In this turnover, the cumulative cover contributions cover precisely the fixed cost block. The theory calculates the same path.

The statement is true.

The threshold is almost 7.3 million. 7 272 727.27 euros is almost 7.3 million euros. Under this brand fixed costs remain uncovered, above which the profit zone begins. The sentence takes over the qualitative conclusion of the numerical example without inventing a new formula. The protection of livelihood depends on full cost recovery from turnover, not on any revenue target.

The statement is true.

Multiplying instead of dividing provides the contribution to cover, not turnover. 4 000 000 × 0.55 = 2 200 000 Euro would be the contribution to cover, which 4 million sales would yield at 55 percent quota, well below fixed costs. The desired break-even turnover is generated by dividing the fixed costs by the quota, not by multiplying. The wrong calculation is a reversal of the equation "Fix costs = 55 percent of turnover". The equation is: 0.55 times turnover = 4 000 000, i.e. turnover = 4 000 000 divided by 0.55. Multiplication of fixed costs with the quota answers another question, namely which contribution a known turnover would be required.

The statement is false.

The company is in the profit zone if sales are higher than break-even. According to the assumptions, every further Euro turnover is 55 cents above the fixed costs already covered. Under the threshold, fixed costs are partially uncovered. The rate follows directly the invoice 7.27 million in theory.

The statement is true.

Cost recovery is the condition of existence here. The company is supposed to make at least 7.3 million sales to cover at least all costs; with higher turnover it comes into the profit zone and thus secures its existence. In the long term no company can exist if costs are not covered by income. The break-even point is exactly this threshold in the numerical example, not a mandatory tax size.

The statement is true.

title: Structure of the income statement
context: Evaluate the following statements the profit and loss account:
statements: In the G&V, the expenses are deducted from revenues and other revenues.
The expenditure includes, among other things, wages and salaries, material costs, rent, insurance, energy, depreciation and the formation of provisions.
If the sum of proceeds and revenues exceeds the expenses, a profit is achieved.
The profit in G&V is always identical to the cash flow of the same period.
Profit increases equity.
tactical_explanations:
Income minus expense, that is G&V. The expenses are deducted from the revenue and other income. Thus, the profit for the period is generated, not by comparison of deposits and withdrawals. The FunBike figures start with revenue and deduct material, personnel, depreciation and other operating expenses, up to EBIT and further to the annual result. The rate describes exactly this structure. Deposits and withdrawals belong in financial and cash flow accounts. Depreciation and provisions show in the G&V expense, which does not have to be money in the same period, and precisely for this reason the income statement stands next to the payment invoice.

The statement is true.

The expenditure list is wider than just material. Wages and salaries, material expenses, rent, insurance expenses, energy costs, depreciation of property, plant and equipment and the formation of provisions are among the expenses. Depreciation and provisions show that expenditure does not have to be the same as a payment of the period. The sentence collects the examples of the definition and identifies the G&V as income calculation.

The statement is true.

If the sum of proceeds and income exceeds the expenses, a profit is achieved. Then the company has become richer in the period, in the sense of the accounting question of the section. If the expenses are higher, loss arises. The rate holds the sign rule without mixing cash flow or unit costs.

The statement is true.

Success and cash flow are falling apart. Cash flow is not identical to profit: you can achieve profit without having liquid funds, and be liquid without earning profit. Depreciation reduces profit without having to drain money in the period; stock building can tie money while the G&V still shows profit. The assertion of a constant identity contradicts this very distinction.

The statement is false.

Profit strengthens the liability side at the bottom left of equity. Profit increases equity and can also be determined from the comparison of current equity with that at the beginning of the financial year. In the FunBike balance sheet, profit of EUR 3 614 250 is explicitly in equity. Withdrawal or distribution would be the countermovement. The rate is the effect attributed to the theory of G&V and double profit determination.

The statement is true.

title: Two ways to determine profit
context: Evaluate the following statements for double profit determination:
statements: The profit is determined in the profit and loss account.
Profit can also be determined by comparing equity at the beginning and end of a financial year.
Both paths must yield the same profit.
This double profit determination is related to the concept of double accounting.
The revenue-expense invoice is considered to be double accounting because it contains depreciation.
tactical_explanations:
The G&V is the first way to the profit for the period. Double accounting results in balance sheet and profit and loss account; the profit is calculated in the G&V. Revenue and income minus expenses lead to the annual profit. FunBike shows this path up to 3 614 250 euros. The rate specifies the one of the two prescribed ways without excluding the equity comparison. FunBike leads this path numerically up to the annual result 3 614 250 euros. The same amount must be found in the equity comparison, otherwise the double determination would be broken. The G&V remains the detailed expense-earnings invoice, not just a residual size of the balance sheet.

The statement is true.

The same story is told by increasing equity. Profit can also be determined by comparing equity at the beginning and end of a financial year. If equity is increased, profits are present, losses are reduced, if withdrawals and deposits are taken into account appropriately. The balance sheet of two key dates thus provides the second measurement. Both paths are considered to be mutually exclusive. Withdrawals and deposits are to be separated appropriately, otherwise a private withdrawal would have a loss. Therefore, the equity comparison is considered to be the second, equivalent path next to the G&V, not an approximate estimate.

The statement is true.

Same profit, otherwise accounting is not correct. Both investigations must yield the same profit, hence double profit determination. If G&V and equity comparison differ, there is a mistake in business cases or in the final thesis. The agreement is the control, not an approximate approximation. The rate represents exactly this must condition.

The statement is true.

The name double accounting is attached to this duplication. It is called double profit determination and in this context also double accounting: balance sheet plus G&V, profit in two ways. That is more than the mere existence of depreciation. The sentence arranges the term as the section introduces it according to G&V.

The statement is true.

EAR remains the simpler alternative, not double accounting. Individual companies and partnerships below 700 000 euros in turnover can create a revenue-expense invoice that is less expensive than double accounting. Depreciation is in the EAR, which does not make it double accounting with balance sheet, G&V and double profit determination. Capital companies and exceeding the turnover limit lead to double accounting. The rate mixes both forms.

The statement is false.

title: Income statement of FunBike GmbH
context: Profit and loss account of FunBike GmbH as at 31.12.20xx (Euro): Revenue 70 656 000, Material expenses 53 175 000, Personnel expenses 7 900 000, Depreciation 1 800 000, Other operating expenses 2 875 000, EBIT 4 906 000, Interest income 12 000, Interest expense 99 000, Financial result -87 000, Earnings before taxes 4 819 000, Taxes 1 204 750, Annual result 3 614 250. Evaluate the following statements:
statements: Earnings before interest and taxes (EBIT) are EUR 4 906 000.
The material expenditure clearly exceeds the personnel costs.
The financial result is -87 000 euros.
The annual result is in line with the profit of EUR 3 614 250 recorded in the balance sheet.
The annual result is 4 906 000 euros.
tactical_explanations:
According to operating expenses, EBIT. Revenues 70 656 000 minus material 53 175 000 minus personnel 7 900 000 minus depreciation 1 800 000 minus other operating expenses 2 875 000 result in 4 906 000. 70 656 000 - 53 175 000 = 17 481 000; 17 481 000 - 7 900 000 = 9 581 000; 9 581 000 - 1 800 000 = 7 7 781 000; 7 778 000 - 2 875 000 = 4 906 000. The theory shows exactly this result before interest and taxes. Interest and taxes are not yet deducted in this 4 906 000 euro size. The financial result and the tax line follow only after and lead to the annual result. Anyone who exchanges EBIT and profit skips exactly these two stages of the G&V.

The statement is true.

Parts and pre-products dominate the expenditure side. Material expenditure 53 175 000 Euro stands against personnel costs 7 900 000 Euro. 53 175 000 is several times as large as 7 900 000; this fits with a bicycle manufacturer who buys many components. The relation can be read directly from the two lines, without estimation. If you thought the staff block was the most expensive, the G&V would be against 53 175 000 to 7 900 000, more than six times the cost bill would read the same material block mainly as variable costs of the components, while staff and depreciation would sit more mixed. The G&V delivers the raw numbers for this internal interpretation without separating fixed and variable.

The statement is true.

Interest net with signposts. Interest income 12 000 minus interest expense 99 000 result minus 87 000 Euro. The financial result is negative and separates EBIT from earnings before taxes. Anyone who confuses EBIT with the financial result reads the wrong line. The statement takes over the reported balance correctly. The negative financial result is between EBIT and earnings before taxes.

The statement is true.

The same 3 614 250 Euro bridge between G&V and balance sheet. Annual profit or profit 3 614 250 Euro is in G&V; the same profit in equity appears in the balance sheet alongside the cash deposits of 525 000 Euro. 4 819 000 - 1 204 750 = 3 614 250 confirms the tax line. The agreement is the double profit determination in figures, not by chance of two independent sizes. 4 819 000 minus 1 204 750 results in 3 614 250 and closes the EBIT chain via financial result and taxes. Without this agreement, the double profit determination in FunBike figures would be refuted.

The statement is true.

The EBIT is 4 906 000 euros, not the profit after interest and taxes. After financial result -87 000 follows 4 819 000 before tax, after tax 1 204 750 remains 3 614 250. title: Cash flow and profit
context: Evaluate the following statements Cash flow statement:
statements: Published financial statements include balance sheet and G&V as well as cash flow accounts.
The cash flow statement shows cash inflows and cash outflows in a period and is also called cash flow statement.
You can make a profit without having liquid funds.
You can be liquid without winning a profit.
Cash flow is identical to profit because both measure the same profit for the period.
tactical_explanations:
Three parts form the published financial statements in this section. In addition to balance sheet and G&V, published financial statements also include cash flow statements. It complements assets and success with cash flows. Investors find there whether the core operation delivers overpayments. The rate counts the components as they are introduced after the FunBike-G&V.

The statement is true.

Cash flow, not expense and income. The cash flow statement shows the cash inflows and outflows in and out of the company during the period considered, usually for a financial year. Therefore, it is also called cash flow statement. Deposits and withdrawals are the focus, analogous to the financial statement, but broken down by causes. The sentence hits object and second name.

The statement is true.

Profit without cash is possible. Cash flow is a measure of solvency and not identical to profit; one can achieve a profit without having liquid funds. Claims instead of payment, stock build-up or redemption pressure can separate the profit from liquidity. Depreciation reduces profit without cash outflow, while other transactions deduct money without hitting the profit as well. The rate holds exactly this possibility. Depreciation of 1 800 000 euros in the FunBike-G&V reduces profit without having to drain money in the same amount. Receivables and stocks can in reverse tie money while the G&V still shows profit. This is precisely why such bridges explain why liquidity and success can fall apart.

The statement is true.

Cashier without profit is also possible. You can be liquid without earning a profit. Borrowing or selling of fixed assets increase means of payment without G&V having to report profit. A loss year with outstanding bank balances fits into the same picture. The sentence is the second half of the same distinction in theory.

The statement is true.

Two key figures, two questions. Cash flow is not identical to profit. Profit answers whether the company has become richer or poorer; cash flow answers cash flow and liquidity. The claim that both are moderate in the same period and are therefore identical, cancels depreciation, provisions, stockpiling and financing operations. This is why the cash flow statement is in addition to G&V, not as a copy.

The statement is false.

title: Areas of the cash flow statement
context: Evaluate the following statements on the cash flow account:
statements: The operating activity division is the most important in the cash flow statement because it concerns the core of the business.
Inflows can arise in the financing sector if new shareholders bring equity or loans to debt.
Interest payments, dividend payments or loan repayments are the outflows in the financing area.
In the investment sector, cash flows are made when capital is purchased and can be paid in when, for example, a property is sold.
Investors are looking primarily at the investment sector because only there is the core of the business visible.
tactical_explanations:
Operations hits the core. Operating activity is the most important in cash flow accounting because it affects the core of the business. It shows whether there are deposits generated. Investors therefore often look at this part in particular. Financing and investment explain capital raising and asset purchase, but do not replace the view of the operational business.

The statement is true.

New funds from shareholders or banks end up in financing. This area shows inflows from financing activities, for example by taking up new shareholders and thus equity or loans and thus debt capital. This is the source of funds in means of payment, not the turnover from bicycle sales. The sentence correctly assigns both sources to this block.

The statement is true.

Outflows of the financing are interest, dividends and redemption. The outflow in this area is, for example, related to interest payments, dividend payments or loan repayments. These are capital costs and capital repayments, not the purchase of a machine. Whoever forces them into operating activities mixes core process and capital structure. The sentence follows the assignment of the definition.

The statement is true.

Investments are linked to money, investments are freed up. In the investment area, it is clear whether payment methods have flowed into long-term investments to buy fixed assets. On the other hand, payment methods can be generated when investment assets have been sold, such as a property or a building. Both relate to long-term bonds, not to daily turnover. The sentence indicates inflow and drain in the direction provided by the book.

The statement is true.

The core is in operating activities, not in investments. Investors often look at the part of operating activities because it shows whether the core business delivers surplus deposits. The investment area explains investment purchases and sales, not the ongoing success of the business model. The claim is that the most important area is swapped with another. Machine purchase can even be negative in the investment cash flow, while the operating business is healthy. A strong negative investment cash flow can even be a sign of machine purchase and growth, while weak operating surpluses would be the real warning signal. The ranking of the three areas must therefore not be reversed.

The statement is false.

title: Current-asset intensity and golden balance sheet rule
context: Balance sheet of FunBike GmbH as at 31.12.20xx (Euro): Land and buildings 750 000, technical installations 2 330 000, financial assets 240 000, inventories 5 400 000, receivables 598 000, bank balance 320 250, balance sheet total 9 638 250.

title: FunBike: golden balance sheet rule

title: FunBike: income statement from sales to EBIT
context: Profit and loss account of FunBike GmbH as at 31.12.20xx (Euro): sales revenue 70 656 000, material expenses 53 175 000, personnel expenses 7 900 000, depreciation 1 800 000, other operating expenses 2 875 000, earnings before interest and taxes (EBIT) 4 906 000, interest income 12 000, interest expense 99 000, financial result -87 000, earnings before taxes 4 819 000, taxes 1 204 750, Annual result 3 614 250. statements: Revenues minus the four operating expenses blocks result in EBIT of EUR 4 906 000.

Operating profit is calculated line by line. Start: Sales revenue 70 656 000. Minus material 53 175 000 equals 17 481 000. Minus personnel 7 900 000 equals 9 581 000. Minus depreciation 1 800 000 equals 7 781 000. Minus other operating expenses 2 875 000 equals 4 906 000. That is exactly the EBIT line of the definition. Sample in one step: sum of the four expenses 53 175 000 + 7 900 000 + 1 800 000 + 2 875 000 = 65 750 000, and 70 656 000 - 65 750 000 = 4 906 000. Interest rates 12 000 and 99 000 and taxes 1 204 750 do not belong in this stage, they come only after EBIT.

The statement is true.

Interests have an auspicious sign and a netting. Formula: Financial result = interest income - interest expense. Insertion from the definition: 12 000 - 99 000 = - 87 000 Euro. The line financial result shows exactly this - 87 000. Interest expense exceeds interest income by 87 000; the balance is negative and reduces earnings after EBIT 4 906 000 to 4 819 000 before tax. The financial result does not replace EBIT or the annual result, it is the interest bridge between them.

The statement is true.

EBIT is an intermediate stage, not the profit after interest and taxes. After EBIT 4 906 000 follows financial result -87 000, after that 4 819 000 before tax, after tax 1 204 750, then annual result 3 614 250. Comparison: 4 906 000 If you read EBIT as an annual result, you stop two lines too early. The balance sheet shows a profit of 3 614 250, not 4 906 000.

The statement is false.

The bridge from operating profit to tax base. Formula: Earnings before taxes = EBIT + financial result. Insert: 4 906 000 + (-87 000) = 4 819 000. The threshold confirms 4 819 000. Sample backward: 4 819 000 - 4 906 000 = -87 000, equal to the financial result. Without this identity, the G&V would be internally inconsistent; with it the next subtraction, the taxes 1 204 750, is on the right basis and leads to 3 614 250.

The statement is true.

Tax line and line of profit do not swap. Comparison in the definition: Taxes 1 204 750 for annual income 3 614 250. 1 204 750 < 3 614 250, difference 3 614 250 - 1 204 750 = 2 409 500. Sample of line of profit: Earnings before taxes 4 819 000 - Taxes 1 204 750 = 3 614 250. The taxes are the deduction from the tax base, not the larger rest. The statement claims the opposite of the last two G&V numbers and would read the profit less than the tax burden.

The statement is false.

title: FunBike: profit in income statement and balance sheet
context: Profit and loss account of FunBike GmbH as at 31.12.20xx (Euro): sales revenue 70 656 000, material expenses 53 175 000, personnel expenses 7 900 000, depreciation 1 800 000, other operating expenses 2 875 000, earnings before interest and taxes (EBIT) 4 906 000, interest income 12 000, interest expense 99 000, financial result -87 000, earnings before taxes 4 819 000, taxes 1 204 750, Earnings for the year 3 614 250. tactical_explanations:

The statement is true.

The profit is the annual result 3 614 250 from the G&V. Insertion: 525 000 + 3 614 250 = 4 139 250. Sample against the balance sheet total: Debt 2 000 000 + 3 199 000 + 300 000 = 5 499 000, and 4 139 250 + 5 499 000 = 9 638 250. The statement is true.

Turnover is the first G&V line, not the line of profit on the balance sheet. Turnover 70 656 000 is only above the income statement. In the balance sheet is profit item 3 614 250. Compare: 70 656 000 If you copy the turnover into the liabilities, you confuse the proceeds with the profit for the period after all deductions and would exceed the balance sheet total.

The statement is false.
