Material is expense, not profit. Material expenditure 53 175 000 is the largest negative line of the G&V. Annual result is 3 614 250. Comparison: 53 175 000 The rest bears staff, depreciation, other expenses, interest, taxes and only then profit 3 614 250, which returns to the balance sheet.

The statement is false.

Final subtraction before profit. Formula: Earnings before taxes. Inserting: 4 819 000 - 1 204 750 = 3 614 250. The same 3 614 250 stands on the balance sheet as profit in addition to cash deposits 525 000. The chain is consistent: EBIT 4 906 000 plus financial result -87 000 equals 4 819 000, minus taxes 1 204 750 equals 3 614 250. This means that the bridge between the profit and loss account and the balance sheet is arithmetically closed, as required by the double profit determination.

The statement is true.

title: FunBike: current-asset intensity and asset shares
context: The simplified balance sheet of FunBike GmbH as at 31.12.20xx (Euro): Assets - Land and buildings 750 000, technical assets and business equipment 2 330 000, financial assets 240 000, inventories 5 400 000, receivables from supplies and services 598 000, bank balances and cash stock 320 250; balance sheet total 9 638 250. Liabilities - cash contributions of the shareholders 525 000, profit 3 614 250, provisions 2 000 000, bank loans 3 199 000, liabilities from supplies and services 300 000. Evaluate the following statements:
statements: The reserves of 5 400 000 euros in themselves exceed the total fixed assets of 3 320 000 euros.
More than half of the balance sheet total is fixed assets.
Current assets account for more than 65 percent of the balance sheet total.
Bank balances and cash stock 320 250 Euro exceed the inventories 5 400 000 Euro.
FunBike is a busy business because 6 318 250 euros of current assets are well above 3 320 000 euros of fixed assets and the stocks dominate this circulation.
tactical_explanations:
A single asset line beats the entire investment block. Inventories 5 400 000, fixed assets 750 000 + 2 330 000 + 240 000 = 3 320 000. Comparison: 5 400 000 - 3 320 000 = 2 080 000 Euro Advance of inventories. Ratio: 5 400 000 / 3 320 000 ᐅ 1,63, well over 1.6 times the total buildings, installations and financial assets. Share of the balance sheet total: 5 400 000 / 9 638 250 ᐅ 0.56, i.e. about 56 percent of the total assets are in the warehouse. That is why the theory speaks of dominance of stocks in a bicycle manufacturer that stores components and finished wheels.

The statement is true.

Investment is the smaller part of assets. Share: 3 320 000 / 9 638 250 ᐅ 0.3444, about 34 percent, not over 50 percent. Half of the balance sheet total would be 9 638 250 / 2 = 4 819 125; 3 320 000 would remain 1 499 125 below. Circulation 6 318 250 / 9 638 250 ᐅ 0.656 is clearly above half. Those who read buildings and machines as majority assets ignore reserves 5 400 000 plus receivables 598 000 plus bank 320 250. The definition is cumbersome, non-plant-loaded.

The statement is false.

Sixty-five percent as a threshold against the calculated value. Current assets = 5 400 000 + 598 000 + 320 250 = 6 318 250. Quota: 6 318 250 / 9 638 250 ᐅ 0.6556, i.e. approximately 65.6 percent. Compared to the threshold: 65.6 > 65, the condition is met. Sample: Appendix 3 320 000 / 9 638 250 ᐅ 34.4%, and 34.4 + 65.6 = 100 percent of the 9 638 250. The statement demands precisely this reading of the three circulation lines, not an estimate without division.

The statement is true.

Cash against stock: the order of magnitude tilts. Bank balances and cash stock 320 250, inventories 5 400 000. Comparison: 320 250 < 5 400 000. Ratio: 320 250 / 5 400 000 ̄ 0.059, about 6 percent of inventories. Difference 5 400 000 - 320 250 = 5 079 750. Liquid funds are available, but do not dominate the circulation (6 318 250) nor the balance sheet total (9 638 250). The claim swaps the two lines and would make FunBike appear as cashy instead of stock-intensive.

The statement is false.

Both book criteria apply together at FunBike. Circulation 6 318 250 against Appendix 3 320 000: 6 318 250 / 3 320 000 ̄ 1.90, significantly more circulation, therefore circulation intensive. Within circulation: Inventories 5 400 000 / 6 318 250 ᐅ 0.855, about 86 percent, therefore dominance of inventories. Claims and bank remain 598 000 + 320 250 = 918 250. The theory applies exactly these two observations to FunBike without needing a second company or a second year.

The statement is true.

title: FunBike: ratios from balance sheet and income statement
context: The simplified balance sheet of FunBike GmbH as at 31.12.20xx (Euro): Assets - Land and buildings 750 000, technical assets and business equipment 2 330 000, financial assets 240 000, inventories 5 400 000, receivables from supplies and services 598 000, bank balances and cash stock 320 250; balance sheet total 9 638 250. Liabilities - cash contributions of the shareholders 525 000, profit 3 614 250, provisions 2 000 000, bank loans 3 199 000, liabilities from supplies and services 300 000. Profit and loss account of FunBike GmbH as at 31.12.20xx (Euro): sales revenue 70 656 000, material expenses 53 175 000, personnel expenses 7 900 000, depreciation 1 800 000, other operating expenses 2 875 000, earnings before interest and taxes (EBIT) 4 906 000, interest income 12 000, interest expense 99 000, financial result -87 000, earnings before taxes 4 819 000, taxes 1 204 750, Annual result 3 614 250. Rate the following statements:
statements: Debt ratio = 5 499 000 / 9 638 250 ᐅ 57 percent, as typical for FunBike.
The material cost corresponds to more than 70 percent of the sales revenue.
The personnel costs of 7 900 000 Euro exceed the material costs of 53 175 000 Euro.
Profit of EUR 3 614 250 in the balance sheet is smaller than EBIT of EUR 4 906 000, as after that financial result and taxes will be deducted.
Depreciation of EUR 1 800 000 is equal to the amount paid out in the same period and therefore identical to the profit.
tactical_explanations:
Liabilities ratio, not from feeling. Debt = 2 000 000 + 3 199 000 + 300 000 = 5 499 000. Balance sheet total = 9 638 250. Division: 5 499 000 / 9 638 250 = 0.570539... ᐅ 57.05 percent, rounded off by the book as about 57 percent. Sample Equity ratio: (525 000 + 3 614 250) / 9 638 250 = 4 139 250 / 9 638 250 ᐅ 42.95 percent, and 57.05 + 42.95 = 100. The capital structure with about 57 percent debt capital, of which the majority of bank loans 3 199 000, is thus fixed on the threshold.

The statement is true.

Material intensity measured by turnover. Meter Material expenditure 53 175 000, Denominator Sales revenues 70 656 000. Quotient: 53 175 000 / 70 656 000 ᐅ 0.7526, i.e. about 75.3 percent. Compared to the threshold: 75.3 > 70, the condition is clearly met. Personnel 7 900 000 / 70 656 000 ᐅ 0.112, about 11.2 percent, remains well below. Depreciation 1 800 000 / 70 656 000 ᐅ 2.5 percent. For the bicycle manufacturer, the material block is the dominant operating expense; the profit and loss account shows this in the first negative line.

The statement is true.

Personnel against material: the larger line is material. Comparison of G&V: personnel costs 7 900 000 against material costs 53 175 000. 7 900 000 - 53 175 000 = -45 275,000, personnel is 45,275 million below material. Ratio: 7 900 000 / 53 175 000 ̄ 0.149, about 15 percent of material costs. The statement turns the two minus lines around. EBIT 4 906 000 is only created after the much larger material deduction has already been deducted from sales revenues of 70 656 000.

The statement is false.

Earnings after interest and taxes are the smaller step. EBIT 4 906 000, annual result 3 614 250, and exactly 3 614 250 is on the balance sheet as profit. Difference: 4 906 000 - 3 614 250 = 1 291 750. Disaggregation at G&V: Financial result 87 000 plus taxes 1 204 750 = 1 291 750. Levels: EBIT 4 906 000, earnings before taxes 4 819 000, annual result 3 614 250. Therefore, the net profit must be below EBIT as soon as interest and taxes are negatively charged. The balance sheet and G&V bear the same 3 614 250.

The statement is true.

Depreciation is expense, not automatic disbursement, not profit. The G&V shows depreciations -1 800 000 and annual result 3 614 250; comparison 1 800 000

Profit and cash flow are not identical: you can achieve profit without having cash and be liquid without earning profit. FunBike illustrates the separation because 1 800 000 reduce the profit without having to drain money in the same amount.

Note: Deposits and withdrawals control the financial and cash flow account, income and expenses of G&V.

The statement is false.

title: Unit contribution margin from price and variable costs
context: A bicycle manufacturer sells a model of 400 euros per piece; the variable cost is 180 euros per piece. Rate the following statements on the gross margin contribution:
statements: The contribution per wheel is the price minus variable costs, i.e. 400 minus 180 equals 220 euros.
The contribution per wheel is 180 euros, because that is the variable costs.
The coverage rate is 220 divided by 400, i.e. 55 percent.
The coverage rate is 180 divided by 400, 45 percent.
The selling price exceeds the variable costs by 220 euros per wheel.
tactical_explanations:
Price minus variable costs per piece. 400 euros selling price minus 180 euros variable costs result in 220 euros unit gross margin. This amount remains after deduction of the quantity costs to bear the fixed costs. It is neither the price nor the variable costs alone. The difference is the central size of the break-even invoice.

The statement is true.

The variable costs per wheel are 180 euros; the cover contribution is the difference at the price: 400 minus 180 equals 220 euros. Whoever uses 180 as cover contribution confuses the cost block with surplus per piece. Fixing costs cover only starts at 220 euros. Only the difference to the price of 400 euros will result in the cover contribution.

The statement is false.

Two hundred and twenty of four hundred are 55 percent. The coverage rate sets the unit gross margin in relation to the price: 220 divided by 400 is 0.55. Of each euro turnover, 55 cents remain for fixed cost coverage. The quota is a ratio, not a euro amount. It later controls break-even sales. Fifty-five cents per turnover euro will later control the break-even.

The statement is true.

Forty-five percent are the variable cost share. 180 divided by 400 is 0.45; that is the share of variable costs in the price, not the coverage ratio. The coverage ratio is 220 divided by 400 equals 0.55. Those who exchange cost share and coverage ratio underestimate the contribution to fixed cost coverage. The coverage rate is 55 percent, not this proportion of costs.

The statement is false.

The price is 220 euros above the volume costs. 400 minus 180 results in the same surplus per wheel, which contributes the fixed costs as a unit gross margin. Without this gap nothing remains for fixed costs and profit. The statement describes exactly this difference. It is the verbal form of the cover contribution formula. Without this difference nothing would remain for fixed costs and later profit.

The statement is true.

title: Break-even sales from fixed costs and contribution ratio
context: The same bicycle producer will bear 4 000 000 Euro fixed costs per year; the contribution per bike is 220 Euro at a sales price of 400 Euro. Rate the following statements about break-even sales:
statements: Break-even sales are obtained by dividing the fixed costs of EUR 4 000 000 by the coverage rate of 0.55.
With a coverage rate of 55 percent, the company must generate more than EUR 4,000,000 in sales to cover all costs.
Break-even sales correspond exactly to the fixed costs of EUR 4 000 000, because the fixed costs determine the turnover threshold.
Break-even turnover is obtained by multiplying the fixed costs by the coverage rate of 0.55.
Above break-even sales, the company achieves a profit because the fixed costs are already covered.
tactical_explanations:
Fixed costs divided by the quota. At the break-even point, the cumulative cover contributions cover the fixed costs: turnover times 0.55 equals 4 000 000, i.e. turnover equals 4 000 000 divided by 0.55, about 7 272 727 euros. The division by the coverage rate delivers exactly this threshold. Without the quota, only the fixed cost number would remain.

The statement is true.

Four million sales are not enough at 55 percent. Only 55 cents of each turnover euro contribute to fixed cost coverage; 4 000 000 times 0.55 would be only 2 200 000 euros of cover contribution. The necessary turnover is significantly higher than, at around 7.27 million euros. Therefore, the company must achieve more than 4 000 000 euros of turnover.

The statement is true.

Fixed costs and break-even sales are not identical. Only with a coverage rate of 100 percent, both fell together. At 55 percent, the turnover must be greater than the fixed costs themselves: 4 000 000 divided by 0.55, the figure is around 7 272 727 euros, not 4 000 000. Those who equate both ignore the variable cost share. At 55 percent quota, the threshold is clearly above the fixed cost.

The statement is false.

Multiplying provides the contribution of a previously known turnover, not the desired break-even turnover.

The statement is false.

Above the threshold, the contribution to profit is a contribution to cover. Every euro turnover above it continues to provide 55 cents of contribution, which is no longer needed for fixed costs, because they are already covered. Below the threshold, fixed costs remain partially uncovered. The profit zone only starts from break-even sales.

The statement is true.

title: Reading the contribution ratio correctly
context: The same bicycle producer calculates 400 euros of sales price, 180 euros of variable costs and 4 000 000 euros of fixed costs per year. Evaluate the following statements about the coverage rate:
statements: The coverage ratio indicates how much per cent of each selling price euro is left after deduction of the variable costs for fixed cost coverage.
The coverage rate can be calculated by dividing the fixed costs by the selling price of a single piece.
At break-even point, the coverage rate multiplied by break-even turnover meets exactly the fixed costs.
The coverage rate shall be equal to the variable cost per unit in euro.
The higher the coverage rate, the lower the required break-even turnover at the same fixed cost.
tactical_explanations:
The quota measures the rest per turnover euro. After deduction of variable costs, a percentage of fixed cost coverage remains; this is the coverage ratio. It is the ratio of cover contribution to sales price, not an absolute euro amount. Anyone who confuses it with fixed costs or unit numbers reads the wrong size. The statement makes the interpretation.

The statement is true.

Fixed costs due to unit price result in a quantity, not a percentage. The coverage rate is generated from cover contribution divided by selling price and does not depend on the absolute fixed cost amount. If you divide fixed costs by 400 euros, you calculate a unit number-like size and miss the quota. The correct counter is the cover contribution.

The statement is false.

At break-even, the percentage of turnover hits the fixed costs. By definition, cover ratio multiplied by break-even turnover equals fixed costs. Exactly there, the accumulated cover contributions equal the fixed costs, without profit or loss. The statement describes this zero profit condition. It is the sample of the break-even invoice.

The statement is true.

The variable costs are a monetary amount per piece, while the coverage rate is a percentage of the selling price. Both sizes are related but are not identical: the quota describes the share of the price left after deduction of the variable costs, not the variable costs themselves.

The statement is false.

Higher quota reduces the necessary turnover. Because break-even turnover is equal to fixed costs divided by coverage ratio, the denominator is larger and the result smaller when the quota increases. If the fixed cost increases, less turnover is enough to cover. If the quota is raised, the threshold is shifted downwards. The statement is made by this inverse.

The statement is true.

title: Finding the break-even quantity
context: The break-even number of items can also be derived from sales price 400 euros, variable costs 180 euros and fixed costs 4 000 000 euros. Rate the following statements:
statements: The break-even number of pieces is obtained by dividing the fixed costs by the unit gross margin contribution.
The break-even number of pieces is obtained by dividing the fixed costs by the selling price.
If you multiply the break-even number with the selling price, you get the same amount as the break-even turnover over the coverage rate.
If a company sells so many pieces that the fixed costs alone would be covered by the variable costs, that is enough for the break-even.
If a company sells more pieces than the break-even number of pieces, the accumulated contribution is above the fixed costs.
tactical_explanations:
Each piece delivers the same contribution. The fixed costs are covered as soon as the sum of the unit cover contributions reaches the fixed costs. Formula: Number of pieces equals fixed costs divided by contribution per piece. This is the quantity threshold in pieces, not in euros. Those who divide by the price instead of by the cover contribution end up with the wrong quantity.

The statement is true.

The selling price alone does not cover the fixed costs, because of which the variable costs per piece must be deducted first. The correct denominator is the contribution of the cover per piece (price minus variable costs), not the full selling price. Division by the price would underestimate the number of pieces.

The statement is false.

Break-even unit number times selling price results in the same break-even turnover as fixed costs divided by the coverage rate. Both ways describe the same point in different units. The sample: turnover times quota returns the fixed costs again. Whoever gets different thresholds has changed the denominator on the way.

The statement is true.

The variable costs are already included in the cover contribution and do not contribute to the fixed cost coverage; they are just deducted before the cover contribution arises. A turnover that only covers the variable costs leaves nothing to be done for the fixed costs and therefore is not enough for the break-even.

The statement is false.

Above the unit threshold, profit arises. Each additional piece continues to provide the same cover contribution that is no longer needed for fixed costs, because these are already reached. The cumulative cover contribution exceeds the fixed costs. Below the threshold, undercover remains. More pieces than break-even therefore means profit zone.

The statement is true.

title: Checking different sales levels for cost recovery
context: Check whether selected annual sales cover fixed costs based on sales price 400 euros, variable costs 180 euros and fixed costs 4 000 000 euros. Evaluate the following statements:
statements: With annual sales amounting to fixed costs, fixed costs remain hidden as long as the coverage rate is below 100 percent.
An annual turnover equal to the fixed costs is already at break-even point.
Annual turnover twice as high as fixed costs inevitably leads to the profit zone.
Whether a certain annual turnover covers fixed costs depends on both turnover and coverage.
Annual sales just below break-even sales are already in the profit zone because it is close to the threshold.
tactical_explanations:
Sales in the amount of fixed costs are not enough for quota below 100 percent. The variable cost share is deducted from turnover first; the residual cover contribution is then below fixed costs. Fix costs remain hidden. Only a higher turnover closes the gap. The statement describes precisely this undercover for quota below one.

The statement is true.

Break-even is fixed costs divided by quota, not fixed costs themselves. For a quota below 100 percent, the actual break-even turnover is above fixed costs, because the denominator is smaller than one. Therefore, a turnover equal to fixed costs is not yet the break-even point. The statement falsely equates both amounts.

The statement is false.

A turnover that is far above break-even sales generates a contribution to cover that exceeds fixed costs - provided that the coverage rate remains positive, which is the case with realistic cost structures. A turnover twice as high as the fixed costs is usually well enough for this.

The statement is true.

Cost recovery requires turnover and quota. First turnover times coverage rate results in the profit margin achieved, which is compared with fixed costs. Turnover alone, without knowledge of the quota, does not say anything about the coverage. Both sizes belong together. The statement holds exactly this two-stageness. Without quota, turnover alone remains silent to cost recovery.

The statement is true.

Just below the threshold is no profit zone. The fixed costs are only fully covered from break-even sales. Closeness to the threshold does not mean that they have already reached them. Below the limit, a rest of the fixed costs remain open. Anyone "just reads as profit" confuses rapprochement with overstepping. Only reaching or crossing the threshold opens the winning zone.

The statement is false.

title: Identities in break-even analysis
context: A bicycle manufacturer calculates the selling price of 400 euros, variable costs of 180 euros per unit and fixed costs of 4 000 000 euros per year. Evaluate the following statements about the calculation context:
statements: The contribution of the cover plus variable costs will return the selling price per piece.
Break-even turnover multiplied by the coverage rate results in fixed costs.
At break-even point, the sum of the cover contributions is equal to the fixed costs.
At the break-even point, sales always correspond exactly to fixed costs, regardless of the coverage rate.
In the long term, the sales price is intended to cover not only variable but also fixed costs per unit.
tactical_explanations:
The price is the cover fee and variable costs. If you add the variable costs to the cover fee, you get back the original selling price. The reversal confirms that both parts are using the price. If one of the two is missing, the disassembly does not fit. The statement checks exactly this identity. If one of the two parts is missing, the price dissipation no longer fits.

The statement is true.

Sales times quota equals fixed costs at break-even. This sample confirms that the division of fixed costs through the quota delivers exactly the turnover, whose cover contributions meet fixed costs. If the product deviates, the threshold is wrongly calculated. The identity is the defining zero profit condition. If the product deviates, the break-even threshold is wrongly calculated.

The statement is true.

Zero profit means: cover contributions equal fixed costs. More not and no less. This applies regardless of whether the point is expressed by number of items or turnover. Below is no contribution, above is profit. The statement meets the defining property of the break-even point. Below is no contribution, above is profit from the surplus.

The statement is true.

Sales equal to fixed costs only at 100 percent quota. For each lower quota, turnover must be greater than the fixed costs themselves, so that the cover contributions reach them. The statement asserts independence from the quota and is therefore wrong. Without the quota, the denominator of the break-even formula is missing. Without the quota, the denominator of the break-even formula is completely missing.

The statement is false.

In the long term, the price must bear both cost blocks. The cover fee exists to finance fixed costs beyond the variable costs. If the price covers only the quantity costs permanently, fixed costs remain unpaid. Therefore, the livelihood guarantee requires the cover of both blocks. The statement holds this long-term rule.

The statement is true.

title: Right and wrong denominators in break-even math
context: Selling price 400 euros, variable costs 180 euros per unit, fixed costs 4 000 000 euros: Check which computing paths actually make break-even sales. Rate the following statements:
statements: Break-even sales can be calculated correctly by dividing the fixed costs by the unit gross margin and multiplying the result by the selling price.
Break-even sales can be calculated correctly by dividing the fixed costs by the coverage rate.
The coverage rate can be calculated correctly by dividing the selling price by the variable costs.
To obtain the coverage ratio, first calculate the coverage contribution as a price minus variable costs and then divide it by the price.
Break-even sales can be calculated correctly by dividing the fixed costs by the variable costs per piece.
tactical_explanations:
The number of units per price results in the revenue path. Fixed costs divided by unit gross margin are provided by the break-even unit number; multiplied by the selling price, the break-even turnover is generated in euros. Both steps together lead to the goal correctly. Anyone who omits one of the steps remains at a piece or at a wrong euro number.

The statement is true.

Direct way through the quota. Fixed costs divided by the coverage rate directly results in break-even sales, because at break-even point sales times quota equals fixed costs. This saves the detour by the number of units. The prerequisite is the correct quota from cover contribution and price. The statement states exactly this direct way.

The statement is true.

Price by variable costs is the wrong quota. This division measures how often the volume costs fit into the price, not the share of the cover contribution in the price. The coverage ratio is cover contribution divided by price. Whoever exchanges counters and denominators or takes the cost amount instead of the contribution misses the quota.

The statement is false.

First difference, then share. The cover contribution is generated as a price minus variable costs; divided by the price, the cover ratio is derived from it. This order provides the correct quota. Whoever exchanges the steps or chooses other denominators ends up with another measure. The statement describes the definition two-stage correctly.

The statement is true.

Variable costs are the wrong denominator. They are just deducted from the price to get the cover contribution that carries the fixed costs. The correct item number is the cover contribution, the correct sales number the cover rate. Who divides by 180 euros does not charge a break-even threshold. The statement chooses the cost block instead of the contribution.

The statement is false.

title: Break-even check and staying in business
context: A bicycle manufacturer knows the selling price of 400 euros, variable costs of 180 euros per unit and fixed costs of 4 000 000 euros per year. Rate the following statements about break-even test and the livelihood protection:
statements: Calculated in units (fixed costs divided by contribution per unit) and calculated in units (fixed costs divided by coverage rate, then by price) lead to the same break-even number of units.
If the contribution is confused with the variable costs per piece, the result is a false, too low coverage rate and thus a too high calculated break-even turnover.
A company should achieve at least so much turnover that all costs are covered; only then does the profit zone begin, which ensures its existence in the long term.
Because the fixed costs amount to 4 000 000 euros, break-even sales are also 4 000 000 euros, regardless of the coverage rate.
The break-even turnover is exactly the fixed costs after deduction of the variable costs; the profit is zero at this point.
tactical_explanations:
Both paths meet the same quantity. Fixed costs divided by unit gross margin and the detour via turnover (fixed costs by quota, then by price) are mathematically equivalent. The number of units in which the sum of contributions reaches the fixed costs is the same. Deviations signal calculation errors, no second truth.

The statement is true.

If the variable costs are wrongly put into the quota calculation counter instead of the cover contribution, a too low coverage rate is obtained. Because break-even turnover is equal to fixed costs divided by the coverage rate, a too low quota in the denominator leads to a too high calculated turnover.

The statement is true.

There is no room for existence under cost recovery. In the long term, an enterprise cannot exist if income does not cover the costs. The break-even point marks this minimum threshold; only turnover above it generates profit and financial leeway. The statement links threshold and long-term security correctly.

The statement is true.

Four million fixed costs are not automatically four million break-even sales. Only with a coverage rate of 100 percent would both be identical. With each lower quota the turnover must be greater. The equation ignores the quota completely and is therefore wrong. The denominator of the formula is missing in the assertion. The denominator of the formula is completely missing in the assertion.

The statement is false.

The amount of fixed costs remains exactly the fixed cost at break-even after volume costs. The contribution of the cover is equal to fixed costs; profit and loss are zero. Each additional turnover euro above this contributes to profit. This is the defining characteristic of the point. The statement describes precisely this zero profit situation. Each euro turnover above this then contributes to profit for the first time.

The statement is true.

title: Marketing is more than advertising
context: Evaluate the following statements on the concept of marketing:
statements: Marketing is the systematic orientation of the entire company, i.e. all operational areas, and its offer to the needs and wishes of the customers.
Marketing is mainly advertising and hardly affects the rest of the company.
If the market is produced by and the offer is not requested, the company cannot cover its costs, comes into payment difficulties and fails.
In a market economy, the orientation towards the market for corporate success is secondary, because demand is already adapting to the finished supply.
The popular assumption that marketing is above all advertising is too short.
tactical_explanations:
All areas, not just advertising. The theory defines marketing as a systematic orientation of the entire company, that is, all operational areas, and its offer to the needs and wishes of the customers. Planning, production, price, distribution and sale are among them. Anyone who narrows marketing on posters and spots describes exactly the common assumption that contradicts the theory. Without this orientation on customer wishes, the offer remains a random product. Those who only surround the communication department and leave production and sales untouched, have not yet oriented the entire company market-oriented and therefore does not meet the definition.

The statement is true.

Advertising alone does not bear the term. The popular assumption that marketing is mainly about advertising is expressly rejected. Marketing is the systematic orientation of the whole company and its offer to customer needs. Advertising messages are later only part of the communication policy. A company that only advertises but produces by the market does not cover its costs. The restriction on advertising makes the sentence wrong.

The statement is false.

Failure to demand is a consequence of payment problems. If a company is producing by the market and if its supply is not demanded, it cannot cover its costs, comes into payment difficulties and fails. In a market economy organized, market orientation therefore decides on survival, not the good will of production. Anyone who denies the link between lack of demand and failure is contradicting this chain.

The statement is true.

The market is not waiting for the finished warehouse. The orientation on the market is crucial for a company in a market economy. If the offer does not fit to demand and wish, it remains lying, the costs remain unmet. The idea that demand is already adapting to what was built internally reverses logic: first clarify customer needs, then align supply. The theory does not assert the marginality of market orientation.

The statement is false.

The short-circuit advertising equal to marketing does not hold. Contrary to the popular assumption that it is mainly about advertising, marketing is the systematic orientation of the entire company and its offer to the customer. Advertising remains a small part of the communication policy. The sentence meets precisely this correction without declaring advertising unimportant.

The statement is true.

title: Tasks of successful marketing
context: Evaluate the following statements on the tasks of successful marketing:
statements: For successful marketing, a company must find out what existing and potential future customers need and wish for.
The offer may be determined internally independently of the determined customer wishes.
Once the product is finished, communication of the benefit can be dispensed with, because good goods sell themselves.
The prices must be designed in such a way that customers can and want to ask the offer.
Whether the offer is available at the right place at the right time does not matter for successful marketing.
tactical_explanations:
Existing and future customers both count. Successful marketing starts by finding out what existing and potential future customers need and want. Market research provides basic information for this. Anyone who asks only today's regular buyers and hides potential buyer groups shortens the first task. The clarification of requirements is the starting point, not an optional addition after production. Without this clarification, price, location and message remain blind flight, because no one knows whose demand the offer should meet.

The statement is true.

Internally, the order of the order of the order of the order of the order of the order of the order of the demand is broken. After the clarification of the needs the offer of the company is to be planned accordingly. A program, which is decided internally independently of the determined wishes, is the production of the market. Planning follows the needs, not the other way around.

The statement is false.

Unknown goods remain in stock. The successful marketing includes communicating the offer and benefits of the customer so that they can learn about it. The bicycle example clearly says: the wheels are good and affordable, but nobody knows them, because nowhere is this pointed out, is also little sold. The claim that communication is superfluous once quality is right contradicts this step.

The statement is false.

Price must enable demand. Prices must be designed in such a way that customers can and want to ask for the offer. If they cannot bear the price or if they do not want to pay it, the product that is otherwise suitable remains. Pricing is therefore a task of its own in successful marketing, not just an internal cost accounting without a view of the willingness to pay.

The statement is true.

The right place and time are part of the task. Successful marketing organises that the offer is available at the right place at the right time. Distribution is crucial because a right product cannot be sold at the wrong place. Anyone who explains availability as a minor matter will remove this fifth point. Without the appropriate sales route, the benefits remain theoretical.

The statement is false.

title: Four areas and the product concept
context: Evaluate the following statements on market-oriented questions and product in marketing:
statements: The marketing measures relate in particular to product and range policy, price and conditions policy, distribution policy and communication policy.
In marketing, only tangible goods such as a bicycle or a packerl of crystal sugar are considered as a product.
Services, organizations, campaigns, ideas, people and places can be marketed and are considered a product in marketing.
A gym, tax consultancy firm or tutoring institute do not operate marketing because they do not produce tangible goods.
If you offer advice, training and ongoing support for a product, the product covers both the cause itself and the related services in the sense of marketing.
tactical_explanations:
Four questions are combined with the measures. What is offered, at what price, where and with which message to whom: exactly this is the case with the marketing measures in particular, in the language of the book Product, Price, Place and Promotion. Product range and assortment, prices and conditions, sales organization as well as advertising, sales promotion and public relations work are included. Those who only consider one of these blocks marketing shortens market-oriented questions. Market research provides the basic information for precisely these four questions, so that the areas are not decided independently of each other.

The statement is true.

In the marketing language, not only vulnerable things such as a bicycle or a packerl of crystal sugar are called products. Services, organizations, campaigns, ideas, people and places can be marketed and are also considered as products. The restriction on goods that can be taken into your hands contradicts this extension. A tutoring institute then markets a product as well as a wheel manufacturer.

The statement is false.

The extended product term is explicit. Services, organizations, campaigns, ideas, people and places can be marketed and are considered as products in marketing. Aid organizations, parties, initiatives, cities, regions and countries therefore operate marketing. The statement is a list of books without explaining any topic already as a marketed product; it is crucial that it is an offer that is tailored to needs.

The statement is true.

Service providers are not outside. A service company such as a gym, a tax consultancy firm or a tutoring institute also operates marketing. The examples are in theory precisely because marketing is not bound to the production of tangible goods. Anyone who discusses marketing for these companies will reverse the extension of the product term.

The statement is false.

Additional services are part of the marketed bundle. Around a product offering advice, training and ongoing support means that the product includes both the product itself and the related services in terms of marketing. Product and product range policy therefore also refers to additional services, not only to the core object. A wheel without training can then be a different marketed product than the same wheel with support.

The statement is true.

title: Price, distribution and communication
context: Evaluate the following statements on pricing, distribution and communication policy:
statements: In addition to the price level, the price and conditions policy also includes discounts, promotions and special prices as well as delivery and payment conditions.
Especially in the case of food, many buyers mainly take advantage of the most favourable offer.
A correct product in the wrong place can still be sold reliably, because the distribution is subordinate.
Advertising is only a small part of the entire marketing of a company.
Communication policy is limited to classic advertising and excludes promotion and public relations.
tactical_explanations:
Conditions are more than the list amount. Marketing measures in the price area refer to the amount and design of the prices, discounts, promotions and special prices as well as to delivery and payment conditions. Who thinks only the final amount on the sign as price policy, leaves off discount, action and payment destination, although it explicitly includes them. The willingness to pay often depends precisely on these conditions. An action price without a payment target or a list price without a discount policy would therefore be only a section of the same price and conditions policy.

The statement is true.

Food purchase often follows the most favourable offer. With many products, customers mainly respond to the price. Especially for food, many buyers mainly resort to the most favourable offer; the willingness to pay more for a high-quality product is often limited. The sentence hits this book observation without claiming quality plays no role anywhere.

The statement is true.

The distribution policy organises the sales so that products can reach customers, for example via wholesale and retail, Internet, stores, franchising or sales representatives. Distribution is crucial, because even a real product in the wrong place cannot be sold. Subordination of the sales route contradicts exactly this sentence.

The statement is false.

Advertising does not carry the whole marketing. Communication policy includes advertising, promotion and public relations. Advertising is therefore only a small part of the entire marketing. This follows the definition that marketing is the orientation of the whole company, not the sum of the ads. The sentence holds this weighting.

The statement is true.

The communication policy refers to advertising, sales promotion and public relations. Those who exclude sales promotion and public relations work leave two of the three mentioned blocks away. Classical advertising remains a part, not the whole message policy. The restriction makes the sentence wrong.

The statement is false.

title: Market orientation across the whole firm
context: A bicycle manufacturer directs offer, price, distribution and advice to parents and children. Rate the following statements:
statements: Some understand marketing not only as a management process, but as a philosophy for the entire company, which is oriented towards the market and the business environment.
Marketing concerns exclusively the advertising department and leaves planning, development, production, distribution and sale unaffected.
If bicycles are produced that do not please parents or children, do not drive well, are too expensive or are only cumbersomely available, the company cannot sell its products.
If the wheels are good and affordable, they will also sell reliably when no one is pointed out to them.
The marketing measures should not only be used in a case or phase manner, but also systematically coordinated with each other.
tactical_explanations:
Philosophy extends beyond the process. Marketing affects many business areas, from the planning and development of the offer to production to distribution and sales. Some also see it as a philosophy for the entire company, which is oriented towards the market and the business environment in its actions. The sentence represents exactly this second reading without deleting the process view.

The statement is true.

Marketing is affected from design to sale. Marketing of a company concerns many areas, from the planning and development of the offer, production to distribution and sale. An isolation on the advertising department contradicts this breadth. Anyone who excludes production and sales treats marketing again only as advertising.

The statement is false.

If the manufacturer does not adapt to the needs of parents and children, the sales will fail: wheels that do not like, do not ride well, are too expensive or are only cumbersomely available, cannot be sold. The example bundles product, price and distribution. The sentence hits the book scene without insulating every single feature as the sole exclusion criterion; together they make the sale unlikely. If one of these links is missing, good will in the workshop is not enough: the market then does not lose the wheel, the costs remain uncovered.

The statement is true.

Invisible quality remains invisible. Although the products are good and affordable, nobody knows them, because they are not mentioned anywhere, little is sold. Communication of the benefit is part of successful marketing. The claim that notice is superfluous as soon as quality and price are right contradicts the example.

The statement is false.

Coordination is a permanent task. The measures should not only be used in a case or phase manner, but should be used systematically in a coordinated manner. This coordination is not always easy; data from market research help to make the right decisions. Those who only provide for campaign islands without ongoing coordination miss this demand.

The statement is true.

title: Aligning product, price, place and message
context: A high-quality bicycle should be perceived as exclusive and high-quality. Rate the following statements:
statements: A high price is interpreted by many buyers as an indicator of quality and exclusivity.
If the bike is too cheap, many will doubt the quality or no longer consider it exclusive.
If the bike is too expensive, potential buyers may still buy another bike.
If you offer the high-quality bike in many, even not so specialized shops, the exclusivity remains untouched.
Product and price must be well coordinated, as must the place of availability and marketing message.
tactical_explanations:
Price often signals quality. A high-quality bicycle has a high price because production was expensive and quality is high; comparable wheels are similar. A high price is interpreted by many buyers as an indicator of quality and exclusivity. The sentence holds this interpretation, without claiming that every high price is already earned. Signal and actual quality must fit together. If the price is well below comparable high-quality wheels, exactly this signal tilts, although the product itself was produced expensively.

The statement is true.

Too cheaply undermines the quality suspicion positive. If the wheel is too cheap, many will doubt the quality or no longer consider it exclusive. The price must fit the product, otherwise the perception will tilt. A dumping price for a supposedly high-quality wheel contradicts the coordination of product and price. Exactly these doubts describe the theory.

The statement is true.

If the wheel is too expensive, potential buyers may still buy another wheel. High price as a quality indicator therefore has a limit in the willingness to pay. Therefore, the product and price must be well coordinated. The sentence reflects this danger.

The statement is true.

Wide dispersion is a little more exclusive. If you offer the bike in many, even not so specialized shops, to reach as many customers as possible, it is no longer considered exclusive. The location of the sales contributes to the positioning. If you claim that exclusivity remains unaffected, this example is ignored. Specialist shops and mass shelves send different signals. Those who want to keep exclusivity must also consider the sales path; mass shelves and specialist shops do not send the same quality promise.

The statement is false.

Four adjusting screws must fit together. Product and price must be well coordinated, as well as the place where the product is available and the message with which it is marketed. Advertising and other sales promotion measures should arouse the desire to buy exactly this wheel and no other. Isolated optimization of a size destroys the coordination.

The statement is true.

title: Goals of marketing measures
context: Evaluate the following statements on marketing objectives:
statements: Most marketing measures aim to reach the target group, that is, the people you want to address with the offer.
A common goal is a high level of awareness and a positive image, if necessary an image correction.
Possible marketing goals are to keep existing customers and attract new customers.
Keeping or increasing sales and covering costs or achieving profit are not among the potential marketing goals.
The share of the total market can be held or increased with held and won customers.
tactical_explanations:
The target group is the common core. The objectives of marketing are diverse. Together, most measures are intended to reach the target group, that is, the people you want to reach and address with the offer. Spreading without this group of people misses the common denominator. The sentence represents this book formulation. Measures that remain attached to completely different persons can spread awareness and still miss the target group.

The statement is true.

Awareness and image are among the common goals. In addition to reaching the target group, the common goals call for a high level of awareness and positive perception or an image correction. Anyone who only allows sales figures as a target, leaves this block away. Awareness without a positive image would be incomplete; correction presupposes that the previous image does not fit. Image correction requires that the previous image of the target group does not match the offer; awareness alone does not cure a negative image. To be seen positively and to be known are therefore two connected but not identical goals of the same measures.

The statement is true.

Holding and winning are side by side. Other possible marketing goals are to keep existing customers and win new customers. Both are aimed at the customer base, not just for one-time first purchases. Those who only count new customers and ignore regular customers, or vice versa, shorten the list. The sentence hits both sides.

The statement is true.

Sales and cost recovery are on the same list. Other possible goals are to keep or increase sales and thus at least cover costs or generate profits. The claim that these sizes were not among the marketing targets, strikes this continuation. Market orientation is to bear in the end economic, not only send messages.

The statement is false.

The customer base supports the market share. Existing customers are supposed to hold and gain new shares in the overall market or even increase. Market share here is the bridge between customer work and position in the overall market. The sentence follows this chain of the book without declaring market share as the only goal.

The statement is true.

title: Marketing concept and customer satisfaction
context: Evaluate the following statements on the marketing concept:
statements: A comprehensive marketing concept is based on the market, defines precisely formulated goals and coordinates all market orientation measures, in particular product, price, place and promotion.
Such a concept should lead to customer satisfaction, which is the prerequisite for corporate success.
A marketing concept does not need defined goals as long as any measures are being taken.
Customer satisfaction is not relevant to the company's success according to theory.
The concept is developed to achieve the marketing goals.
tactical_explanations:
Market, objectives and the four areas are all together. A comprehensive marketing concept is developed to achieve the marketing goals. It is oriented towards the market, defines precisely formulated goals and coordinates all measures within the company that serve the market orientation, in particular product, price, place and promotion. If one of these elements is missing, the concept is not the comprehensive one described. Coordination means coordination, not parallel individual actions. If coordination is missing, a high price and a mass distribution can contradict each other, although each instrument has a sound basis for itself.

The statement is true.

Satisfaction is the key to success. Such a concept should lead to customer satisfaction, which is the prerequisite for corporate success. Without fulfilling needs, sales will remain fragile, even if sales are generated at short notice. The sentence establishes the book link: concept, satisfaction, success. Satisfaction is a condition here, not just a soft extra. Dissatisfied buyers do not bear repeat purchases or the market share that the further marketing goals aim for.

The statement is true.

Without goals, the core of the concept is missing. The concept defines precisely formulated goals and is developed to achieve the marketing goals. Measures without this definition are not a comprehensive marketing concept in the sense of the book. Any activity does not replace market orientation or coordination of the four areas. The sentence precisely cuts the target function.

The statement is false.

Success depends on satisfaction. Customer satisfaction is explicitly the prerequisite for corporate success. Unimportantness would deny this requirement. The concept should lead to this, because dissatisfied customers do not carry the offer. The sentence reverses the book relationship.

The statement is false.

The aim is to create a comprehensive marketing concept to achieve the marketing objectives. It is not an end in itself, but an objective in addition to the objectives. Orientation on the market and coordination of the measures serve the same purpose. The sentence takes this purpose.

The statement is true.

title: The market concept in marketing
context: Evaluate the following statements on the market and market research:
statements: In general, the market refers to the combination of supply and demand for a particular commodity.
In marketing, market means the sum of the persons and/or companies who have a need that can be met with the product offered.
Market in marketing includes only those persons who have already purchased the product.
Market research provides basic information on market-oriented issues.
The market is a side-effect for the marketing measures.
tactical_explanations:
General definition remains supply meets demand. While the market generally refers to the combination of supply and demand for a particular good, marketing uses a narrower, need-based term. The sentence captures the general side. Without supply and demand, this market concept would not exist; it is the starting point before the marketing language reformulated.

The statement is true.

Marketing counts for providers, not just transactions. Market means the sum of people and/or companies who have a need that can be met with the product offered. This includes those who are not yet buying, but whose need would be met. This is exactly what the market potential builds on later. The sentence reflects this definition.

The statement is true.

The marketing sum includes persons and companies with a need to meet, not just previous buyers. Market potential makes it clear how large the market would be if everyone actually bought with this need; this requires non-buyers in the market concept.

If you limit the market to past purchases, you confuse market volume with the other market in marketing.

Note: Market volume is the quantity actually sold; market in marketing is wider. Market potential is precisely expected by those demand carriers who do not yet buy; those who remove it from the market concept cannot distinguish saturation from unused leeway.

The statement is false.

Market research feeds the four questions. A company is oriented to market-oriented questions for which market research provides the basic information. Without these data, the coordination of the measures remains uncertain. The sentence takes the auxiliary function without the market research equates with the whole marketing.

The statement is true.

The market is essential for the orientation of the marketing measures. Adversely, this sentence and the whole market orientation contradicts. Objectives, concept and indicators presuppose that it is clear which market is meant. Whoever cuts the market leaves the measures without a reference point.

The statement is false.

title: Market potential and market volume
context: Evaluate the following statements on market potential and market volume:
statements: The market potential is the maximum possible sales volume of a product.
The market volume is the actual quantity sold of the product.
If the market volume is close to market potential, the market is almost saturated.
Market potential and market volume are the same because each demand carrier is already buying.
Saturated markets are often turned into unsaturated markets by changing products or by responding to new layers of buyers.
tactical_explanations:
Maximum of all conceivable purchases. The market potential is the maximum possible sales quantity of a product. It makes clear how large a market would be if all persons and/or companies who have a need that could be met with the product would actually buy this product. The size is thus a cap, not a booked actual quantity. If you equate potential with today's sales, you miss this maximum. If the volume is significantly lower, there is room; if it is close to that, there is hardly any additional sales in the existing market.

The statement is true.

The market volume measures the actual quantity of the product sold, not the theoretical maximum. The difference to the market potential shows unused scope. Anyone who exchanges volume and potential is confused and capped. The statement holds the actual size. The difference to the potential shows the unused scope only.

The statement is true.

Close gap means saturation. If the market volume is close to market potential, no additional sales on the same vehicle are possible. Almost all achievable buyers then buy. A wide gap would mean unsaturated. Closeness of the two sizes is the saturation signal. A wide gap between both sizes would, on the other hand, mean unsaturated.

The statement is true.

Equality is the limit case, not the rule. Potential is the maximum quantity, volume the actual. They only coincide if really everyone with a fulfilling need buy. The claim that they are always the same amount because each demand carrier already buys sets saturation as the normal case. To separate the terms are precisely because this often does not apply.

The statement is false.

New models or new layers open the market. Often, saturated markets are tried to turn into unsaturated markets through changed products or by responding to new layers of buyers, for example by new models with new functions. Then the relevant potential or demand increases above the previous volume. The sentence reflects this strategy. New functions or new age groups shift, who has a fulfilling need, and thus the gap between volume and potential.

The statement is true.

title: Sales potential, sales volume and market share
context: Evaluate the following statements on business-related sales indicators:
statements: The sales or sales potential of an undertaking is that of a sales volume which the undertaking can or hopes to achieve in the best case.
The volume of sales or sales is the sales of an undertaking for a particular product or group of products.
The market share of a company for a product can be determined in terms of quantity or value.
The sales potential and volume of a company are conceptually the same size.
The sales potential of woom GmbH is the sales volume of bicycles that it can ideally sell.
tactical_explanations:
The best case of the company's own quantity. The sales or sales potential of a company for a product or group of products is that quantity of sales that the company can reach or hopes to achieve in the best case possible. This is the company-related upper limit, not the market potential of all suppliers. Hope and best case are the ones that mark that this is not the already realized sales. Market potential remains the upper limit of all suppliers; the sales potential of a company may be lower than that, because not every company can serve the entire market.

The statement is true.

The sales volume or sales volume is the sales volume of a company for a particular product or product group. It corresponds at the company level to what the market volume is at market level: the actual sales volume, here only of the one operation. The rate separates this actual size from the potential.

The statement is true.

The market share of a company for a product can be determined in terms of quantity or value. Thus, the units and sales can bear the same share idea, but at different prices they lead to different percentages. The theory allows both paths. Whoever acknowledges only one of the two types of calculations shortens the measure.

The statement is true.

The best case and the best case fall apart. Potential is the quantity in the best case or the desired quantity, volume of the actual sales. They would only be the same size if the best case had already been fully realized. The conceptual equation strikes the difference that the theory draws with two terms. woom can ideally sell more wheels than it currently sells. woom can ideally sell more wheels than in the current year, which is exactly why two key figures stand side by side.

The statement is false.

woom illustrates the best case. The sales potential is the quantity that the company can ideally sell, not the current sales. The example makes the company-related ceiling concrete. Between potential and actual volume lies its own growth margin. The statement is precisely this best case size. Between potential and actual volume lies the own room for growth.

The statement is true.

title: Absolute and relative market share
context: A bicycle manufacturer is implementing 15 million euros, the market volume is 100 million euros, the largest competitor is implementing 30 million euros. Evaluate the following statements:
statements: The absolute market share indicates the share of the company's turnover in the market volume and is calculated as the enterprise's turnover by 100 times divided by the market volume.
The relative market share is related to the turnover of the largest competitor.
A relative market share greater than one indicates that the company is the market leader.
In the case of figures, the absolute market share is 15 percent.
In the case of figures, the relative market share is 2, so the company is the market leader.
tactical_explanations:
Formula binds sales to market volume. The absolute market share indicates the share of the company's sales in market volume. Computerized: company turnover times 100, divided by market volume. Thus, a percentage of the entire actual market is created, not a comparison only with a rival. Those who set the biggest competitor in the denominator already calculate the relative share and miss the absolute formula.

The statement is true.

The relative market share is the relative turnover of the company in relation to the turnover of the largest competitor. Denominator is therefore not the market volume, but the strongest rival. This creates a characteristic of the ranking, not a percentage of the total market. The rate meets this relation.

The statement is true.

A relative market share greater than one indicates that the company is the market leader because its own turnover exceeds that of the largest competitor so far. One equals the largest, one below the other means a gap. The threshold one is the book rule for leadership in this figure.

The statement is true.

Fifteen by one hundred times one hundred. Absolute market share = company turnover × 100 / market volume = 15 × 100 / 100 = 15. The manufacturer therefore holds 15 percent of the value of the market volume. 15 divided by 30 would be a different bill and relate to the relative share. The 15 percent follow only from sales and volume.

The statement is true.

Fifteen by thirty is half. Relative market share = enterprise turnover / turnover of the largest competitor = 15/30 = 0.5. This is smaller than one, so no market leader. The claim that the relative share is 2, twists counters and denominators (30 / 15 = 2 would be the advantage of the rival).

0.5 shows a gap from the largest, although 15 percent are already a significant chunk in volume.

Note: Absolutely 15 percent and relatively 0.5 can coincide; one number does not replace the other. Absolutely 15 percent describe the chunk at the total volume; relatively 0.5 describes the gap to the greatest. Both numbers are needed because one does not replace the other.

The statement is false.

title: Market segmentation
context: Evaluate the following statements on the division of the market into groups of buyers:
statements: It is usually not useful to develop products for the overall market and to operate marketing for each product in all markets.
The market is divided into groups of buyers, which include persons with common features, such as age, income or consumption habits.
Through segmentation, product development, prices, sales channels and advertising can be more targeted.
Target groups are exclusively the persons who ask for and buy products.
The needs and purchasing behaviour of the different buyer groups are so similar that a division is unnecessary.
tactical_explanations:
The needs and purchasing behaviour of the different groups of buyers are very different. Therefore, it is usually not useful to develop products for the overall market and to operate marketing for each product on all markets. Undifferentiated dispersion misses the differences. The sentence reflects this initial criticism. A children's bike for all age and income groups at the same time would fail due to these differences, so you share the market. More targeted prices and sales routes presuppose that you have formed these groups before.

The statement is true.

The market is divided into buyer groups (target groups), segmented. Each group includes persons with common features in particular characteristics, such as age, income, consumption habits. Homogeneity refers to these characteristics, not to the complete identity of all persons. The sentence meets definition and examples.

The statement is true.

More targeted instruments follow the division. This allows the product development, prices, sales channels and advertising to be more targeted. Segmentation is therefore a means of more appropriate market processing, not an end in itself. Without division, the four areas remain coarse. The sentence holds this benefit.

The statement is true.

The target group is not only the people who ask and buy products, but also those who influence the purchase decision, or those who do not buy but then use the product. The restriction to demanders and buyers removes influencers and users. Children and parents count differently, especially for children's bicycles. Parents pay, use children, recommend friends: three roles that the theory explicitly brings into the target circle.

The statement is false.

Differences are the reason for division. Needs and purchasing behaviour are very different, so they segment. The claim that the groups are so similar that division is unnecessary, reverses the book premises. Uniform marketing for the overall market would then be the rejected solution again.

The statement is false.

title: Target groups beyond buyers
context: Parents buy a children's bike, the child drives it, friends recommend the model. Rate the following statements:
statements: People who influence the purchase decision can also be part of the target group of marketing activities.
People who do not buy but use the product can also be part of the target group.
Only those who pay the purchase price are eligible as target groups.
The child who uses the bike without paying for it can be a target group.
Because friends can influence the decision, the company can dispense with any segmentation and work on all markets equally.
tactical_explanations:
The circle of influencers is not only the demander and the buyer, but also the ones who influence the purchase decision. Friends who recommend a model belong to this wider circle. Marketing, which only sees the paying person, fails to provide recommendations that trigger the purchase. The sentence follows the book extension. A campaign that only the paying person sees leaves out recommendations and user requests, although they trigger the purchase. It is called buyers, influencers and users side by side, not as ranking in which only the paying person counts.

The statement is true.

The benefit without purchase remains relevant. The target group also includes those who do not buy, but then use the product. Satisfaction and desire often arise with the user, while another person pays. Anyone who hides users, plans to use it. The sentence holds this second extension.

The statement is true.

The book list lists buyers, influencers and users. Only the purchase price to allow paying persons, scraps two of the three roles. Parents pay, use children, influence friends: all three can be target group. The narrowing on the payers makes the sentence wrong.

The statement is false.

The child rides the bike while the parents buy and pay. Product design and message must therefore not ignore the user role. Target group includes more than just the paying person. The scene consciously separates buyers and users. Buyer role and user role are to be consciously separated in the target group.

The statement is true.

Several roles do not replace the division. Different buyer groups remain the reason to segment. That friends influence, expands the target group, but does not cancel the statement that it is usually not useful to advertise for the overall market and in all markets alike. Doing without segmentation contradicts market processing in three phases. Segmentation remains necessary because age, income and consumption habits continue to form groups with different purchasing behaviour.

The statement is false.

title: Three phases of market cultivation
context: Evaluate the following statements on the phases of target group-oriented marketing:
statements: The first phase will segment the market, the second will determine which market segments will be processed, and the third will place the company's offer on this target market.
The offer is positioned before the market segmentation.
Positioning describes how the product is seen or to be seen by consumers in terms of important properties.
After segmentation, the company will necessarily process each segment formed, and no selection will take place.
The target market on which it is positioned is determined by the selection of the segments to be processed.
tactical_explanations:
Three steps in a fixed sequence. Target group-oriented marketing takes place in three phases: first the market is segmented, then the market segment is determined, then the company positions its offer on this target market. Selection follows the division, positioning follows the selection. Who turns the order misses the phase scheme. If you skip the selection, you position yourself in the unfiltered overall market and miss the meaning of the second phase. Only after this episode did the company make sense of a target market, which makes sense to the target group.

The statement is true.

Without segments, the target market is missing. Positioning is the third phase and requires that segments are formed and selected for processing. Before segmentation, there would be no such specific target market for the offer. The claim that positioning comes first, reverses the scheme. Image and distinctiveness aim at a group that has already been chosen. An image in the heads without clarified segments remains undirected, because it is unclear whose perception is to be designed.

The statement is false.

The positioning of the product on the market describes how the product is seen or is to be seen by consumers in terms of important characteristics. The target and actual image are both included. It is about the consumer's view, not just about internal characteristic lists. The sentence meets this definition.

The statement is true.

Phase two is selection, not automatic. In the second phase, it is defined which market segments are to be processed. This includes that not every segment is to be edited. Compulsory processing of all segments is precisely this determination. Resources and matching control the selection.

The statement is false.

The segment selection creates the target market. After deciding which segments are processed, the company positions on this target market. The target market is the result of the second phase, not the unfiltered overall market. Phase three builds on this selection. The statement correctly closes the phase sequence. Phase three builds on this segment selection, not on the overall market.

The statement is true.

title: Positioning and unique selling proposition
context: Woom GmbH wants to stand out with particularly suitable for children, high-quality bicycles that last long. Rate the following statements:
statements: The product should stand out clearly and distinctively from the competition and be particularly desirable for the target group.
The product is to obtain a unique selling proposition.
For Woom GmbH, Unique Selling Proposition is particularly suitable for children with high quality bicycles that last long.
A unique selling proposition means that the product is identical to the competing products in all its features.
Positioning and Unique Selling Proposition aim at perception in the selected target group, not at any image in the overall market.
tactical_explanations:
The product should stand out clearly and distinctively from the competition and be particularly desirable for the target group. Together, the desired position results in the selection of the target market. Taking off without the target group would remain empty, desire without difference would remain interchangeable. The sentence holds both requirements. Child fitness without distinction to competition would be interchangeable; difference without wish of the target group would remain technical supplement.

The statement is true.

USP calls the distinctive advantage. The product is to obtain a unique selling proposition, that is exactly the distinctive position that sets it apart from the competition and makes it particularly desirable for the target group. The English expression is in theory the goal of positioning. Without USP, the offer remains interchangeable.

The statement is true.

woom is the USP's concrete feature. For woom GmbH, Unique Selling Proposition is a particularly suitable high-quality bicycle that lasts long. Child fitness, quality and durability bundle the difference that parents and children should seek. The sentence gives the example without excluding other manufacturers; it is the formulated USP of this company.

The statement is true.

Identity with the competition would be the opposite. Unmistakably distinguishable does not mean being identical in all characteristics. A unique selling proposition requires the difference that the target group sees as an advantage. Full identity made positioning superfluous. The sentence reverses the definition.

The statement is false.

Positioning describes how the product is seen or to be seen by consumers, and the product should be particularly desirable for the target group. After the three phases, this is the chosen target market, not an arbitrary picture for all. woom formulates the USP for children-friendly wheels, not for the entire two-wheeled market without difference. The set connects phase three with the USP. Whoever pushes the USP into the overall market without selected segments, treats each product in all markets the same, although it usually rejects it.

The statement is true.

title: Core benefit and additional benefit
context: A household buys a bicycle. Rate the following statements for the benefit of the product:
statements: If you buy something, you expect that the purchased will have a benefit.
The basic benefit of a bicycle is driving, the primary purpose of the product.
Additional benefits mean only the same primary purpose as the basic benefit.
The benefits of the wheel can be to afford a particular wheel.
Experience benefits can be that driving is fun or the bike is particularly safe.
tactical_explanations:
Buying is not an end in itself. The section begins with the fact that anyone who buys something expects the purchased to have a benefit. In the notebook, this is the installation and use of programs, for example, for which work can occur anywhere, light weight or a nice look. Product development and subsequent marketing must consider these benefits precisely, otherwise an offer will be created that no one needs. Without expected benefits there would be no reason to pay the price. The sentence holds exactly this expectation, which precedes the theory of product policy.

The statement is true.

Driving is the core, not the prestige. Tab. 6 describes as the basic benefit the primary purpose of the product and explicitly indicates when riding a bicycle. Everything else, meaning or experience, is an added benefit. Anyone who confuses the basic benefit with a beautiful varnish or with the impression that you can afford the bike, exchanges the two levels. They are conscious of separating: first the purpose, then the benefit beyond.

The statement is true.

Addition means, not the same purpose again. Added value is the benefit beyond the basic benefit. Benefits of validity and experience are the two forms mentioned. Reducing the added value to the same primary purpose makes two categories one. Then prestige would be the same as driving, and the table would have no meaning. This is precisely the same equation that contradicts the distinction in the text of the teaching.

The statement is false.

Prestige is hanging on the wheel that you can afford. It is explicitly mentioned as a value for value that a particular bike can afford. This is not the basic benefit of driving, but a signal to the outside: it is shown that this model is within its own framework. Product policy must think about such added value when it plans to design and market. The sentence hits the first of the two additional categories, not a freely invented third.

The statement is true.

Fun and safety are beyond mere moving. Experience benefits describe the theory with two examples: It is fun to ride with it, or it is a particularly safe bike. Both require driving, but go beyond the primary purpose. Anyone who only lets the basic benefit apply, exactly this second additional form is removed. The product policy should have customer benefits in mind overall, reason and addition together.

The statement is true.

title: Four instruments from product policy to communication
context: Evaluate the following statements on product, price, distribution and communication policy:
statements: Product policy is part of the marketing mix and concerns the offer that needs to be of benefit to customers.
Price policy determines, among other things, the price and the payment conditions.
Distribution policy deals with how the product comes to the customer, i.e. the way in which it is sold.
Communication policy includes advertising, promotion and public relations.
Of the four areas of the teaching text, only advertising is important; price, location and product design are not part of the mix.
tactical_explanations:
The product is not a product policy, but a product itself, and later on price, sales route and message are added. Product policy is not a decoration, but a product itself, and the product itself is a product that is not a product that is not a product's product.
