If you remove the product policy from the mix, you will leave the first of the four blocks with which the section handles the mix and will no longer be able to properly coordinate the other instruments.

The statement is true.

The price policy is based on a policy of high prices and low prices or discount prices; in addition, the payment conditions are important. So it is not only a question of a number on the price tag, but also of how to pay. The three factors cost, competitive price and willingness to pay control the fixing. The sentence remains on this level and does not invent its own price technique, which the theory does not call.

The statement is true.

The distribution policy tries to answer two questions: how the product comes to the customer, which means how the sales route is to be designed, and which transport route is to be chosen. Place means the way of the goods, not the company headquarters. Direct and indirect sales, trade and franchising are manifestations of this very question. If you confuse distribution with the address of the central office, miss the section.

The statement is true.

Advertising is the entry, not the whole list. Communication policy includes advertising, besides the internet presence, sales promotion, personal selling and public relations including sponsorship and investor relations. Promotion is therefore broader than an advertisement. The sentence mentions three of the explicitly listed fields and thus remains within the text without prejudgeting social media details that follow later.

The statement is true.

Four blocks, not one. The mix part divides product policy, pricing policy, distribution policy and communication policy one after the other. Advertising is only a part of communication, and communication is only one of the four areas. The claim that only advertising counts and price, location and product design did not belong to it, overturns the structure. Those who reduce the mix to ads can explain neither the benefits nor the life cycle nor the sales path and price.

The statement is false.

title: Introduction stage in the life cycle
context: Evaluate the following statements on the introduction phase of a new product:
statements: The introduction phase introduces the new product on the market with various advertising measures.
If the product is successful and in demand, sales will increase slowly in the initial phase.
Because development and advertising costs are high, profit is already achieved on the first day of sales.
Profit is only achieved towards the end of the implementation phase.
If the product is not successful at this stage, it will disappear sooner rather than later from the market.
tactical_explanations:
Introduction means creating visibility. The new product comes on the market with various advertising measures. Without this introduction, potential buyers would often not know that the offer exists. The section connects the phase to advertising, not to silent delivery without communication. Anyone who reads the introductory phase as pure production without a market presence leaves away exactly this advertising effort, which the theory later also calls a cost-response for late profit. Development plus introduction advertising are high, therefore profit is not on day one, but only towards the end of this phase, if demand arises at all.

The statement is true.

Slowly, not abruptly. Sales in this phase are slowly increasing in terms of success and demand. This is the typical curve before the strong growth phase. Anyone who reads the maximum turnover of the maturity phase here already mixes two stages. The slow increase explains why the high introductory expenditures push the profit backwards: The curve does not carry the preliminary costs immediately. If the success is not achieved, the strong phase does not come at all.

The statement is true.

Costs are at the beginning, profit is not. The costs for product development and advertising expenditure of the introduction are high. Therefore, only towards the end of the introduction phase profit is achieved, not on the first day of sales. The absolute early claim ignores exactly this cost burden. A company that expects profit on day one did not understand the logic of the phase described.

The statement is false.

Towards the end, not at the beginning. Because development and introduction advertising are expensive, the profit is only towards the end of the introduction phase. Before that, sales can increase slowly, but they do not cover the preliminary costs. The sentence indicates the time shift, which the teaching text explicitly sets. Those who shift the profit to the middle of the growth phase leave the introductory phase.

The statement is true.

No success, short life. If the product is not successful in the initial phase, it disappears sooner rather than later from the market again. It does not enter the growth phase. The phrase "more sooner than later" comes from the theory and warns against artificially extending a failed introduction. Product elimination can follow before maturity or saturation occurs at all.

The statement is true.

title: Growth stage and imitators
context: Evaluate the following statements on the growth phase in the product life cycle:
statements: In the growth phase, sales are rising strongly and profits are also increasing.
In this phase, competition becomes increasingly aware of the product.
Imitation on the market is unlikely in the growth phase.
Pricing is crucial in the growth phase to expand market position.
In the growth phase, sales already reach their maximum, while profits are already falling.
tactical_explanations:
Strong rather than slow. If the product is successful, it will be a growth phase: Sales will rise strongly and profits will increase with them. This distinguishes the phase from the introduction, in which the increase was slow and profit will only come about late. Anyone who confuses growth with the shrinking market of saturation will read the curve backwards. Sales and profits are growing together before maturity pushes profit again, although sales there still reach its maximum. Imitation and pricing policy already belong in this growth stage, not only in degeneration.

The statement is true.

Visibility attracts competitors. Now the competition is increasingly alert to the product. Success is not only a curve of its own, but a signal to other suppliers. This is precisely why the pricing is subsequently called decisive. Anyone who assumes that growth runs without the rivals' eyes, scrapes this sentence of the teaching text.

The statement is true.

Imitation is likely, not unlikely, and it is likely that there are imitators on the market now. The assertion of the opposite turns the word "probably" over. Imitation explains why the price at this stage must secure or expand the market position. A market without imitators would be the exception, not the rule of this phase described by the book.

The statement is false.

Price as a lever of position. After imitators appear, pricing is crucial to expand market position. It is not just about cost recovery from the introduction, but about competition for the same benefits. Anyone who considers the price in the growth phase to be secondary because sales are increasing anyway, overlooks precisely this choice. Later, in maturity, additional discounts and promotions are added as expense.

The statement is true.

Maximum and decreasing profits are part of maturity. The growth phase is followed by the maturity phase, in which turnover reaches its maximum and profits fall again. Those who prefer both to the growth phase merge two stages. In growth, sales and profits are still growing together. The confusion is typical because both phases are successful; the book curve still divides them sharply.

The statement is false.

title: Maturity and saturation stages
context: Evaluate the following statements on maturation and saturation phase:
statements: In the maturity phase, turnover reaches its maximum.
The profits continue to rise in the maturing phase, because hardly any effort is needed for advertising.
The profits are falling in the maturing phase because of increasing competition, more effort is being put into advertising, discounts and promotions.
In the saturation phase, both sales and profits fall and the market is beginning to shrink.
At the beginning of the saturation phase, it must be clear how to continue to handle the product.
tactical_explanations:
Sales peak, not profit peak. In the maturity phase, sales reach their maximum. This is the key figure of this stage, not automatically the profit. Anyone who equates maximum with further rising profits overlooks the next set of the book. The top of the sales coincides with increasing advertising and promotional effort, which already presses the profit.

The statement is true.

Advertising becomes more expensive, not superfluous. Because of increasing competition, there is an increasing amount of effort for advertising and other sales promotion measures, discounts and promotions. Therefore, the profits are already falling in maturity, although the turnover has its maximum. The claim that hardly any advertising is needed and the profits are continuing to rise, the cost logic turns back. Maturity is not a spare space, but an expensive defense struggle for the same market. Anyone who attributes the declining profits to saturation overlooks the fact that the text of the teaching starts the decline here even before the market begins to shrink.

The statement is false.

Competition drives the effort. More and more advertising, discounts and promotions are the reason why the profits are already falling again in maturity. Sales promotion is a means against rivals, not just decoration. The sentence gives the mechanism and direction right. Anyone who puts the decline in profits into degeneration first overlooks the fact that he already starts to mature, before the market shrinks.

The statement is true.

Both sizes fall, the market shrinks. In the saturation phase, sales and profits fall, the market begins to shrink. This is sharper than the maturity in which sales were still at their peak. Shrinking means that even the cake becomes smaller, not just its own slice. That is why the further strategy must be established at the beginning of this phase before high costs of degeneration threaten.

The statement is true.

Early decision, not in degeneration. At the beginning of the saturation phase it must be clear how to continue to deal with the product before it enters the degeneration phase. Waiting until the pure cost phase is too late. Elimination or relaunch are mentioned in the next paragraph exactly as this preliminary decision. The sentence records the time-memories of the teaching text.

The statement is true.

title: Decline, elimination and relaunch
context: Evaluate the following statements at the end of the product life cycle:
statements: In the degeneration phase, the product only causes high costs.
Whether you remove the product from the offer or try to relaunch it with a product change, it must be clear before the degeneration phase.
Product elimination means taking a product that is no longer successful from the market.
A relaunch attempts to restart with a product change.
A company may only think about elimination or relaunch in the degeneration phase, because there are no costs before.
tactical_explanations:
Only costs, hardly any more earnings. In the degeneration phase, the product only causes high costs. Sales and profits have already fallen in saturation; now the burden remains. Therefore, the decision on the further handling should not fall here. Anyone who reads the degeneration as a quiet residual phase without cost pressure contradicts the wording. The phase is the end point you want to avoid or control, not the moment of first reflection.

The statement is true.

Before we do, we need to clarify, not after. It has to be clear whether the product is being withdrawn from the offer or a product change is trying to restart, a relaunch. "Before that, it refers to the time before degeneration, following the beginning of saturation, in which sales and profits are already falling and the market is beginning to shrink. Those who make the choice only when costs are still running, act against the time limit of the book. Elimination and relaunch are the two mentioned ways, not a third unnamed middle way as a duty. The product policy measures should control the cycle, not comment after the collapse.

The statement is true.

Take off the market if success is lacking. Product elimination is the measure in which a product that is no longer successful is taken off the market. It stands alongside innovation and variation in the list of product policy measures. The aim is not to artificially prolong the life cycle in the cost zone. The sentence repeats the book definition and does not invent any additional condition such as a legal obligation to delete.

The statement is true.

Change as second start. Instead of eviction, a product change can be tried to restart; the theory adds relaunch in brackets. This is not the same variation where only the new version is running, but it is related: one changes to stretch the cycle. Overall, the product policy measures serve to optimize the life cycle and extend its success. Relaunch is exactly this attempt at the late edge.

The statement is true.

Costs arise far earlier. Development and advertising costs are already burdening the introduction; advertising and promotion costs are increasing in maturity; sales and profit are falling in saturation. Degeneration is the end point with only high costs, not the first cost point. The claim that one should only think about elimination or relaunch, because there are no costs before, is wrong in both halves. The theory demands clarification before.

The statement is false.

title: Product differentiation and product diversification
context: Woom GmbH is adding to its offer. Evaluate the following statements on product policy innovations:
statements: If Woom GmbH offers further wheel models in addition to existing wheels, it will deepen its range of wheels and operate product differentiation.
If it offers not only wheels but also sports equipment and fitness equipment, it widens the range; that would be product diversification.
Further wheel models besides the existing wheels are product diversification in the text, because each model opens up a completely new business field.
Product innovation can complement existing products and make the range deeper or wider.
Product differentiation and product diversification are in theory the same word, because both only deepen the assortment.
tactical_explanations:
Further models of wheels in addition to existing wheels deepen the range of wheels; this is called product differentiation. The bicycle field remains, only the variants become more. which serves as an example, not as a mandatory mark of the test. Whoever already calls this deepening diversification confuses depth with width. Diversification would only be the inclusion of completely different product groups next to the wheels, such as sports equipment and fitness equipment. Innovation is the generic term, the direction decides the name.

The statement is true.

The range would widen into new product groups. Sports equipment, clothing, rain protection and fitness equipment next to wheels would widen; that would be product diversification. New product fields are joining the core business. The direction is width, not yet a wheel model. The sentence follows the second woom example word-based and maintains the distinction to differentiate.

The statement is true.

Additional wheel models are differentiation, not diversification. Diversification would be the expansion of sports equipment, for example. The claim that each model is a new business field and therefore diversification, tilts the book pairing deeper versus wider. Another children's bike remains in the range of bikes, even if it looks different.

The statement is false.

Innovation complements and shapes the product range. Various forms of product innovation complement the existing products and make the product range deeper, product differentiation, or wider, product diversification. Innovation is the generic term here, the two forms describe the direction. If you think of innovation as a complete replacement of the old program, you will not be able to use the logic of the addition. Variation changes an existing product and takes the old version from the market; elimination takes an unsuccessful product completely. Both stand next to the innovation, but do not replace it as a product range deepening or widening.

The statement is true.

Deeper and wider are two directions. Differentiation deepened, diversification widened. They are not the same word and they do not deepen both. The equation strikes the exact distinction that the woom example should bear. Without them, it would no longer be possible to say whether new models or completely new product groups are meant.

The statement is false.

title: Product variation and market entry
context: Evaluate the following statements on product variation and entry into the market:
statements: The product variation changes an existing product.
The product variation only offers the modified new version, the previous version no longer.
Product variation means to keep the old and new versions in parallel in the range.
Going first into the market can mean higher entrepreneurial risks, such as market opening costs for development and communication.
A company can also see how the market is developing and then follow up with a similar product.
tactical_explanations:
Change in the existing product. Product variation means that an existing product is changed. It is not about an additional model next to the old one in the sense of differentiation, but about the change of what was already there. The measure is on the list next to innovation and elimination. If you confuse variation with the mere inclusion of another, unchanged article, this point is missing. The decisive factor is the following sentence: Only the new version remains, the previous version is no longer offered. This is exactly what separates variation from a deeper range supplement, where old models may continue.

The statement is true.

Only the new version remains. Expressly: Only the modified new version is offered, the previous version no longer. The old offer disappears with the variation. This is exactly what distinguishes it from a differentiation in which other models complement the existing one. The sentence is the book rule, no interpretation.

The statement is true.

Parallel operation is not the variation of the text. Because the previous version is no longer offered, old and new cannot stand together permanently. Whoever claims parallelism describes a range deepening rather than variation. The confusion is close because both "new" looks; the criterion is whether the old version disappears.

The statement is false.

The first is cost. Even when entering the market, it is important to consider whether one can dare to enter the market first with higher entrepreneurial risk. In brackets, market opening costs, such as development and communication costs, are mentioned. Pioneering role is therefore not merely a prestige, but a question of cost and risk. The sentence holds this page of the alternative without inventing numbers.

The statement is true.

The second option remains to be followed. One can rather wait as the market develops and then follow with a similar product. This is the counter-strategy to the early entry with market opening costs. Both ways serve to optimize the life cycle as best possible. Whoever thinks that the pioneer is only admissible, scrapes the alternative mentioned by the book.

The statement is true.

title: Price setting and demand
context: Evaluate the following statements on pricing policy:
statements: If many products compete with roughly the same benefits, pricing policy plays a crucial role.
Price policy is based on high-price policy and low-price policy or discount policy.
The cost of the product, the price of comparable competing products and the willingness to pay are important for the price.
Demanding a higher price than the customers can or want to pay is basically sensible because high prices always increase demand.
In addition to the price, the payment terms are important.
tactical_explanations:
The price is also of equal benefit. If many products and services compete, whose benefits are similar for customers, price policy plays a decisive role. Cheap prices are then relevant for food, everyday clothing, air travel or mobile phone tariffs. If the USP is established, however, many also pay higher prices. The rate is the first case where the price is the decisive factor.

The statement is true.

Two poles, in between the practice. Price policy is located between high-price policy and low-price policy or discount price policy. The theory spans precisely this range, without defining intermediate forms as own mandatory strategy. Payment conditions are added. Anyone who thinks only one of the poles as the only allowed policy narrows the range. The sentence correctly reproduces the settlement.

The statement is true.

Three factors, not one. In practice, there are three factors: How much are the costs, can they be covered with the price at least? What is the price for a comparable competitive product? How much are the customers willing to pay? Cost, rivals and willingness to pay together control the fixing. If you only let the cost plus logic apply and the other two are scraping, you can undercut the list of the section.

The statement is true.

It makes little sense to be above the willingness to pay. To demand a higher price than the customers can or want to pay is not useful. Basically, with high prices, demand is usually low and high at low prices. The claim that too high a price is reasonable because high prices always increase demand is distorted by both rates. The three factors cost, competitive price and willingness to pay set a limit to the amount. Snob, runner and quality effects are later exceptions where expensive is bought; they make overpriced beyond skill and want no general rule of success.

The statement is false.

Conditions in addition to the amount. In addition, the payment conditions are important. Price policy is therefore not only the amount, but also how and under which conditions is paid. This is directly after the range between high and low price. Anyone who excludes conditions from the price policy leaves a explicitly mentioned building block away.

The statement is true.

title: Seller's market and buyer's market
context: Evaluate the following statements on seller market and buyer market:
statements: If demand exceeds supply, it is called a sales market.
On a seller market, the sellers have easier to influence the price than the buyer side.
In the long run, a seller market often leads to several companies producing the desired goods, the offer increases and prices fall again.
If supply exceeds demand, a buyer market is created in which buyers have more bargaining power.
In a buyer market prices are rising permanently because the buyer side has no bargaining power.
tactical_explanations:
Demand over supply. If demand exceeds supply, it is called a seller market. The definition depends on the quantity ratio, not on the industry name. Here prices are rather high or tend to rise. Whoever uses the same name for the case in which supply exceeds demand, exchanges seller and buyer market.

The statement is true.

The power lies with those who offer scarcely. On the seller market, the sellers have it easier than the buyers to influence the price. As the buyer, there is comparatively little bargaining power and creative scope. The price advantage of the supplier side follows from the scarcity relative to the demand. The sentence represents exactly this asymmetry.

The statement is true.

Offer is catching up, prices are falling. In the long term, a seller market often leads to several companies producing the desired goods, thus increasing the offer and falling prices again. High prices and slight sales attract additional production. The market therefore does not remain permanently on the seller side. If supply subsequently exceeds demand, the buyer market will emerge with more power on the demand side. Anyone who thinks of the situation as an eternal high price without the reaction of the suppliers ignores exactly this long-term movement, which the theory joins to the seller market.

The statement is true.

Supply over demand is overturning power. If supply then exceeds demand, a buyer market is created. There, buyers can influence prices and have more bargaining power. The definition is the mirror image of the seller market. In the long term, prices will fall until some suppliers stop selling at this price and the offer decreases.

The statement is true.

In the buyer market, the buyer side has more bargaining power, not no power. Prices fall in the long term until suppliers leave; after that the offer can decline and prices rise again. Constantly rising prices for faint buyers rather describe a seller market. The statement mixes both market forms and is wrong.

The statement is false.

title: Snob, bandwagon and quality effects
context: Evaluate the following statements on price changes and not entirely rational reactions:
statements: In principle, high prices usually have low demand and low prices.
The reactions of the customers to price changes are always completely rational in the text of the teaching.
The snob effect is expensive to buy to show that you can afford it.
The follower effect is expensively bought because others do it too.
In terms of quality, it is assumed that expensive products are better than cheaper ones, and therefore buys the more expensive ones.
tactical_explanations:
Normal price-quantity direction. In principle, high prices usually have low demand and low prices are high. Usually high demand means that prices can be slightly increased; lower demand, often lower prices. That is the starting rule before exceptions. Those who deny it can no longer see snob and quality effects as deviation.

The statement is true.

Not always rational. The customer's reactions to price changes are not always rational. Consideration should be given to snob effect, follower effect and quality effect. The word "always" in the statement makes a rule an absolute that explicitly relativizes the theory. The three effects are precisely the deviations mentioned above, in which expensive purchases are made, although the normal curve at high prices would be expected to be rather low demand. Snob shows laxity, running follows others, quality suspects better in the expensive good. None of these three motives cancels the basic rule, they limit only the claim of complete rationality.

The statement is false.

Show that you can afford it. In the snob effect, it is expensive to buy to show that you can afford it. The motive is validity, not the most advantageous benefit per euro. A high price can even support the demand of this group, against the normal rule. The sentence meets the book definition and does not mix it with running behind other buyers.

The statement is true.

Others do. The runner effect is expensive to buy because others do. Connection to the group, not the individual prestige signal of the snob, is the motive. Both effects can bear the same high price, but for different reasons. Those who equate with the assumption of better quality, apply to the third effect, which the theory lists separately.

The statement is true.

The quality effect is assumed to be more expensive than cheaper, so you buy the more expensive one. The price figure becomes a quality indicator, regardless of whether the costs justify it. This is not the third rational reaction to the price, in addition to snob and running along. The sentence correctly reflects the assumption and the order of purchase.

The statement is true.

title: Direct and indirect distribution
context: Evaluate the following statements on distribution policy:
statements: Distribution policy tries to clarify how the sales route is to be designed and which transport route is chosen.
Direct sales are sold directly by the manufacturing company to the final consumer.
In indirect sales, one or more commercial establishments are intermediated on the way between producer and final purchaser.
Wholesalers sell to the final consumer, retailers sell to other retailers.
If you order directly from the producer, who fulfils from the headquarters or own branch, it is a direct sales route.
tactical_explanations:
Two questions, one policy field. Distribution policy tries to answer two essential questions: how the product comes to the customer, which means how the sales route is to be designed, and which route to choose. Place is thus the organization of the way, not just a sign at the warehouse. Those who think of the truck without the question of intermediaries leave the way of sales. Directly to the end user or indirectly via wholesale and retail, to this franchising: these are answers to the first question. Both questions are at the beginning of the section and bear the rest of the distribution policy.

The statement is true.

No trade in between. In direct sales, the manufacturing company sells directly to the end consumer. No wholesaler or retailer stands in between. The subsequent order from the manufacturer from headquarters or branch is exactly this case. Anyone who regards every branch as an indirect salesman even though it belongs to the producer blurs the line that draws the theory.

The statement is true.

In the case of indirect sales, one or more commercial establishments are inter-mediated between producers and end-users, including wholesalers who sell to other retailers and retailers who sell to the final consumer. One link is sufficient; several are possible. The sentence holds the definition without prejudgeting franchising.

The statement is true.

Wholesalers sell to other retailers, retailers to the last consumer. The statement turns both assignments around. This would be the last step towards the household in wholesale, which contradicts the teaching text. Indirect sales use this sequence of steps, not the reverse.

The statement is false.

The central or branch office remains direct. If you order directly from the producer who fulfills the order from his head office or from his own branch, it is a direct sales route. The own branch is not an independent commercial enterprise in between. Those who equate them to a foreign retailer make direct sales indirect. Both places of performance are explicitly named as direct.

The statement is true.

title: Franchising as a distribution channel
context: Evaluate the following statements on franchising:
statements: In franchising, the franchisee provides the franchisee with brand names, products and marketing know-how against payment of a franchise fee.
The franchise fee usually consists of a fixed amount plus a share in sales.
The franchisee is economically and legally independent.
The franchisee is bound to the agreed level of the franchiser's marketing concept and business model.
The franchisee loses all legal independence and becomes the dependent branch of the franchisee.
tactical_explanations:
The name, goods and know-how for a fee. Franchising is a special sales route: The franchisor provides another company, the franchisee, with its brand name, its products and all its marketing know-how, such as business design, advertising and internet presence, against payment of a franchise fee. It is not a mere supply contract without concept. The fee is usually fixed amount plus participation in turnover; the contractor remains economically and legally independent, bound only to the agreed extent. The sentence bundles performance and consideration, as the text of the teaching lists, without removing independence already.

The statement is true.

Fix plus turnover. The fee is usually a fixed amount plus a share of turnover. Both together, not just a one-time flat rate without a current share, describes the theory as a common pattern. Concrete euro amounts do not call it; the structure is enough. Those who cancel the share of turnover undercut "mostly fixed amount plus share of turnover".

The statement is true.

The franchisee is economically and legally independent. He remains another company, not an independent part of the company. This is exactly what makes Franchising a special sales route between the parties, not a mere branch establishment. The next link to the concept does not change the independence in its opposite.

The statement is true.

Despite the independence of the franchisee, the franchisee is bound to the franchiser's marketing concept and business model to the agreed extent. Uniform appearance is the sense of the know-how transfer. The bond is contractually limited, not limitless and not zero. Anyone who reads every requirement as a loss of legal personality goes beyond the representation; anyone who denies any bond makes franchise a free resale without a concept.

The statement is true.

Branches would not be independent. Legally independent and at the same time bound to the concept: this is the combination of the book. Unindependent branch would delete legal independence. The statement claims exactly this loss and is wrong. Franchise remains a contract between two companies, not the conversion of the owner into a permanent establishment without its own legal entity.

The statement is false.

title: Advertising media and advertising vehicles
context: Evaluate the following statements on classic advertising in communication policy:
statements: Communication policy is primarily concerned with advertising.
Advertising or ads are advertising media; daily and weekly magazines can be advertising media.
TV spots and radio spots use television and radio as advertising media.
Advertising media and advertising media indicate in the text the same subject with two names.
Posters and billboards can be distributed via billboards, port columns or public transport facilities.
tactical_explanations:
Advertising first, not alone. Communication policy primarily includes advertising, as is known in the classic form of the table: advertisements in magazines, radio and television spots, posters on walls and columns, letters and brochures on distributors. "First and foremost, priority in the presentation does not mean that sales promotion, personnel selling and PR are missing. The sentence hits this entry. Whoever derives from it that communication is merely advertising, goes further than the wording; here only the priority that is in theory, before website, actions and public follow.

The statement is true.

Medium versus carrier. Tab. 7 puts advertising media and advertising media side by side. Advertising (inserate) is the medium; daily and weekly magazines, magazines, and event programs as carriers. The medium is the designed message, the carrier the medium that transports it. The sentence holds exactly this pair. If you drop the ad and magazine into one, you will not need the table.

The statement is true.

Spot is medium, station is medium. TV and radio spots use television and radio as advertising medium. The same two-part is valid for display and magazine. A spot without a transmitter would be means without a carrier. The statement correctly assigns both sides to the communication chain. The same two-part is analogous to the advertisement and magazine.

The statement is true.

Two columns, two reels. The table separates advertising media and advertising media. Any synonyms would be they only if the advertisement and the magazine were the same. They are not: the one is designed, the other is wearing it. The statement claims identity and is wrong. Whoever gives up the separation can no longer distinguish between the poster and the billboard.

The statement is false.

The poster is a poster's surface. Posters and billboards are media; billboards, billboards, public transport facilities and sports courts call the table a carrier. The sentence mentions three of the carriers correctly. It remains within the classical advertising and does not already prejudge blogs or social media, which later get their own sentences.

The statement is true.

title: Sales promotion, personal selling and public relations
context: Evaluate the following statements on other communication policy instruments:
statements: Communication policy includes the entire company's presence on the Internet with its own website and on social networks.
Promotion of sales through certain actions is part of the communication policy.
The behaviour of the salesmen, in theory called Personal Selling, is part of the communication policy.
Public relations often refers to the whole company, such as press conferences, press releases, targeted information from investors and sponsorship.
Communication policy concerns only the individual product and never the enterprise as a whole.
tactical_explanations:
The company's entire presence on the Internet with its own website and social networks is part of the communication policy. Besides various forms of advertising, it is not only a technical attachment to distribution, even if the sales route can run in parallel on the network. If you take out websites and networks from promotion, you will be able to score the first of the four points after classic advertising. Social media marketing will deepen the same idea later as advertising and PR on platforms like Facebook and X. Here, the assignment of the appearance to communication counts.

The statement is true.

Promotion through certain actions is explicitly on the list. In the mature phase, discounts and promotions were already mentioned as costly measures against competition; here they belong to the communication policy. The sentence remains with "certain actions" and invents no obligation to book any price reduction as a promotion. He holds the assignment to the Mix instrument promotion.

The statement is true.

People at the point of sale. The behavior of the salesmen is assigned as personal selling to the communication policy. The message runs not only via advertisement and spot, but via the conversation. Who thinks personal selling only as personnel management without customer reference, takes the English expression out of the marketing mix. It is considered a standard in brackets exactly behind the behaviour on the sale.

The statement is true.

PR often targets the organization. Communication policy also refers not only to the products, but often to the whole company, for example in the field of public relations. PR includes press conferences, press releases, targeted information of certain target groups, for example investors as investor relations, as well as sponsorship. The sentence summarizes this range. He does not make PR any product display under other names.

The statement is true.

Product and company. PR in particular shows that communication often affects the whole company, not only the individual product. The absolute limitation "exclusively" and "never contradicts this sentence. Advertising can put the product in the foreground; PR, investor relations and sponsorship widen the view. The statement is therefore too narrow and wrong.

The statement is false.

title: Social media marketing and event marketing
context: Evaluate the following statements on social media marketing and event marketing:
statements: Social media marketing usually refers to advertising and PR of a company on social media such as Facebook and X.
Public relations through social media are called social media relations.
Through social media, companies can quickly and directly contact many potential customers, introduce products and communicate messages.
Event Marketing includes event-oriented events that are intended to trigger a strong customer activation process.
Event Marketing is limited in the teaching text exclusively to internal employee training without any external effect on customers.
tactical_explanations:
SMM is an advertising and PR in networks. Social media marketing is a marketing activity, usually advertising and PR, a company on social media such as Facebook and X, formerly Twitter. So it's not a fifth P in addition to the four instruments, but communication on these platforms. The number of users has increased many times; the importance has increased enormously. Public relations there is called social media relations. The sentence remains with the rule "Advertising and PR" and does not invent any mandatory figures. Contact, product presentation and mood follow as effect in the next paragraph, not as own definition.

The statement is true.

Relations as a name of public relations. Public relations through social media is called social media relations. This parallels PR with a channel-related expression. Whoever equates relations with pure banner switching without public relations, narrows the name set by the book. The sentence represents the term that the text of the teaching explicitly introduces.

The statement is true.

Direct, fast, many addressees. Companies can contact a wide range of potential customers quickly and directly via social media, introduce products, communicate messages and make positive moods for themselves and their products. That's why SMM has gained in importance. If you think of social media as a one-sided billboard without a contact possibility, "directly contact" leaves away.

The statement is true.

Event marketing includes event-oriented events that are intended to trigger a strong customer activation process. They should focus on a company, product group or event: fashion shows, fairs, exhibition and business openings, cultural and sporting events. The sentence meets the definition before the example series. Activation is the goal, not a silent information without experience.

The statement is true.

The events mentioned above focus on companies, product groups or events and should activate customers. Internal employee training without any external impact is not included in this list. The restriction "only internally" marks fashion show, trade fair and sports event. Event Marketing is an external communication tool, complementing advertising and SMM.

The statement is false.

title: Absolute and relative market share (15/100/30)
context: An Austrian bicycle manufacturer A achieves sales of EUR 15 million in a value-added market of EUR 100 million; the largest competitor implements EUR 30 million. Evaluate the following statements regarding absolute and relative market share:
statements: The absolute market share of Company A is 15 percent, because its sales represent 15 percent of the market volume of 100 million euros.
The relative market share of Company A is 0.5 because its turnover is half as high as that of the largest competitor.
Because A's relative market share is smaller than one, A can still be the market leader.
The relative market share is created by dividing A's turnover by the total market volume.
If A's turnover were as high as that of its largest competitor, the relative market share would be exactly one.
tactical_explanations:
Fifteen out of a hundred are 15 percent. The absolute market share sets its own turnover in relation to the market volume: 15 million euros of 100 million euros. The turnover of the largest competitor does not belong in this denominator; it controls the relative market share first. The statement takes the absolute measure. Rivalen sales belong only to the relative market share formula.

The statement is true.

Half as much as the rival is 0.5. The relative market share is 15 million euros related to the turnover of the strongest competitor of 30 million euros. The ratio describes a ranking, not a share of the overall market. One means: smaller than the strongest one so far. The statement correctly calculates. One means: smaller than the strongest competitor so far.

The statement is true.

A relative market share below one means that one's own turnover is smaller than that of the strongest rival - that just excludes market leadership in this figure. The market leader would only be a company with a relative market share above one, i.e. a turnover higher than that of the largest competitor to date.

The statement is false.

The total market volume belongs in the absolute, not the relative formula. Relatively, the sales of the largest competitor are divided. If you instead set the market volume in the denominator, you confuse both key figures and lose the comparison with the strongest rival.

The statement is false.

The ratio is exactly one. Only above this does market leadership begin in the sense of this ratio. Under one, one remains behind the rival. The threshold one marks the equivalency. Only a quotient via one signals market leadership.

The statement is true.

title: Distinguishing market potential and market volume
context: A manufacturer of everyday bikes knows its market potential with 80 000 pieces, the actual market volume with 48 000 pieces and its own sales with 6 000 pieces.
statements: The market potential of 80 000 pieces describes the maximum possible sales volume, not the actual sales.
The market volume of 48 000 units is already the maximum possible sales that the market allows.
Because the market volume is well below market potential, this market is almost saturated.
The sales volume of Company A of 6 000 units corresponds to the total market volume.
Between market potential and market volume, 32 000 pieces of unused space for additional sales remains.
tactical_explanations:
Eighty thousand are the intended upper limit. Market potential describes how large the market would be if everyone bought with a need to be met; it is not an actual size. With 80,000 pieces it is above the market volume of 48 000. Anyone who reads potential as already sold confuses maximum and is. This results directly from the mentioned sizes.

The statement is true.

The market volume is the quantity actually sold; the upper limit is market potential and is 80 000 pieces. Whoever exchanges both is mistaken for actual and maximum size. The statement makes the volume falsely the absolute ceiling. The upper limit is market potential and here is 80 000 pieces.

The statement is false.

Sixty percent of the upper limit is not nearly saturated. 48 000 out of 80 000 leave 32 000 pieces gap. The market would be almost saturated only when the volume moved close to the potential. Here, there is ample unused scope. The statement overestimates the saturation massively. With 32 000 pieces gap, the market remains clearly unsaturated.

The statement is false.

Six thousand are part, not the whole. The sales volume of A is only a fraction of the market volume of 48 000 pieces; other suppliers contribute the rest. A single company cannot be the total market volume as long as competitors are effective in sales. The statement equals part and sum. Other suppliers contribute the rest of the market volume.

The statement is false.

Difference marks the margin. 80 000 minus 48 000 results in 32 000 pieces between potential and volume. As long as this gap exists, theoretically, even more could be sold. The number is pure subtraction of the two market sizes. The statement is exactly this unused remainder. The 32 000 pieces are pure subtraction of potential and volume.

The statement is true.

title: A nearly saturated market in numbers
context: A regional market for city bikes has a market potential of 50 million euros and a market volume of 48 million euros; Company A implements 8 million euros, the largest competitor 12 million euros. Rate the following statements:
statements: Because the market volume of EUR 48 million is close to the market potential of EUR 50 million, this market is considered to be almost saturated.
In an almost saturated market, sales can hardly be increased on the same, unchanged demand carriers.
The absolute market share of Company A is 16 percent, because it shares its sales through market potential rather than market volume.
The relative market share of Company A is two thirds, because its turnover represents two thirds of the turnover of the largest competitor.
An almost saturated market cannot be transformed into an unsaturated market in any way after the teaching text.
tactical_explanations:
Forty-eight of fifty million are 96 percent. Market volume is close to market potential; if the is so close to the theoretical upper limit, the market is considered almost saturated. Additional sales to the same demand carriers become tight. The figures show saturation, not a wide gap. The statement makes this relation.

The statement is true.

Almost all available demand carriers are already buying. The remaining gap of 50 minus 48 equals 2 million euros leaves hardly any room for additional sales at the unchanged buyer group. Growth then requires new products or new target groups. Increases are hardly possible on the same unchanged demand carriers. The statement describes precisely this narrowness.

The statement is true.

Absolute market share requires the market volume as denominator. The own turnover of 8 million euros is to be related to 48 million euros, not to the potential of 50 million euros. Those who share through the potential choose the wrong, too large reference size and receive 16 percent instead of about 16.7 percent on volume basis. The statement explicitly mentions the wrong denominator.

The statement is false.

Eight to twelve are two thirds. The relative market share compares its own turnover with that of the largest competitor: 8 divided by 12 results in about 0.67. One does not mean market leadership, but the calculation is correct. The ratio measures rank, not share of the total market. The statement is made by the quotient. The ratio measures ranking, not the share of the total market.

The statement is true.

Saturation is not a final state. Changes in products or new layers of buyers can expand the circle of demand carriers, so that there is scope for volume and potential again. An almost saturated market can be reopened. The assertion of an unchanging state contradicts these opening strategies.

The statement is false.

title: Computing sales shares of several providers
context: A value-based bicycle market of 100 million euros is distributed among companies A with 40 million euros, the largest competitor B with 25 million euros and provider C with 20 million euros (remain: other suppliers). Evaluate the following statements about the sales shares:
statements: If A converts EUR 40 million in a 100 million euro market, its absolute market share is 40 percent.
The largest competitor of A is automatically the one with the highest turnover among all other suppliers.
If A's turnover is higher than that of its largest competitor, A's relative market share is above one and A is considered the market leader.
The relative market share of A is obtained by dividing its turnover by the total market volume.
A less-than-A provider can still have a higher relative market share than A if it is closer to the largest competitor's turnover.
tactical_explanations:
Forty of a hundred are 40 percent. The absolute market share sets its own turnover in relation to the market volume. Sales of the other suppliers do not change this own share; they only explain the remaining 60 percent. B and C do not belong in the denominator of this ratio. The statement calculates the own share correctly.

The statement is true.

The largest competitor is the highest turnover among the rest. Not A itself, but the strongest of the other suppliers is the denominator of the relative market share formula. This definition controls who is compared. If the strongest rival changes, the denominator changes. The statement makes exactly this selection rule. If the strongest rival changes, this denominator also changes.

The statement is true.

Over one, market leaders are called in a relative sense. If your own turnover exceeds that of the strongest rival, the ratio is greater than one. That is exactly what marks market leaders in this ratio. Below one, you stay behind the rival. The statement links quotient and leadership correctly. Under one, you stay behind the strongest competitor.

The statement is true.

The market volume belongs to the absolute market share formula. Relatively, the sales of the largest competitor are divided by the turnover of the company, not by the total market volume. The confusion erases the direct comparison with the strongest rival and makes the threshold meaningless.

The statement is false.

The relative market share measures the ratio of two sales to the turnover of the largest competitor, not the proximity of two figures to each other. A lower-in-house provider cannot achieve higher quotas than a higher-in-sales provider, provided that both use the same rival as a reference; the ratio grows with the counter, not with the optical proximity of the numbers.

The statement is false.

title: Sales potential and sales volume of a single firm
context: A producer of children's bikes (Company A) knows the market potential with 20 000 pieces, the market volume with 12 000 pieces, its own sales potential with 4 000 pieces, its sales volume with 2 400 pieces and the sales of the largest competitor with 3 000 pieces.
statements: The sales potential of an enterprise is not the amount it can achieve or hopes to achieve in the best case, the sales already realized.
Sales potential and sales volume of an entity are different key figures; the potential may be higher than the actual volume.
The sales potential of a single company is conceptually the same as the market potential of the entire market.
The absolute market share of a company in terms of volume is its volume of sales in relation to market volume, not in relation to its own sales potential.
However, a company whose sales volume is below the sales volume of the largest competitor can achieve a relative market share above one.
tactical_explanations:
Sales potential is best, not is. It describes the amount that the company can achieve or hopes to achieve in the best case. Typically, it is above actual sales because untapped opportunities still exist. Whoever equates potential and volume, removes the scope for growth. The statement clearly separates both.

The statement is true.

Two key figures, often separated. Sales potential is the desired best case, sales volume of the realized sales. As long as opportunities are open, the potential is above the actual volume. Both sizes belong to the company, but measure the goal and is separate. The statement captures exactly this difference. Target size and actual sales consciously measure different things.

The statement is true.

The market potential refers to the entire market and all the providers of demand, the sales potential only to a single company and its own best-case quantity. A single company cannot claim the entire range of requirements for itself, which is why its sales potential usually remains significantly smaller than the market potential.

The statement is false.

Absolute volume share requires market volume. The own actual sales are related to the sales of all suppliers, not to the own sales potential. The potential is an internal target and does not belong in this denominator. Whoever takes potential instead of volume distorts the market share. The statement calls the right reference.

The statement is true.

The relative market share compares its own sales directly with that of its largest competitor. If its own sales are lower than one, the ratio is smaller than one; a value above one presupposes its own sales above that of the rival. A lower sales volume cannot exceed this threshold.

The statement is false.

title: Market leadership: absolute and relative share together
context: In a value-based market for e-bikes of 90 million euros, Company A implements 45 million euros, the largest competitor 30 million euros and the other suppliers together 15 million euros. Evaluate the following statements about market leadership and market share:
statements: An absolute market share of 50 percent automatically means that the company is also relatively market leader.
A relative market share greater than one indicates that own sales are higher than that of the strongest competitor to date.
Market leadership can only be seen in the absolute market share, and the relative market share does not provide additional information.
If the turnover of the largest competitor is higher than the turnover of its own, the relative market share is automatically above one.
The market share of an undertaking may be determined exclusively in euro in value, never in quantity.
tactical_explanations:
Absolute and relative market share are two different key figures. A company with a 40 percent absolute share can still be the market leader if the strongest rival holds only 25 percent (40/25 > 1); vice versa, an absolute share of 50 percent alone does not say what the largest competitor's turnover is. Only the comparison of both transactions decides on the relative leadership.

The statement is false.

About one means: own turnover higher than that of the strongest rival. This is the central condition of the relative market leadership. The ratio of own turnover and competitor turnover is then above one. Under one one one remains behind the rival. The statement meets exactly this definition. Under one the company remains behind the rival.

The statement is true.

The relative market share is precisely the information that the absolute share does not show: the direct comparison with the strongest rival. A high absolute share may coincide with a relative share below one if the market has very few but unequally large suppliers overall.

The statement is false.

Higher rival sales pushes the ratio below one. If the turnover of the largest competitor is higher than its own, the relative market share is below one, not above one. A value above one presupposes the opposite. The statement claims the wrong sign of the relation. Above one, it requires a higher own turnover.

The statement is false.

Market share may use quantity or value. Both types of calculations are permissible and can lead to different percentages at different average prices. "Exclusively in terms of value", the quantitative variant wrongly deletes. Piece and Euro are parallel measuring paths. The statement is therefore wrong. Piece and Euro remain parallel, equal measuring paths.

The statement is false.

title: Quantity share and value share can diverge
context: The same bicycle market comprises 200 pieces or 1,000 million euros. Company A sells 40 pieces for 280 million euros, the largest competitor 50 pieces for 200 million euros. Rate the following statements on the volume and value share:
statements: If a company sells more expensive products than the market average, its market share in value may be higher than its market share in quantity.
The absolute market share in terms of volume and value must always be the same for different average prices of suppliers.
A company that sells less pieces than its largest competitor can still be a market leader in value if it achieves significantly higher prices.
The relative market share may vary depending on whether the quantity or value is calculated, and may even be on different sides of the threshold one.
The market share of a company in value depends solely on the number of units sold, not on the price obtained.
tactical_explanations:
Expensive units raise the value share. If a company sells comparatively few but expensive pieces, its share of total turnover may be higher than its share of the total number of pieces. Higher average prices explain the gap. Quantity and value must then be read separately. The statement describes exactly this effect.

The statement is true.

Different average prices of suppliers typically cause quantity and value to diverge, not coincide. Only if all suppliers had the same average price would both types of calculation be equal to the percentage. In the case of different prices, equality is the exception, not the rule.

The statement is false.

Fewer units, more sales are possible. If, despite a smaller number of units, turnover is higher than that of the largest competitor, the relative market share in value is above one, while the quantity can remain below one. Higher prices are equal to the residual share. This is the statement of this decoupling. Higher prices can more than compensate for the residual share in turnover.

The statement is true.

The same supplier can be in quantity below one and above one in value, or vice versa. Both types of calculations are independent and do not necessarily provide the same result. Prices of the suppliers drive the deviation. The statement holds this possible gap.

The statement is true.

The value share is derived from turnover, i.e. from quantity multiplied by price. Two companies with the same number of units, but different prices achieve different sales and thus different value share. Thus, the price is by no means irrelevant.

The statement is false.

title: Saturation, market share and sales potential in the same market
context: The Austrian children's bike market is subject to market potential of EUR 200 million, market volume of EUR 190 million, sales company A EUR 38 million, sales largest competitor EUR 57 million, sales potential company A EUR 50 million.
statements: A market can be almost saturated, even if no provider is a relative market leader.
The absolute market share of a company is always calculated in relation to market potential, not to market volume.
If the turnover of the largest competitor significantly exceeds its own turnover, the relative market share of the company can still be above one.
The sales potential of an sole proprietorship may be higher than its own actual sales volume without exceeding market potential.
An almost saturated market can also be transformed into an unsaturated market through new product variants or new target groups.
tactical_explanations:
Saturation and market leadership are independent. Saturation measures volume to potential; relative market leadership measures own sales to the strongest rival. A market can be almost exhausted without any provider being above one. Both key figures answer different questions. The statement divides them correctly.

The statement is true.

Absolute market share refers to market volume. The denominator is the actual sales of all suppliers, not the theoretical market potential. The potential would be a larger reference and would artificially reduce the share. Whoever shares through the potential chooses the wrong denominator. The statement is therefore wrong.

The statement is false.

Higher rival sales keep the ratio below one. The relative market share is divided by the turnover of the largest competitor. If the rival sales are significantly higher, the value is below one, not above one. A value above one requires higher own sales. The statement claims the impossible. A value above one requires higher own than foreign sales.

The statement is false.

The sales potential of a company is the best target and is typically higher than the actual sales volume achieved, but remains below the market potential that describes the entire market. This ranking - actual sales smaller than own potential, own potential smaller than market potential - is the normal case.

The statement is true.

New variants or target groups open up saturated markets. The circle of demand carriers can be expanded, so that there is scope for volume and potential again. An almost saturated state is thus no end point. The statement describes precisely this reopening. Growth remains conceivable via product and target group.

The statement is true.
